review_text:
Chef Josh Capon of Burger & Barrel keeps on winning this Burger Bash competition thing at the NYC Wine & Food Festival every year with his Bash Burger. Now, he has another incredible burger at this awesome new steakhouse on a quiet side street just off Bowery.

The menu is pretty extensive, with plenty of interesting options beyond just steak. We ordered a ton of stuff, which was all incredible:

- Bacon Rosemary Focaccia (complimentary to start)
Off to an excellent start, these two small pieces of bread accompanied by some charcuterie were delicious. Still warm, with some bacon bits inside the bread, this was really great.

- Oxtail Arancini ($13 for 6)
These tiny, fried, crispy arancini were delicious. Much smaller than typical arancini, these were bite size and addictive. There were 6, but I still wanted a lot more than my half.

- Bitter Greens ($14)
Opting for something non-beige and non-meat for once, we went with this very refreshing and delicious take on a caesar salad. Finely chopped with toasted bread crumbs on top, this was a great option that made me not regret ordering a salad.

- Spaghetti Aglio e Olio ($19)
Heartbroken that they didn't have the Duck Lasagna for some reason, we still wanted some pasta so we tried this, and it was a good consolation prize. It was perfectly al dente with tons of flavor from the lemon ricotta and the crunchy breadcrumbs. This is a great mid-course option.

- Short Rib ($37)
From the meat section, we went for the short rib, which came pre-sliced into perfect little medallions of meat, laid out alongside some tasty shishito peppers. They were a perfect rare, with almost no fat but still packing plenty of flavor.

- Cheeseburger ($22)
This is the definite must. Made with dry-aged beef, this is up there with the best new burgers this year. On par with the amazing one at Cherche Midi just a few blocks away, this is definitely worth the seemingly steep price tag for a burger. Even better, the price includes an amazing bucket of perfectly crispy and golden french fries. The place is considered a steak house, but if you are only going with one meat dish, make sure it's this one.

- Hash Brown Potato ($8)
Because we didn't have enough meat and potatoes, we went with even more, with this perfect little disc of a hash brown. Deliciously greasy and crispy, this is a good complement to your beef if you want something a little different from the fries.

- Donuts & Coffee ($12)
This was a pretty good dessert. You get four cinnamon & sugar donuts accompanied by a cup of mocha pudding topped with coffee cream, a sort of pot de creme. The donuts on their own are a little plain, but go great when paired with the creamy and chocolatey pudding.

- PB&J ($12)
Another pretty good dessert, and better than the donuts, but also not as impressive as the main meal, this consists of peanut butter mousse with a red berry filling and  strawberry cereal crunch on top, alongside a small scoop of sweet cream ice cream. It's super smooth and creamy and not as intensely peanut buttery as a peanut butter addict would hope, but still very delicious.

Not only was all the food excellent, but the atmosphere in here is beautiful too. It's pretty swanky, but with a more casual vibe than your usual steakhouse. Service was great too, with very friendly servers and management. I will be back for that Duck Lasagna and probably another steak. And it will be hard to resist that burger again.

Walked in early tonight and grabbed the last seat at the bar. Bartender was cool and welcoming as was the sommelier. They recommended a house cocktail called the 'Last Monk' (sp?) which was delicious and balanced. Not at all heavy or sweet.

Had the oxtail arancini to begin which was flavorful and crisp without being oily. Afterward, enjoyed a salad with a tangy greek yogurt dressing which was like a yummy alternative to a typical wedge salad.

I was going to skip red meat, but couldn't avoid it when they described their grilled short rib prep which sounded like an exciting alternative to the more common braised short ribs. I didn't want to finish the plate for dietary reasons, but I couldn't help it - too good. Also came with some solid shisito peppers.
 
Too full to try dessert, but will next time when I;m with people. Very impressive showing early on. Will definitely be a busy joint.

It was good, not great. My boyfriend and I went here on Saturday night and ordered the steak tartar, bitter greens, bowery steak and the short rib.

Steak tartar: nice texture, but overall flavor was pretty dull. $18

Bitter greens: we really enjoyed this version of a Caesar salad. $14

Bowery steak: he said it had the texture of a flank steak but enjoyed the flavor. Although not worth the price. $48

Short rib: it wasn't anything special at all. I did not enjoy the "salsa verde" flavor. $37

Service was great and since it was opening weekend they gave us 20% off of the food (not drinks). Overall it was a good meal but probably would not want to go spend over 200 bucks on 3 star food.

Disappointed. Poor service - definitely need more knowledges of the food, ok food - kitchen needs to speed up, ok interiors - no surprise just like those industrial style places. This place definitely needs more time to grow. Not recommended if you like quality meats or try it after a few months.

Let me just say that I had high hopes after the syrupy sweet of a review from Mike C. I would have never brought my client here for dinner if I'd known. I wouldn't say I'm an official foodie but my review of one restaurant was quoted in Eater. I guess that does say something. So, it's when I say NEVER in my 30 years of living and dining in NYC have I ever had an experience like this one. And this is not a preamble to something great. 

The food was good. Was it better than any other "high end" steak joint I've been to? No. Was it mediocre? No. It was above average. Don't get me wrong the steaks were cooked perfectly. One guest of mine raved how perfectly the steak was cooked even along the bone. The duck lasagna was scrumptious. The wine on the wine list was good and steak house pricey. Albeit the sommelier described the one wine we ordered completely wrong.

So what made this a 2 star rating? Let's just say the chef/owner. The poor waiter who was serving us the duck lasagna tableside could do nothing right. And all of us sitting at the table were made painfully aware that he could do nothing right because the chef was breathing over him letting him know he was far from perfect. But, the be all to this fiasco of a 3 digit meal was when the chef came over to the table after we finished dessert and said "I need to have this table back." Rude is an understatement. Here's the thing. If the dude can cook keep him in the kitchen because his people skills will drive customers and repeat customers away. I can say that my clients were thankful for the meal but mentioned "there would be no need to come back."

Do I recommend this place? Nope. For the price and the service I say go to Del Frisco's or Capital Grille because you will pay just as much, get just as good of a steak minus the attitude from an ill mannered chef.

This is an amazing restaurant. I can't believe they've only been open for one week. The duck lasagna was amazing and the staff was kind and knowledgable. I'm excited to go back and try more of their amazing food.

Had a wonderful dinner last night. Sounds like some other reviewers have an axe to grind...

I was very pleasantly surprised about how seamless and smooth the service was, especially for a restaurant that has only been open for 4 days! Everyone was very friendly and not intrusive. I was there for a client dinner and they knew the right time to come. 

Food-wise. Spot-on. A delicious steak restaurant that doesn't serve your usual, bland, buttery sides. This is what we got:

- complimentary foccacia, charcuterie, and oxtail arancini = so good!
- Baked Oysters = amazing. I took more than my share and we should've ordered more.
- live scallops = delicate but just okay.
- crispy polenta = good. The mushrooms on top almost tasted like short rib.
- duck lasagna = WOW. Definitely order this and I usually do not like to eat duck. I know, I'm an alien. It says it's for two but you could definitely order this for 4-6 people to share as an app.
- short rib ravioli = Delicious. The ravioli was seriously cooked to al dente perfection and I loved the crispy sage on top. 
- bitter greens caesar salad = yes, it was almost mainly a salad of cheese...but it was tasty.
- korean short rib = i liked how they sliced it perfectly. it was cooked perfectly.
- lamb chops = I didn't have it but two of my dinner companions did. Both polished them off and loved it with the yogurt sauce.
- sour cream hash browns = SO GOOD. Next time, I'll be ordering my own and not sharing with anyone. 
- cinnamon sugar donuts with a mocha dip = definitely order.
- some chocolate kind of cake with ice- cream = it was just average. 
- wine list was pretty reasonable. We had a few bottles of a great malbec. 

All in all, I would definitely come back. The food was great, drinks were awesome, and the ambience was very lively and buzzy. Great addition to that area.

Long story short, the bad reviews are pretty funny.If you'd rather go out at Capital Grille or Del Frisco's (Maybe they can get one of those sweet "Double Eagle"designations), then you know who you're dealing with. If you're going to a brand-new restaurant and complaining about the speed, you were looking for something to complain about. 

With that out of the way - absolutely amazing meal, once again from Chef Josh Capon - huge fan of B&B, and Lure (both locations). Tried out too many items to list, but the Côte de Boeuf was a hit - i'll be ordering that each time -  so was the house special prime rib, and the burger. On the appetizer front, you have to check out the scallops, the oyster list is on point, and the beef tartare is a must order. 

Oh, and as an FYI if you're into that sort of thing - healthy craft beer selection with some nice California beers (Stone, Sierra Nevada), which go very well with the fare. I'm sure that list will be expanding because it seems you can't hit a new Manhattan restaurant that doesn't have at least 20 different craft brews. Pretty excited to see a few Belgian beers on there and a great midwest sour.

Had the coconut cake that we preordered, absolutely delicious. The pastry chef for this group is a national treasure. 

But, don't put too much weight into this - my reviews are never quoted in Eater. :)

Awesome spot, great atmosphere,  tasty appetizers, extensive wine list. Menu varied in price and the pork ribeye was special. Friendly service coupled with professionalism (like the exchange for clean silverware between courses) definite returning customer and highly recommend.

The food here is pretty good. The foie gras was amazing, but my chicken was too salty. Overall it was disappointing that we had to wait for an hour for our 10 PM reservation to be seated. The hostess kept avoiding our questions for an ETA for the table, insisting that it was almost ready when it was not.

Recommend:
- Broiled Oysters
- Steak Tartare
- Short Rib Ravioli
- Pork Rib Eye
- Duck Lasagna
- PB&J dessert

Our server Joshua was excellent! 

Cocktails are okay.

Decor is kinda meh.


Expensive, but worth it.

Despite being in a new building that robs the east village of its charm, this place is great for dinner out.

Dressed oysters are the best I've had, steak was on point, and that oxtail thing - I wish they gave everyone more!

Just had a wonderful dinner at this warm and stylish place  Food was delicious. Lots of excellent choices. We had the cauliflower appetizer as well as the liver pate. Both were excellent. For dinner we shared the duck ragu lasagne. Delicious!  Don't miss dessert. We had the the peanut butter and jelly mousse and the donuts with mocha pudding. The service, by Joshua, was outstanding.

Had a great meal at Bowery Meat Company last night. Four of us went to celebrate a birthday. We had a 6:45 reservation. The place was pretty empty, so we were seated right away. Vibe was good--very retro feel to the décor, nice lively crowd.
I had The Loneliest Monk cocktail, which was great. Maybe a little too sweet, but very enjoyable (if you like a good whiskey or bourbon cocktail.) They brought out some focaccia and cured salami-type of sausage (very cumin-heavy) for the table, followed by oxtail and bone marrow arancini. All were good and a nice comp, but nothing spectacular. (I've seen tons of people raving about the arancini, but honestly I wasn't super impressed.)
We decided to share the duck lasagna to start and then share a T-bone (special that night) for our main. We also ordered the potato fondant, hash brown, and spinach.
Chef Capon served us the lasagna. He was very friendly and personable. (We saw him interacting with a number of tables.) The lasagna was delicious--very rich. My only complaint is that it wasn't quite hot enough. I don't want to burn myself on it, but I got the feeling it had been sitting around.
The T-bone was also delicious. I think it was aged for 40 days. It was a very thick cut and perfectly cooked (medium-rare) and served with shishito peppers. The filet side could have been bigger, but both sides of the T were tender and flavorful. 
The sides were all very good, if not a little skimpy. Each would be fine for one person and sharing the three worked out OK, but the look of one lonely potato on a plate for $8 (potato fondant) leaves you thinking that you may have been robbed. (Although, that one potato was incredibly luscious and tasty.)
We ordered two desserts to share--the PB&J and the mocha donuts. The donuts were incredible. I could have eaten a tray of them. And the PB&J was also good. The peanut butter was almost like a custard. They also brought out some ice cream bonbons--a nice touch.
Overall, a great meal, but for the price, probably reserved for special occasions. That said, I'd like to go back and try the burger. I think a burger and a cocktail would make a fine non-special-occasion meal.

The atmosphere and food here was spectacular.  The Bowery steak, which was described as deckle, was phenomenal and I haven't seen this on any menu in NYC.  The spaghetti with jalapeño and ricotta was amazing.  All of the apps- cauliflower steak, zucchini carpaccio, were great but the star was the polenta with mushrooms.  Leave room for desert..,,,the donuts were to die for!

Nothing exceptional here. Broiled oysters tasted like heavily breaded blue points. Bitter greens salad needed something crunchy like croutons or lardons. Spaghetti with jalapeño was so spicy it should've been noted by the waiter. I love a hint of jalapeño, but this was dry-ish spagetti and it was missing something like pancetta to make it savory. Desserts were a disappointment. Overall, standard steak house which I imagine more in the UES or midtown, since it's rather ho hum. I prefer BLT Steak for a more memorable steak experience.

I'm conflicted about this place.  I read about Bowery Meat Co. in one of the Thrillst emails and when I looked at the menu and saw all things meat, I immediately made a reservation for a Friday night date night with my husband.

The good: The food was excellent.  First, we had two mini starters, compliments of the kitchen.  One was bacon foccocia, and further proved all things are better with bacon.  We shared the steak tartare as an appetizer, and it too was amazing.  THe steak was incredibly fresh.  For the mains, I had the hanger steak and my husband had the special, which was the chateaubriand.  Again, awesome.  The staff was also very warm and welcoming.  

The not-so-good:  Although the staff was exceedingly pleasant, I feel as though we were misled when it came from to the specials.  As mentioned, my husband got the chateaubriand.  When it arrived, there was easily two pounds of meat, and the special was clearly for two people.  However, the waitress didn't tell us that when I ordered a main of my own.  Why not say, "Well the special serves two, so would you like a separate main course," or something along those lines?  Chateaubriand does not ALWAYS serve two.  

When the bill came, we were given the unpleasant notification that the chateaubriand special cost $98!  I know specials are a bit more expensive, but once again, we should have been told exactly how much food the dish came with, and that the cost was significantly higher than any other main dish.  

We were so put off that the meal cost so much more than anticipated that it kinda put a damper on our date night.

Fantastic meal full of flavor. Highlights; melt in your mouth aged filet mignon on the bone au poivre; short rib ravioli, surprising and delicious donuts and coffee dessert; steak tartare.  All were amazing. Highly recommend this place.

Went here with another couple last night. Manager Morgan was super friendly. Waiter was professional but not over bearing. Sommelier Michael knew his stuff. Food was outstanding. Would eat here again in a flash. Only thing I didn't like was their inflexible policy with the $35 corkage fee but I know I am spoiled living in Philly with all the BYOB's so it's not their fault. Try the duck lasagna!

I have never felt the need to write a review, but I swore to myself I'd start writing them when I loved a place.

Bowery Meat Company is excellent. Very nice mid-century modern lux interior, comfortable, classy... Great ambience. Also, the bar is super cool, would be good for a date.

Food is phenomenal. Had the filet mignon, A+. Also, the pork belly lettuce wraps are a hit. Great service and coffee and donuts dessert was legit awesome.

I'm a restaurant snob and I recommend this place with enthusiasm.

Visiting NYC for a girls weekend and found this place on a NYC new restaurant list, so glad we did. I do not seek out steak houses but let me tell you, everything I tried melted in my mouth. Filet Mignon, ravioli, Bowery steak, pork belly lettuce wraps, dounuts and coffee dessert... Everything was to die for! Interior was very luxe and high end yet approachable.

If I could give 4.5 stars, I would... but figured the one fault doesn't warrant an entire star's downgrade.

Great restaurant, great service, amazing food! The one thing I can say is that they use a little too much butter for my liking, but other than that every single thing they served us was phenomenal. And how'd they get the steak like that?? Perfectly medium rare on the inside and just the right amount crisp on the outside.

Would highly recommend coming here!

Umm yes. Just yes. You have to try this place!! Tried the oysters and the chateaubriand for two with a friend along with some whipped potatoes. Everything  was on point and melt in your mouth goodness. The place has a great vibe and the staff were very sweet. I've already made another booking so I can show some others friends what the hype is about :)

Bowery meat company lives up to its name! Had the steak tartare (light & savory), Bowery steak (damn good steak), cheeseburger (standard burger, tad salty) and finished with donuts & coffee cream (almost stole the show from the steak). Will be back to try the duck lasagna! BUT was disappointed not to see the short ribs on the menu
The place was very nice, the meat was very very good. The service was as good as it could possibly be. It was also fairly priced. Do not know if I would go again though, too many places to try.

Cutie and The Beast "Bowery Meat Company"

I finally made it to this dinner after running late for over an hour and a half. Geeeeeee!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Three of my friends were already seated since 7ish and had many, I mean many, cocktails and glasses of wine while waiting for HOTMESS me. I normally like to order the food for the table, but obviously I felt so bad that I let my friend's boyfriend order everything.

The decor of Bowery Meat Company is a trendy New York steakhouse look. By this I mean not an old-school Peter Lugger's look. It's more modern and sleek.The place has dark and cool lighting which proved to be too hard for me to use my camera so some of my photos were done using my iPhone 5C with flash. Chef Josh Carpon came over to our table to show us the meat board. Since I was so late I missed out on most of the appetizers and he was kind enough to bring me two extra broiled oysters. The broiled oysters were really really good! I can eat 20 raw bar oysters by myself within no time, but I normally don't care for heated/cooked oysters. This is my exception! These broiled oysters were fantastic! Still raw on the inside and topped with delicious garlic, romano cheese, bread crumbs, and parsley. I also had a few bites of Spaghetti Aglio e Olio. It had a delicious lemon and cheese flavor. (I took really crappy photos below)

For dinner, I enjoyed the Cote du Boeuf for Two 38oz. The steak was cooked to a perfect medium rare and came pre-sliced. Each piece packed plenty of flavor. I also had cauliflower, sautéed mushrooms, and whipped potatoes on the side, but the truth is I didn't need them! I don't eat steak often, maybe once a month, so when I eat gooooood steak I'd rather just enjoy the meat and nothing else. Good, aged beef is like a superstar and a true star does not need a backup dancer or singer!!!! That is how Cutie rolls with steak (^_^)

A serious steakhouse never existed in my neighborhood and this place is officially the first one to open in this area. Since 2010, many big name owners/chefs have opened restaurants on Bowery. DBGB was first opened by chef Daniel Boulud. Since then, others include The General by EMM Group and Gemma at Bowery Hotel. The three latest additions to the area have been BAR PRIMI by Andrew Carmellini, Narcissa at Standard Hotel, and Cherche Midi. After a few short years of Pulino's Bar and Pizzeria, Keith McNally closed it to then recently open the space again (without any major renovations) as Cherche Midi. Bowery Meat Company was already packed with all kinds of people from those who love meat to those who, like myself, don't wait for a NY Times review to come out three month later. I'm sure the Wall Street crowd will be here in no time, too. I always notice that these kinds of new steakhouses are filled with finance people. I'm not sure why, but my guess is that men like to talk business over a good steak!? I recommend you to come here any night of the week for dinner and drink.

With such rave reviews from Mike C, Foodiemagician and every burger article written this place was a MUST try!!!!  I had to wait for Jan 4th after the holiday rush to get a reservation to try this place.  

With a lot of research on what to order I must say it was a huge disappointment.  

Venue: (4/5) trendy, a beautiful steakhouse.  The restaurant is perfect to impress.  The bar is inviting which would attract  'let's be scene' crowd.  

Food (2/5) let's just start this off by saying I love salt.  I add salt to most things I order.  BUT today WOW on the salt, a bit too much for me.

Bitter salad (1/5) Salty.  If there was less salt I would recommend this salad to everyone, but all I can remember was the amount of water I had after my salad.

Burger (3/5) very good although I ordered my burger rare and got a medium rare burger.  Not sure how this happened because rare is pretty easy. Not my favorite burger in the city but I would order this again.  Raclette is an amazing choice for a cheese. 

Bone in Filet (4/5) my friend raved how his steak was the most tender steak he had.  Have to give this a shout out.

Service (3/5) our waiter was great and perfectly attentive.  The food service to the table was super slow.  I'm unsure why because the restaurant seemed overstaffed.  My water glass was always filled, but the food took longer to get to the table.  I met the owner and he was gracious.  I feel with more time these kinks will be worked out.

The recent Eater coverage of the duck lasagna intrigued me to try Bowery Meat Co.
Sadly, I did not order the hyped dish but the meal was excellent and I have no doubts I will go back again to eat it!
After ordering our dirty martinis we were served oxtail bone marrow arancini bites (risotto balls) courtesy of the house
In the end, my boyfriend and I ordered:
Live Sea Scallop with Yuzu, Radish, Apple, Pink Sea Salt  
Bitter Greens Caesar Dressing with Toasted Breadcrumbs, Parmesan
as well as that evenings special steak dish: The dry-aged ribeye "Tomahawk" steak for two 
The meat was cooked to a perfect medium-rare and served sliced with the bone on the board..perfect for carnivorous nibbling 
We added some charred brussel sprouts as a side in addition to the steak being served with potato croquettes.
Chef Josh Capon came out during our meal and advised us to let the croquettes soak up all the runnings from the meat which is a nice personal touch making especially good impressions from such a new restaurant.
Can not wait to return for that lasagna.......

The first of 4 birthday related fashionplates is our timeless Bianca top at the new steakhouse Bowery Meat Company.  One of the besties took me here for my bday and we waited at the marble bar having some bday champs- Veuve, while waiting for our table to become ready.  We decided to dive right in and split a bunch of items.  The broiled oysters were almost as dope as Dirty French and we were thankful we were not on a romantic date as we were loving the extra garlic.  The foie gras was creamy and decadent but not as heavy as usual which was a nice pleasant surprise!

We then opted for a nice red wine to complement the red meat that was coming.  We split the Bowery Steak medium rare which was perfectly cooked and delish, we also split the sour cream hash browns which was amazing.  We were super full but the lovely couple next to us ordered the pb&j bread pudding that was crazy big and filling.  It was yummy and a great way to end our bestie bday meal.

This place will put a dent in your wallet, but it's worth it.  The decor kind of reminds me of Mad Men a little bit.  All the food was delicious, and they throw you out something to try along with your bread.  The burger was great and my friends veal was off the charts according to her.

I had a NYE dinner here with my best friends and it was seriously the BEST food I have ever had!!! 

We got the deviled eggs, oysters and foie gras as appetizers.   And let me tell you - the deviled eggs were AMAZING!  So was everything else, but I am just a HUGE fan of deviled eggs since I'm from the south.   I never thought i'd say this but they definitely beat my grandmas.  (Sorry, Grandma)

Then as our main course we had the Steak and PORKCHOPS - just amazing. 

Josh Capon is such a talented chef and I think everyone should go to this restaurant.  Its definitely a treat!

Maybe I went on an off-night, but I'm a little surprised by the overwhelming hype and positive reviews for BMC.

Everything about my experience was completely fine...but nothing was particularly memorable.  The complimentary bacon rosemary focaccia and oxtail bone marrow arancini were a nice touch - the arancini in particular was very good (although in my mind, it's hard to mess up fried risotto balls too much), but the flavors of the oxtail and bone marrow didn't really come through.

For our mains, we had the duck lasagna for two and the bowery steak.  Although there were other meats that sounded great, I felt we had to get the much talked-about lasagna, and given the portion size, I didn't really have room in my stomach to order much else.  The lasagna was...extremely average.  Similar to the arancini, the ingredients sounded amazing, but in actuality, you really couldn't taste the duck at all.  Maybe I would've enjoyed it more if it were a smaller, regularly priced portion - although I do understand the benefit of the larger portion, which allows the outside to crisp up without drying out the inside.

I was excited for the steak, since rib eye is my favorite cut, and I was interested in their take on it - unfortunately, I really didn't love it.  I'm not sure if it was overcooked (the restaurant's pretty dark, so I couldn't judge based on color), but it was pretty tough/chewy.  Side of fries was meh...not very crispy and incredibly salty.

I was really really excited to come here and had been salivating at all the pictures I'd been seeing of the food, but it was a little bit of a letdown.  I might come back to try some of their other cuts...but based on their bowery steak, I'm slightly skeptical.  This is definitely a place where you benefit by coming in a larger group though, so maybe that was part of the issue.  Since we were only a party of 2, our desire to try the lasagna prohibited us from trying much else on the menu, which was a shame - maybe the other meat options would have left us with a better impression.

This place crushed it! Great food, service and atmosphere.  Try the off menu Kobe beef meatball appetizer: 2 amazing meatballs with sauce  I have never had meatballs this good! Last night we had the sirloin cooked to perfect which was tender and delicious. The bone-in filet was terrific. The hash browns with sour cream and scallions was amazing. Service was terrific. No rushing here   This is now our go to steak restaurant. Can't wait to try more on the menu since everything sounds great. This is a true 5 star experience!

without a doubt lives up to the hype

capon works the room with the best of them

NY strip steak is a clear ciut favorite

notable mention for zuchinni carpaccio

PB&J dessert was insane!

How do I even begin... This was one of the most indulgent, and still well balanced restaurants I have eaten at since spending a month in Europe this summer.

We began with braised oxtail and bone marrow arancini and bacon Rosemary foccatia bread from Lafayette. Compliments of the house, yum.

For starters we had Chinese bbq pork belly lettuce wraps which were flavorful but still light, and a great twist on pork belly. New also had crispy polenta with mushroom ragu which was phenomenal, along with grilled zucchini with feta cheese and almonds that was so fresh and unique that it was a pleasant surprise.

Oh, also did I mention broiled oysters? This was a great twist on a classic. I highly recommend for those who enjoy raw oysters and those who don't alike.

For the main course we shared duck lasagna which was out of this world! I am usually hesitant with duck because it can be too gamey for me, but this lasagna was so well balanced and incredibly delicious. We shared the Chateaubriand... which was so incredible! So tender, and flavorful without being overwhelming. I am getting hungry all over again thinking about it!

&& when I thought there wasn't any room left to eat, I made some, because coffee and donuts... dear lord, those coffee and donuts... Just do it.

All in all, this was an amazing experience. From the service to the food, it was absolutely incredible, and any hype on the restaurant is well deserved. I will recommened Bowery Meat Company to meat lovers and non-meat lovers alike.

When Justin Bieber visits the Bowery, you know times have certainly changed. Right off the city's latest haute dining strip, on the corner of 1st St and Extra Pl lies Bowery Meat Co. Ever so ironically, this is not some kind of butcher shop, but rather John McDonald and Chef Josh Capon's newest steak house. I didn't encounter the previously mentioned controversial Canadian singer (rapper?) on my visit. Better yet, greeted by an array of uniformed servers, hosts and Matire D's. We had a reservation, which helped. Although the restaurant was nearly empty when we arrived, it was sure to fill up fast on a Monday night. Now that I mention it, the butcher shop in question did exist on the table. First to land in front of us were two Chef amuse bouche: Oxtail Arancini and Charcuterie with Bacon Rosemary Focaccia.  I'm a sucker for oysters  so when I spotted Broiled Oysters with Garlic, Romano Cheese and Parsley, I could not resist. Hot and broiled as promised, I was easily transported back to New Orleans, almost forgetting to use my tiny fork in the process. A knockout. Next, we decided to get a bit ballsy for the Bowery and try the Duck Lasagna for two. You see, I'm also a sucker for duck and even though I was at a steakhouse, again I had a moral responsibility. The Chef (unsure if it was Capon, he didn't present himself) presented and served this ooey, gooey experience.  Glorious, wonderful, marvelous! A 10 out of 10. Follow our lead and get a side of spinach to add some variety to all the meat and cheese and pasta. Room for dessert was no where to be found, a quarter portion of the lasagna needed to be packed to go. With our check was presented 2 bite-sized frozen petit fours. Oh the temptation. Delicious. All in all, an enjoyable experience, friendly staff and good portions. Maybe this new Bowery isn't so bad. If it's good enough for Bieber, it's good enough for me.

This place is incredible.  It sounds like a steak house, and it is, but the food is better (and more imaginitive) and the vibe is way more cool and modern.  

My friend made us make the trek on a weeknight after work - after initially being pissed at how far it was worth the trip.  I thanked him forever.

Five stars because this is worth a trek across town.  The food is a little pricey, but you won't regret it.  Solid beer and cocktail selection.  The servers are all awesome - friendly - and they brought us like a million bites to eat before our meal.  No reason.

The bowery steak is awesome - comes with some chimchurri sauce.  Duck - awesome.  Bone-in filet - yep you guessed it, awesome.

Great Lively Space , interesting crowd and attentive wait staff.  Tried all 3 varieties of oysters. All extremely crisp and fresh. Kumamoto's Dressed with Wasabi Leaf & Lemon are a can't miss. Had an interesting appetizer - Roasted Cauliflower Steak with Almonds, Capers and Raisins - expertly explained by waiter and it was terrific. 
As an entree I had  Herb Crusted Lamb Chops with a wonderful cucumber yogurt "salad" on the side....excellent. Partner had Charred Hanger steak and it was terrific as well. Forgot to mention that during the seating the waiter brought over a few small appetizers for us the try as well, nice touch including the Bon Bon at the end of dessert.  This is a must try in NYC this winter.

The meat is out of the this world!!

Pros: get the filet! It was the best filet I have ever had!! The wine was very delicious. The ambiance is sexy and great for a nice Friday night dinner 

Cons: none!
Took my wife here for her birthday. In a word, AWESOME. The pork rib eye was incredible.

Great steaks, and great meatballs (special dish)
Also the desert - cookies with ice cream was amazing!

My girlfriend and I were having a nice experience at bowery until the actual steak came.  It's a nice place with a good vibe. Bread was good. We started with the broiled oysters and the Caesar salad both were good. I go to steak houses all the time and always get the bone in filet. So we ordered the bone in filet and it was drenched in some sauce.  I didn't realize what au poivre was and didn't see it next to the bone in filet on the menu. We hated the sauce.  Just a side not if you have a very delicious tender piece of meat it doesn't need to be drenched in sauce. I have had bone in filet from strip house to mastros to del friscos and it maybe has some butter or salt and
Pepper and that's it. It's obviously not a good cut of meat bc would have enough flavor without the sauce on top. So we told the waiter and he brought the menu over and showed me the "au poivre ra". We Obv had no clue what that was.  The manager than came over and offered us free dessert. My gf and I didn't touch the steak at all. The right thing to do was to take it off the bill. There are way too many steakhouses in the city to deal with poor customer service like this. If you want a good piece of meat with good customer service skip this place!

WOW.  What a surprise this place was.  This was totally unexpected and I was overwhelmed by everything here.  We booked a last minute 9pm reservation on a Saturday night and I thought, "Here we go, just another steakhouse..".  This was certainly not the case. This place exceeded all expectations.

We sat about 10 mins after the reservation time, which was fine with me given that they have a tasty and varied cocktail list and wine list.  We sipped at the stylish bar for a few and then were escorted into a the well-decorated dining room.  Divided into a couple of rooms, it looked as if we had stepped into a West Elm or Restoration Hardware.  The place was packed and the room was buzzing.  It's not where you come if you want a quiet Friday night dinner, but you probably shouldn't be eating down on the Bowery if that's what you're looking for, anyway.

We were promptly greeted by our server, who was on point at every moment of the evening.  At no point did we have to wait for anything and he anticipated every one of our needs.   We were greeted with mini short-rib risotto balls, which I could have eaten a dozen of.  The section of breads was also excellent.

We started with the Chinese Pork Belly, which was served as do-it-yourself lettuce wraps accompanied by picked vegetables.  They were excellent.   We also had the Broiled Oysters, which were throwbacks to some of the great places in New Orleans that serve them so well.  They were perfection.

For dinner, we decided to split the dry-aged NY Strip with Roasted Shallots and the Cheeseburger with Fries.  The strip was delivered a perfect medium and the roasted shallot added a nice accompaniment.  It was as good a strip as you can get in New York.  The burger, however, was incredible and the fries were cooked to perfection.   The burger rivaled anything the best of NYC could throw at it and it was served on the perfect brioche bun.  The fries were as good as the best Steak Frites places the city can offer, such as Les Halles.  The waiter asked if we were splitting the burger and it arrived cut perfectly into 4's, without a crumb of the bun damaged.  We were stuffed and elected to skip dessert.

This is a place I want to go back to with a group.  It's loud and rowdy, but not in a frat boy way and not in an Del Frisco's fat-cat expense account kind of way.  It's just fun.  There was a birthday party of 10 behind us and they delivered a cake with sparkers.  Even the chef took part in the celebration and got sucked into the rowdiness himself.  Maybe not a good choice on his part given that it was a busy weekend night, but maybe he's got the kitchen under total control.  The food certainly seems to suggest so.

I'd say this steakhouse is for the person that wants steak, but doesn't value steak as the #1 priority.  I came on the strength of a NY Mag review, and the large amounts of top reviews given here.  When I heard about the Bowery Steak, I thought, how can this miss?

Apps:

Bitter Greens - Fresh salad, was a nice different take on a typical caesar salad.  I thought it was good, albeit a bit overdrenched in dressing.

Roasted Cauliflower Steak - Good, but my wife thought it was great.  Tastes like roasted cauliflower, which is good.  She ate the stem, which I did not like (I never do).  She loved the capers.

Mains:

Spaghetti Aglio e Olio - A great pasta side with the mains.  Flavorful, not overly saucy, and perfectly cooked.  Not sure if it is enough for a full main, but I'm a big pasta eater.

Cheeseburger - Wife wanted to try the great chef's burgers, as he is known for his burgers.  I thought it was good, not great.  I'd prefer Shake Shack any day, but I suppose this is a "luxury" burger.  The patty is crazy thick, so be ready to get that "burger intoxication" while eating.

Bowery Steak - This was supposed to the the coup de grâce for steak for me - a steak made up of the outer ring of the best cut of steak (in my opinion) - the rib eye cap.  8oz of the juiciest, tenderest, most flavorful piece of beef.  And it fell flat on its face.  I had it cooked medium rare, which should keep the juice and flavor there.  It looked wonderful when it came, but alas, it was not meant to be.  The meat was not juicy, it was not flavorful, and it was just like eating a sirloin steak.  I was heartbroken.

Sides:

Sour Cream & Onion Hash Brown - a potato "puck".  Was good, crispy outside, potato-ey inside.  Very greasy, I do not recommend eating it by itself, or with only 2 people.  Best for 4 people.

Garlic Spinach - Alas, this was my favorite dish of the evening.  Sad when you think about it, but happy because it was a greatly prepared vegetable.  Very tasty.  Not overly greasy/creamy/garlic-y.  Very good overall, would've eaten on a regular basis.

Dessert:

PB&J - Very good ending to the meal.  Not super sweet, very tasty.  I'd recommend.

Coffee - Good coffee.

Honestly, this should be a 4.5 star but there's no half stars so I had to give them 4 stars. It couldn't round up to 5 stars because of the service but overall wonderful experience. I made reservations for me and my best friend for her birthday and it happened to be super bowl Sunday so the restaurant was fairly empty. We got here around 815pm when my reservation was for 830pm. Got seated right away at this little circle booth perfect for a couple (perfect for two girls right???) but I really did love our seats cause we got to sit right next to each other which made talking much easier. 

We started off with cocktails, I had the loneliest monk because I read someone's review who said it's too sweet for their liking so I thought it'd be perfect for me. Boy was I wrong!!! SOOO STRONGGG!!!! It was way too strong for me. Even my best friend who likes to drink Jameson on the rocks thinks it's a tad too strong. She had an amazing drink, the  BEYOND THE WALL, it was nice and refreshing and came with a candied ginger. It was so good she ordered a second one while I was having trouble downing mine. ONTO THE FOOD!!!!

So we already explored the menu prior to coming to this restaurant so we sort of knew what we wanted to order. They gave us the focaccia bread and salami and an oxtail bone marrow fried rice ball before we ordered. So for starters we had the foie gras and chicken liver pate and the steak tartare. The foie gras is definitely a MUST!! It came with thick slices of bread and upon spreading the pate on the bread it melted perfectly in my mouth. Super flavorful and not too heavy. The steak tartare was had a very nice texture and was seasoned very well. At one point we just ate the raw meat without the toast cause it was so good. Onto the main course, we were debating between each ordering a dish or doing the steak for two. We decided that to do the chauterbriand steak for two, it was the most expensive price per ounce on the menu and we love our chauterbriand. We also got a side of fries just because who doesn't like fried potato. The steak came with a sauce and some brussel sprouts and potato. The potato was a bit plain (fries were yummier) but the main attraction is the steak. very very flavorful and I love how it's precut so it wasn't much work to start eating. The steak was a bit tougher on the outside, but for such a big piece of meat Im not surprise. But once you got to the center, it was the perfect pink and was super tender. One of the best chauterbriand I've eaten. We were so full by the end of our main course we almost skipped dessert, but we ended up getting one to share. We got the cookies and cream which was chocolate walnut cookies with vanilla bean ice cream. We each took a cookie and the minute we picked it up we could already feel how warm it was and we took one bite and both of us went "Mmmmmmm." The cookie was the perfect perfect definition of a crunchy of the outside but soft and gooey on the inside. SOOO GOOD AND IT WAS STILL HOT!!! With a scoop of vanilla ice cream and it was match made in heaven. But sadly we were too full and only ate one cookie each (order comes with 4). I was a bit disappointed in that they didn't have the soufflé anymore but overall definitely a procey restaurant but I'd say it's worth the price you pay.
Legit. Loved the Filet, Short Rib Ravs, and meatball apps. Had an awesome server named Paul. He was the best I had in a while.

Place was fantastic. Great meal but can't say that was the best steak I ever had. The Bartender with the sickest stash was the best part of the night, he was personable and made u feel special. Had a four course meal and felt kind of rushed and felt forced into ordering more food -i.e. He said we should get a mid course bc we would have to wait a really long time for our meat to rest ! Hind site ... That was stupid. Wish I could of rated It higher but the Waiter was being pushy to the point where it was kind of uncomfortable - so if you got money to burn , want to be told what to do and feel taken advantage of then you should try it out

We were really excited to try this new place. When we did, however, it was very disappointing. The place itself has a nice interior and a good wine list. About the food: steak was by far the worst one I've ever tried: it has a weird perfume-like taste and weird aftertaste. I couldn't make myself eat any more than one bite. The fish was ok, the sides were ok too: not great, not horrible. Just ok. The service was the only thing that was splendid: waiters were attentive and polite. It is still definitely not a place I would go back to again.

KenScale: 8.0/10

Bowery Meat Company looks like everything a New York local would avoid if what you care about is the quality of the food, not the glitzy scenery. Opened by the duo of John McDonald and chef John Capon, it looks like a very predictable steakhouse that you go to not for the meat but for people-watching. Surprisingly, I had a pleasant meal at the restaurant, with some outstanding meat dishes for a carnivore feast. 

I tried to minimize my share of starters so I can focus on the meat dishes more, but all the dishes that came before the steaks were enjoyable, starting with the complementary bread and arancini. Wedge salad with came with nuts, seeds and Greek yogurt dressing was more than serviceable, and I loved the broiled oysters that came with garlic, romano cheese and bread crumbs. Now, on to the steaks. I've ordered three different slices of meat. Veal chop that came grilled with Moorish spices and burnt orange that you can rub onto the meat looked and sounded so promising, yet I was surprised with the rather tough texture of the meat. On the other hand, bone-in filet mignon was quite juicy and tender. The best meat of the night though was the Bowery steak that came with salsa verde and whipped potato. It looks rather simple-looking with none of the decadence you look for in an excellent steak dish, but the meat was very well-cooked and worked very well with the potato. The sides of mushroom and hash brown were also quite nice. Even if you're stuffed at this point, don't skip dessert, with such decadent options like s'mores sundae that consists of toasted marshmallow ice cream, brownie bites and chocolate dipped Graham crackers. 

As noted above, the restaurant has all the elements of a sexy restaurant perfect for watching young, handsome people. The services were surprisingly attentive, and there is a rather large wine list so make sure to supplement your feast with a glass of cocktail or a bottle of wine. The restaurant was absolutely packed even on one of the coldest nights of the year, and a table (especially for a larger group) seems rather hard to come by so make sure to book early. Bowery Meat Company is definitely worth checking out if you're looking for a chic night out to start with serous meat feast.

Just what NYC needs. Another overpriced steakhouse. And FU RR and RP at NY Mag for touting the ribeye Bowery steak as genius. 

Greeting- yes
Vibe- mini- Vegas restaurant
Prices- sky high
Wine list- limited and sky high mark ups. A high $35 corkage fee
Parking- lot next door
Service- Marion was excellent
Bathroom- Fail
Food
I love it when a restaurant offers amuse bouche. It makes the the meal exciting. With the prices here it is the least they can do for you.
- cauliflower $15! For a small piece. If you are going to rip me off at least give me the whole head of cauliflower for $15!
- here is comes. Bowery steak $54. A small piece of meat. Tasteless. Looks and has the texture of flank steak. Putting salsa on the top proves it is all a farce. A quality piece of meat at $54 does not need salsa. Do not get this steak. One of the biggest disappointments in my food dinning experiences ever. 
- dessert of s,more ice cream Sunday $10 is cute and good. Donuts with mocha budino was good $10. Chocolate layer cake was horrible. A cake from a $1 Better Crocker box would blow this one away.

WIGB? What do you think?

Food (5/5)   Decor (5/5)   Service (4/5)   Value (3/5)

Bowery Meat Company is, in my opinion, one of the best restaurants in New York City. While the name suggests that it's a steakhouse, it's really much, much more. The focus of the restaurant is definitely on meat, but they serve it in a wide variety of different ways. For instance, to start, we were served bacon focaccia. It sounds a little unusual (meat baked into bread), but it only goes to confirm the age old wisdom that everything tastes good with bacon. My favorite dishes were the zucchini carpaccio, short rib ravioli, and duck lasagna. Zucchini carpaccio sounds pretty boring and not something I would normally order. Fortunately though, I came here with some coworkers who had had it before and it was outstanding. They top the zucchini with different herbs, seasonings, and nuts, and they turn turn it into a veggie you really want to eat. The duck lasagna is probably the best item at the restaurant. I was too busy wolfing it down to focus on how it's composed, but what struck me was that unlike a traditional lasagna, it is relatively light on sauce. This works well because the duck itself is plentiful, tender, and juicy. For the steaks, we had the cote de boeuf and bowery steak. Both were delicious steaks, but as a whole, I thought the items I mentioned earlier stood out to me more as what really makes Bowery Meat Company worth coming back to. And, for what it's worth, I thought the steaks were on the expensive side, even for New York City, and caused me to knock off an additional point for value.

I think a number of people on Yelp have rated this restaurant poorly because they expected it to be a steakhouse and it didn't meet their expectations in that regard. So here is your warning: this is not a traditional steakhouse! The genius is in the appetizers and pastas. I thought the steaks were good, but you won't find them hype-worthy per se. Also, I would recommend coming in a larger group. Some of the items, like the duck lasagna, are so big that if you came in a party of two, you could maybe order an app or two plus the lasagna and you wouldn't be able to eat anything else. A larger group will allow you to order all the different things and try them. Highly recommended!

Thankfully I read through the website before visiting, and already knew not to expect a steak house, so don't let the name fool you or else you may be disappointed.

The menu here was nice, variety of different dishes.  Lots of shell fish, and seafood (hence my previous paragraph).  We shared oysters, shrimp cocktail and the meatball for an appetizer.  Which were all fresh and good.  For dinner I had a lobster, and steak share setup with company.  I really enjoyed my drink from the bar, and the dessert was warm baked cookies and ice cream.

Service was on par, and the atmosphere was what you would expect from a restaurant in this area.

Overall, I think as NYC residents we are spoiled with the amount of great restaurants.  Being from anywhere else I probably would have given it 5 stars, being from NYC and enjoying fine dining I really wanted to give it 3 stars, but found it might be misleading so I stuck somewhere in the middle.  Give it a go, you won't be blown away or disappointed.

Fairly new to the New York dining scene Bowery Meat Company has strong potential.

The bar area - while attractive - can be uncomfortably tight. With tables positioned awkwardly one must constantly move aside to let others pass.

Once seated for dinner we found the music to be alarmingly loud and inappropriate. When mentioned the music was lowered to the point of nonexistence and the four of us enjoyed the rest of our stay.

Appetizers included the Meatballs and Octopus specials which did not disappoint. However the highlight was the Dry-Aged 14 oz New York Strip with Roasted Shallots. Cooked perfectly medium with juices flowing this was certainly one of the best New York Strips I've tasted. A wonderful choice.
Other selections included the Herb Crusted Colorado Lamb Chops and Grilled Veal Chop which were both enjoyed. The sides included Fondant Potato and Garlic Spinach - both worked.

Service was professional, friendly and attentive - no issues

A nice twist on the traditional italian steakhouse.  The duck lasagna (for two) alone is worth coming here for.  But the appetizers, meat dishes, and desserts are all firing on all cylinders.

We had the scallop crudo, deviled eggs with caviar, broiled oysters, wagyu meatballs, duck lasagna, burger, and the "Donuts and Coffee" for dessert.

Great cocktail and wine list too.  All around top-notch restaurant.

It's all about he meat and the atmosphere at Bowery Meat Company. I was lucky enough to book in advance and get a corner book that over looked the main dining area. Everything from top to bottom was too notch from the service to drinks. We started with Wagyu Meatballs and steak tartare both were exceptional, me and my fiancée had the pepper crusted ribeye and lamb. Everything couldn't have been more perfect.

I am probably the only vegetarian writing a review & the restaurant deserves all 5 stars. Brought my brother here for a birthday dinner and the service was amazing. Thank you :) Oh! and the music was great too. 
 
We started with the Farmer's Salad. (Great)  also shared the crispy polenta & the Zucchini  starter. All amazing & cooked so perfectly.

For dinner the ravioli on special (asparagus and ricotta, i believe) was amazing
And my brother raved about the Bowery Steak. 

The sides were also done so well. Very refreshing to go to a restaurant where everything is seasoned so perfectly. (I'm am an avid salt/pepper'er & it never crossed my mind to do so to the food in front of us. So melt in your mouth good- (spinach/potatoes especially.)

Also appreciated staff knowledge. (Especially for dessert, & alerting us to ingredients that coincide with dietary restrictions.) It was awesome for a steakhouse to know so much about the exact opposite diet!

I had high expectations. The burger was phenomenal but the steaks were only so so. When I order a ribeye I expect a steak that's at least 1.5inches thick. The steaks here were only about an inch thick. They lacked flavor and weren't cooked to order. One of my friends sent back his steak because it was overcooked. The chef handled it well and personally came to apologize. The service is good but the steak quality lags. But the s'more Sunday was awesome.

World class restaurant with excellent food and wonderful, friendly service. Best Italian steakhouse in the city; head and shoulders above Costata and Quality Italian in midtown. While the steaks are top notch, don't neglect the rest of the menu which is prepared with the same quality and attention.  Chef Paul Dibari does a fabulous job with the menu.  My wife and I try to go back as often as we can.

This place is so damn fantastic. 
The service was wonderful. 
You are greeted with a big smile. The people who work there seem to be happy to be there. 

I got myself a girly cocktail.. forgot the name but it was fruity and pink, which was great because it was my birthday.

We got the complementary oxtail arancini balls and couple bites of bacon focaccia with some sort of charcuterie (sopressata, maybe?) - hmmm doesn't really matter because it was delicious and it was put in front of me. 
I wanted to order more arancini balls but wanted to save room for the entree. 

We ordered the filet mignon for 2 and it was to die for. 
Do you know when a steak is so tender that it MELTS in your mouth? 
Buttery perfection. Absolutely perfect. 
I ordered steak and eggs for brunch a few days later and it tasted like crap after that dreamy fillet mignon. 

We shared the s'more sundae at the end of the meal. That thing was huge. There were brownies freaking bites on the bottom... I regret nothing. It was worth the calorie bomb. 

I am a fan. This is really a place where they are focused in every little detail. From the ambiance, to the service, and omg the food is spectacular. 

I would like to have THAT filet mignon as my last meal please, and yes I'll eat the one for 2 because it'll supposedly be my last meal anyways. lol yolo 

p.s. is it weird to mention that the hand soap in the restroom was also great? yup, that's weird indeed. Details, man. Details.
The best burger I've ever had. Garlic spinich was also very good.  Great service. I like the decor and everything else. I had 2 glasses of 1942 which was expensive but worth it.

Among the four of us the person who scored the highest was the person who ordered the Filet Mignon.  The fish and chicken received poor ratings, the salads were uninteresting.  Not sure how this restaurant received two stars from the NYTs, but experience would rate it one star at best.

By far my favorite restaurant in NYC! The added bonus - super star chef, Josh Capon, will often be seen on-site doing what he does best - hosting & ensuring a truly memorable experience. Bowery Meat is my go to for fine dining fun, hands down!

Definitely a destination .
Starting with the appetizers 
Good red wine selection 
And most important -the meat.
Fantastic ribeye done right  .
Finish with the little doughnuts .....
And you will be back!
Should have went all out and just got the steak for two. It looked like the best option. Food was just okay.

This restaurant is pretty serious about their meats! Everything was delicious - In addition to the steak I also enjoyed the cauliflower appetizer, duck lasagna, and bread pudding dessert. It was also a pretty cool vibe - so overall a good experience.

First restaurant I'm giving five stars. Broiled oysters and duck lasagna was my meal oh yes with garlic spinach. The duck lasagna is baked for two so there was plenty to take home. I shared a piece with a friend who is not big on duck but she loved it. My daughter and fiancé shared this place with me and we had a lovely evening. From the moment we entered, too the moment we left the Bowery night was just the best.

I was prepared not to like this place because it seemed overhyped, very expensive, and Justin Bieber had been here... (what could be more repellent than that?) but had a really enjoyable experience.

It's beautiful inside in a fancy but manly decor kind of way. I felt a little spoiled with the little extras: bacon focaccia and cured meat and some kind of truffle arancini ball for amuse bouches and a dessert bite of something potentially with hazelnut and ice cream. Our waiter was really nice and attentive. He smiled at us a lot and swooped in immediately to remove items or take orders.

We had the burger and the Bowery steak. The Bowery steak was good, but was actually outshined by the burger. That was really awesome. I can't wait to come back for that. We were thinking that it was much better than the Minetta Tavern burger. I also liked the Grenache they offered by the glass.

Terrible dining experience. Packed in like sardines, deafeningly noisy. These conditions could have been tolerable if the food was good. The much touted "Bowery Steak" came out cold, with no char at all, tasteless carrots, and less than eager service. And all this for exorbitant prices!! Never Again!

If you are interested in trying Bowery Meat Company, you should do it soon. Because if there's any justice in the world this over-priced, over-hyped, nightclub of a restaurant should be closed soon. The famous "bowery steak" seemed like the grisly trimmings of a nicer steak - rolled into a cute circle! $56 for that? Really? Service was condescending and indifferent - like the food. Of course, if you ENJOY a noisy, packed, hostile dining environment, by all means give it a chance. My opinion is you could spend your money elsewhere and have a better meal and better dining experience.

Thrill ist says it's one of NY's 10 best steak houses. So I went on Sunday.

Sat at bar but dining area looked good 

First.  Good red selection by the glass.  Bars are notorious for bad bar wines but The Butcher cab or the Malbec do the trick

Nice treat of salami and focaccia as well as a warm gooey ball of something

Pasta with jalapeño is good as it's a dryer pasta with a garlic base and a pleasant bite. Needed a tad more butter ( ask for it. It's perfect) and Batali touch, but good. Oh, it comes out FAST!

Main course. Bone in NY strip, rare plus with a slight char. Perfectly delivered. Nice cut at about an inch and an eighth and great quality. 

Note. Need a real steak knife.   Kmart knife does not cut it

Menu needs another veggie dish that's green 

Do units and coffee for desert.  Sooo good.  Great texture on both. Ice cream ball after! 

Music. 90s hits.  Works. Some good songs.

Easy to get to with the F subway

No Bieber. .....perfect!

Solid.  Go! Not bad Thrillist. Thanks

I came here for the Bowery Steak and chickened out at the last minute as I've heard such terrible things about the particular cut and preparation of this dish. I went with the bone-in Filet Mignon and it was incredible. It was super tender and was served a perfect medium rare. The Au Poivre sauce added great flavor to the steak. For apps, I had the Wagyu meatballs and the Zucchini Carpaccio. The meatballs were served atop delicious creamy cheesy polenta and the Carpaccio was nice and light. The mushroom fricassee and the sour cream & onion hash brown as sides were very good and the triple chocolate layer cake was very dry. Don't order it.

This place has a really good bar area, great service and gorgeous dim lighting and would be suited for a girls' night out, birthday celebrations or date night.

Just as amazing as i expected. Capon can do no wrong by me. This place is swarming with business men in the best of ways. I sat in the lounge for a casual bite with a friend. Impeccable service, just the right amount of attention (great staff in the bar area). Complimentary starters of mini arancini pesto balls and bread with a slice of cured meat. I was dying for the steak tartare which was very good and had a strong mustard to it, but the standout was the cauliflower steak. The capers,oil, golden raisins, and cauliflower has to be one of the best bites ive had in nyc for a while. Finish off the meal with a complimentary mini ice cream ball (think of it as a chic "dibs"), and we were on our way. I would love to come back for a filet and martini and sit at that bar and people watch (and mingle!). Bravo,
Glad i celebrated  my belated birthday here

The 1st visit: Yes to the strip steak, grilled onions, hash brown potatoes, and the donuts and coffee. So far the customer service is A+.

The 2nd visit: Loved the T-bone steak. And the grilled onions were again a winner. My husband was not in love with the bitter greens salad.

The 3rd visit: they have a discounted burger Sunday night which was pretty good.

Non steak items: Ravioli is descent. Pork buns were tasty. Brussel sprouts are yummy. The smores desert seems like a lot but the flavor combo is delightful.

This is now my go to steak house! Yummy!

This place is a joke. If you are a celeb and willing to get in an instagram photo with the Chef then you get treated A+. 

Mediocre across the board. Go down the street to cherche midi for the prime rib or across the bridge to Lugers.

Five Stars. Boom. I went here expecting an overrated steak place however I was pleasantly surprised.  I loved it so much the very next day I attempted to make one of their appetizer dishes I liked so much at home. As far as what to order - Duck Lasagna hands down - my mouth is still watering at the thought of it. I don't even eat duck! The Bowery steak was great, a nice center cut. The Zucchini Carpaccio - yum and the wedge salad complemented everything as a refreshing bite.
Fantastic!  Food, service, ambience.  Love loved the filet mignon and steak tartare.  Smore desert was fab!

I loved this place from start to finish. The decor, ambience, music set the tone for a great dinner experience. Waiter wasn't up to the standard of the restaurant, on the contrary, the sommelier was very nice and helpful in navigating their good selection of wines. 
Overall, we had a great experience, we loved the food and the place. Will definitely come back!

I would go once in a while. It is a nice place to take your date to. The food is clean and good. Oysters with Yuzu was a highlight. New York Strip could have been better. We asked for Medium rare but it came out Medium. Service could be improved. 

Anyway, it is a nice place, but I'd also be happy just to get steak from Whole Foods and cook it myself at home as well.

I've given four stars because of the quality/price ratio - otherwise this meal might have yielded five.

The amuse bouches are a simultaneous exercise in parsimony and generosity . The delicious arancini are the size of large marbles, and one each is barely a taste. A savory focaccia was presented in four pinky size slivers and a like number of paper thin rounds of a roughly 1 and 1/4" diameter salami. This will certainly leave you hungry for more. There is no bread basket.

Cocktails, a negroni, and a Tito's martini, were expertly made. A glass of Riesling was on the sweet side, exactly as advertised. 

Our first starter, a plate of broiled oysters comprised six of the mollusks, lightly cheesed and subtly garlicked, a bit of the brine puddled underneath. The Gem Heart salad was a good size, its dressing of yogurt and sunflower seeds worked well.

There were three of us, so we shared a duck lasagna and the cote de boeuf for two as our main course. The waiter brought the duck lasagna before the steak, as a sort of mid-course. It was cut into four portions, so a piece went home. This is basically your nonna's lasagna with duck ragu substituted for the sauce bolognese. I was kind of hoping for something a bit earthier and mushroomy - duck with cepes and balsamella maybe.  I washed down the lasagna with a very fine, austere glass of Gruner Veltliner. 

The cote de boeuf for two was ample for three after the duck lasagna. It arrived artfully sliced and staged on the plate. The temperature was perfect, and it somehow remained warm as we ate it. The Parisian potatoes that accompanied the steak were not the expected pommes allumettes, but crispy little balls from the small end of a melon scoop. Could have used a few more. The whole thing was lightly dotted with salsa verde, which did good things to the meat and potatoes. Beef this good doesn't need a chimichurri, but the salsa verde was a more subtle stand-in. I thought this dish was spendier than it needed to be at $140, but I see that Minetta Tavern is now charging $145 for their version- but MT includes marrow bones.

To offset the richness of the beef, we went with vegetable sides, a light garlic spinach and minted fresh peas, but the mint taste was lacking. 

I accompanied the beef with glasses of the Nebbiolo and Garnacha/Syrah. Both were excellent.

For dessert  we enjoyed the "donuts and coffee" - four munchkin sized mini donuts with a coffee flavored pot de creme, but the rave reviews are for the "brookies and cream" four nutty fudge warm cookies, we substituted salt caramel ice cream for the listed vanilla.

Along with the dessert we were presented with small balls of frozen chocolate, another bit of generosity. By this point in the meal, the small portion was perfect.

Service was very good - but not clarivoyant. 

It's all good, but a bit pricey for a place that eschews tablecloths.

Great place for a special occasion! My husband and I went here for my birthday and everything was impressive from start to finish. We started with the waygu meatballs and shrimp scamp appetizers which were both generous in size and delicious in taste! We then split the duck lasagna (which is enough for 3) and the filet mignon au poivre. Dessert wasn't necessary but when we saw the doughnut and coffee pudding dish on the menu, we couldn't resist! Drinks were refreshing, including the moscato I had ordered with dessert. I'd definitely go back!

This. Place. Is. AMAZING!!

I showed up at Bowery Meat Co. around 6:30 on a Wednesday with no reservation. Asked how the wait would be around 7:30. They took my name and said if they couldn't put us in the main dining room, they would put us in the lounge, which is just as nice from what I could see. Got back at 7:40, got seated right in the main dining hall. Yay!!

This place has a great atmosphere. Lots of good looking people coming after work for dinner and cocktails. Loud, but not too loud; close to the table next to you, but not too close.

I came here for the "award winning hamburger" ($22) so the "award winning hamburger" is what I got! It was just as delicious as I anticipated. The bread was perfectly toasted, the burger was cooked just how I like it. It comes with fries and some pickles. The fries were AMAZING!!! We also tried the mashed potatoes which were good, but VERY buttery and not as delicious as the fries. So. much. food. We couldn't finish it all.

The chef sent over two different small plates before we even ordered apps. Both delicious! I tried the broiled oysters (best I've ever had) along with the meatballs (again, delicious...slightly rare and melted in my mouth). Also got a bottle of wine that the sommelier helped us pick out, which ended up being fantastic.

Overall just a really great experience at Bowery Meat Co. I will be back to try their steaks!
Nailed it! What a treat. I will be returning myself one day to devour that foie terrine with onion jam the color of wild peony flowers. The wine som is an ace. Will be returning soon!

Definitely a contender for the best burger in NYC!! My party shared burgers as an appetizer because we ordered the 38oz tomahawk ribeye steak and chateaubriand. We only had a quarter each to my great regret because it made the steaks pale in comparison. Must go back for a whole burger!! The tomahawk is impressive as well but the chateaubriand was the weakest of the three. Filet mignon is a boring flavorless cut. Go for the tomahawk but save room for dessert! The s'mores sundae was delish and the little donuts with the cup of coffee pudding. Excellent service, decor and cocktails!!

For our mains, my bitch-ass friends wanted to share two entrees rather than three.  Whatever. We ordered the Bowery Steak, which is the first time I have ever seen anything like it on a menu. It's essentially a pinwheel-wrapped fat cap from a rib eye, fashioned into a circle/spiral that's roughly 10oz, if I had to guess, trussed, and cooked like a proper cut of steak. They serve it on top of creamy whipped potatoes, and top it with a chimichurri-like salsa verde.

The owner, John, explained to me how the dish was conceptualized one night when coming home from a wedding that he and Josh had attended. They prepped that night, and the next day they brought it to life. Bravo, gents. You've made me very happy. This steak was fantastic, unique, innovative, tasty and perfectly cooked. Medium rare inside with a nice crust on the edges. Mmm.

We also tried the cheeseburger. This baby has been gaining some serious notoriety in burger circles, so I was excited to try it. It comes topped with griddled onions, raclette cheese and tomato aioli.

Unfortunately, splitting it three ways left me wanting more, much more. It's tough to make a solid review off just a bite or two. I did notice, though, that it was a bit salty, and could certainly have benefited from a cool, crunch element like lettuce. Here's my pathetically small third of a burger. Thanks boys... Next time I'm ordering my own.

The burger also came with fries, and a little tray of pickled tomato, okra and cucumber. The fries were really nice. Beautiful golden brown, crispy, herby and flavorful. I suppose we should have topped the burger with some of the pickles to get that needed crunch element, but digging into them on the side was nice too.

Find your way to my page for pics and a more thorough review of all the food we tried.

IN SHORT: A steakhouse for Generation Y that is serious on flavor, high in energy, and no stranger to creativity.

THE STORY: Branded as a "meat-centric" restaurant by restauranteur John McDonald and chef-partner Josh Capon of Lure Fishbar, El Toro Blanco, and Burger & Barrel, Bowery Meat Company is really like the old, traditional steakhouse's fun and frisky little sister. She's young, hot, and a little crazy, but she knows what it means to play with the big boys, and Bowery Meat Company is certainly keeping pace with the more storied steakhouses around the city, but not without a little bit of fun.

In this chic, dark space, one can still find seven different cuts of beef, a burger, and plenty of potatoes and greens for appropriately high-end price tags, but there is also a Duck Lasagna for two, a Chinese BBQ Pork Belly appetizer, and some Zucchini Carpaccio with feta and mint that all challenge the notions of what can fit into a steakhouse menu. Indeed, while the eponymous Bowery Steak, a cut from the famed butcher Pat LaFrieda, may share such a classic heritage with other legendary cuts of meat at older, famed steakhouses, it is decidedly new. The trimmed rib-eye cap here is topped with an almost upsettingly acidic chopped salsa verde and sits on a bed of creamy whipped potatoes, becoming simultaneously familiar and exciting to its consumers, even if the raw herbs occasionally overwhelm the perfectly pink meat.

Another fresh creation on the menu are the Wagyu Meatballs, resting on soft polenta and a light tomato pan gravy sauce with plenty of parmesan. Because the fats in wagyu beef melt at a lower temperature than any other animal fat, the meatballs are delicate and tender, the liquid fat having added a rich, juicy flavor with no detectable grease. The result is a recognizable piece of meat of premium quality in a young, accessible, and somehow acceptably gauche form.

Indeed Bowery Meat Company has done well transforming its menu to its kind, meaning that a table full of 20-something women in stilettos will all be ordering the Bone-In Filet Mignon, providing them with 14 ounces of light, peppery drama, even if no one finishes it. The real question is if the restaurant, which seems to cater so well to the youngest working and monied generation of the city, can evolve as its clientele ages. Will we still want to hang around the wild little sister when we're 40? Or will this affect of cute, but psycho, but cute wear thin by then, leaving room for another steakhouse to come in and reinvent its culture?

Whatever the answer may be, for now Bowery Meat Company, with its fresh, "meat-centric" menu, is ours.

Ate here 6/21/15. I am a Josh Capon sucker, having eaten at all his restaurants. While Danny Meyer makes all of his diners feel like kings, Capon has mastered the ability to make all diners comfortable, no matter the milieu. I've had quite a few meals at Lure where I never felt weird gawking at a table of UES trophy wives passive aggressively eating AT each other.

Also, weirdly, BMCo's layout is like a mirror image of the restaurant next door, L'Apicio, which by the way is a great place to go for polenta, the dish least likely to give you first date gas.

The cocktails are fair, though my martini came with a lemon instead of the expressly demanded olives. The wine list is very appropriate, and lots of good affordable choices. We went with a nice beaujolais, because I'm good with red wine and meat, but would rather the red wine not taste heavier than the meat, thanks Burgundy.

Kumamoto oysters - who doesn't like kumamoto? Get them "dressed" with the wasabi leaf, because it is a very light seasoning that just slightly adds to the oyster.

Bowery Steak - why, it's another "proprietary" cut of meat for a new steakhouse! Pat La Frieda must make his cows do burpees or something to grow all these weird new muscles that didn't exist before. Anyway, it was perfectly cooked, though it doesn't have the integrity of other cuts, so it kind of cuts into three separate pieces. I liked the chimichurri-like topping, even if Pete Wells bitched about it.

Duck Lasagna - oddly, this is the best thing we ate at this steakhouse. It's huge, so order it for the table, and have at least 4 hungry people. Highly cheesy, tons of succulent duck, crispy at the edges, noodly in the middle. 

Burger - it's Josh Capon - you know the burger is going to be good. A little less metallic and funky than other aged burgers, with a nice choice of raclette cheese and a very soft bun, which I prefer. Good for aged meat burger beginners.

Hash Brown - a little small, and much less chivey than I'd expect given it's a sour cream and chive hash brown, but actually rather delightful, if you like your browns very crispy. I'd order it again.

French Fries - GEEZ this is a lot of french fries. Have some respect for yourself and don't eat all of them. But they are the triple cooked style, and crispy and good with the burger, but unneccesary if you order anything other than the burger and want a potato side.

Smores Sundae - insanely sweet, very smorsey. I'm not a dessert person, but I can see sweets people having uncontrollable orgasms over this.

Chocolate cake - skip. The pudding is kind of grainy, and it seems pre-prepared. Possibly the only loser in the whole meal.

Capon's joints make you feel comfortable in a high end setting (I wore my finest purple converse and plaid shirt) with reasonable prices. Really, you can't lose at any of his places, and BMCo is the same.

Whatta meal! We shared the chateaubriand for two. Luscious rich decadence. The little buttery balls of potato with the shallot snap peas on the side were heaven. Would definitely go back. These guys have the meat all figured out, none better. Dessert of "coffee" (a mocha mousse) and donuts was also pure pleasure. 
Don't miss it for a great meal out, and a fun bar scene too.

Big fan of Burger and Barrel so decided to ck out BMC.  The restaurant's decor is dark but modern so its not your old school steakhouse on the inside.  Service was excellent so would give it 4 stars there.  However, while the food was good it wasn't spectacular and for the price I would like it to be spectacular.  So, if you are on a date with another carnivore BMC is the place for you, but you crave some great steak there are several options in the city that are better for less money.

Went to Bowery Meat Company with family.  Nice place. Great wait staff and my glass of water was always full. Big deal to me. The chicken was great as were the salads that my wife and daughter ordered. I was a bit surprised by the price of the house cab. $25....my two drinks were more than my meal. i must admit though....it was pretty good wine. They also came out with a lot of little fun items from the chef...pre dinner and post. Nice touch.
