We had a great dinner - the steaks were great and service was as good as anyplace in NYC. Very good and diverse wine list. Good bar area as well as outdoor space make this a must visit.

The food here is good, especially the meat, but a bit overpriced.

For appetizers, we had foie gras and raw sea scallops. Foie gras was pleasantly lighter than most preparations of this dish and worked well with the cranberry jam and toasted and buttered bread. The sea scallops were so so, not much flavor. 

NY Steak Strips was incredible. The duck lasagna was a little bit too rich. Duck meat already has a strong flavor and the combination of the cheeses made the dish way too intense for my liking.

The PB&J mousse dessert was the only unique dessert item on the menu, but turned out to be excellent. It's a peanut butter flavored mousse slice with jelly on the inside served with vanilla ice cream.

We also ordered two wine bottles for ~$60-70 each. Way overpriced.

If you're looking for good value, I wouldn't recommend this place. However, if you're looking for high quality steak, this place delivers in that regard.

Good food, tender meat, tried NY stripe and carrots and hash side which was so good! their pork belly was excellent too, with lettuce wrap. One thing, they should have their AC higher, at times it was a bit warm.

This was an incredible experience! Everything we tried was amazingly delicious. I would suggest foie gras and pâté, the duck lasagna was to die for and the farro risotto side was tasty along with a perfectly medium rare ribeye. Overall a great dinner. Chef Paul DiBari did an amazing job. The next time we are in NYC we will definitely come here again.

Yeeeeaaahhhh...so you gotta get the duck lasagna.  It's melt in your mouth amazing.  Huge portion - we took home about half of it.  So rich and delicious!  Really nice touch with the complimentary arancini, salami and bonbons.  Delicious steak tartare as well.  The ambiance is a little too trendy/business lunch-ish for my taste, but the food is worth coming back for.

I finally made the stop at Bowery Meat Company, as a part of my Ron Swanson series, a bi-monthly ritual I invented last year. Basically, it's an excuse to go out with my friends and eat quality steaks and drink spirituous beverages (mostly whiskey) at the many famed (or trendy) steakhouses of New York City. I'm a fan of Burger and Barrel in SoHo, so I wanted to see what else Josh Capon's restaurants had to offer. In this case, a good friend of mine was taking me out for a belated birthday celebration, so she deferred all of the dish choices to me. I was more than happy to oblige. 

The restaurant has a look of a modern day steakhouse, with a full bar near the entrance. They do have a happy hour menu, but it only applies to the bar and lounge, and not the main dining area, so make sure to keep that in mind. The clientele looks to be mostly middle-aged businessmen, and yuppies celebrating birthday parties, not unlike many other steakhouses in the area.

We went with broiled oysters to start, the duck lasagna for two, the shishito ribeye (14 oz), and a side of the mushroom fricassee (basically a mix of various types of sautéed mushrooms). After we got our drinks, they came out with sort of an amuse bouche of basil pesto arancini (about the size of a gumball), bacon rosemary focaccia, and small slices of what looked like soppressata. Very delicious. The broiled Blue Point oysters were very meaty, rich, and full of crispy, buttery bread crumbs and parmesan. For our "second course", the duck lasagna for two came out in a very deep casserole dish, and the portion could easily feed 4. DUUUDE. Easily one of the best lasagnas I've ever had. It was bursting with rich duck meat, and had a full layer of crispy cheese and shredded parmesan on top, which gave the lasagna a number of different rich textures. We ate about two thirds of the lasagna before opting to box it up, and moving onto the "third course", which was the ribeye steak. The ribeye was topped with blistered shishito peppers, which gave the steak a good Southwestern flair. It should be worth noting that the ribeye wasn't dry-aged, but still very delicious, and cooked to a beautiful medium rare. The mushroom fricassee was delicious, and it included hen of the woods mushrooms, which are my favorite mushrooms.

The service was very attentive and gracious, and our waiter made a lot of good recommendations. Every dish came out at the right time and the drink refills were on point.  Prices were pretty much on par with most steakhouses, but it should be worth noting again that if you're someone who has to have their steak dry-aged, then you might want to go elsewhere for a better selection of dry-aged meats. That being said, as a steakhouse, Bowery Meat Company more than holds its own with its selection of steaks, as well as their pastas and other dish offerings. I've been told that they have a killer dry-aged burger, which is on special on Sundays for $12 at the bar/lounge, so I'll definitely be back soon to try that.

At one point - Bowery Meat Company was my favorite steakhouse (they don't like to be called a steakhouse) in the city. I love Mastro's because it reminds me of home. But Bowery really hit it out of the park when I first started going there the beginning of this year. Since then I've been back almost every 3 weeks and enjoyed the meal less and less. I can't say going there roughly 8 times now that one bad experience should warrant such a low rating of 2 stars but I think last night's dinner on the 21st really made me think wow this place just went downhill or I've been having some bad luck.

On the 21st of July - we had a reservation for 2 people at 6PM - early dinner and I called a few minutes before if they can accommodate another 2 people. We are big eaters so we definitely wouldn't have a cheap bill. The lady on the phone said don't worry (not sure if its because I'm listed as a frequent customer on their computers) but I was fortunate enough to get us a table for 4 on the very last minute but we were sitting in the lounge/bar area of the restaurant. (first time ever dining there) We had only one waitress to cover more than 30 guests probably in that area. So obviously the service would be slow and the attention to detail would be very low quality. Fine! I definitely get it - we came in with an extra two people for dinner and I understand it won't be the best.

We started off with our favorite meatballs and broiled oysters and pork belly. We tried the scampi for my friend and we weren't a fan compared to the other 3 items above. We got the east coast oysters and they were wonderful. We prefer the naked but they do have a nice topping on the oysters to make it even more refreshing but cuts down on the natural flavor we thought.

Main courses came out with our steaks and this is where I personally went downhill. When I first had my tomahawk here - it was big and really satisfied both of us even though we had another steak to share. So 3 steaks for 2 was a nice touch. A couple more visits and we noticed that we went from 3 steaks turned into 4 for 2. We don't believe our appetites have grown but that the portions have shrunk. We didn't realize how bad it was until our last visit where I had a tomahawk all by myself. WHAT? What happened? When it came out - I was like - why does this looks so small? Plus I asked for medium rare - it was crisply cooked. Of course the waitress was no where to be seen since she was so busy with the rest of her tables and bar stool tables. So the outer piece of pretty thin cut were burned to a crisp. The inner parts were great - still thinly cut - only about 6 pieces - pretty thin - usually they're thick and big...not so this time around. So I'm waiting - hoping the waitress can come by - and I can say "I don't want to be a pain but don't you think this is kinda small" --- but she never came by to ask how's your meat cooked or how is your steak? nada - now I know she's busy and I'm sure they can do is hire another waitress for quality control check - but no manager walked by and asked even if we liked our meal at the end. Which we've experienced in the past - so does it mean the lounge / bar seating area is a bad area to eat - take notice diners!

So overall - I came out eating all of my tomahawk for 2 - which was not cooked well or prepared well - and was missing at least half of the order as I came out hungry. I actually went home to find food in the fridge. Should not be the case when your tab is over $300 per person after wine and drinks. We ordered a nice montrachet - not saying it was an overly expensive bottle but a decent one where the sommelier should have walked over and introduced himself and said something about our order. None whatsoever...sad to say - are we not spending enough money in this place?...could they now expect a check for $400 to $500 a person?

The waitress did come around and noticed our unhappy faces after our meal. The other 3 guys loved their food - one was semi ok burger - the other was a bone filet and the other was a pork rib eye. The 2 out of 4 enjoyed the meal minus mine which was just awful. The waitress said she'll talk to the manager to see what she could do...she ended up giving us a dessert wine for free - nice touch I guess at the end but still wish it was better service and better food for me.

This is me venting and wish my new go to steak wouldn't lose its luster and unfortunately its starting too...time to find another steakhouse as they don't like to be called one...

Having really enjoyed a previous meal at Bowery Meat Co. (the Bowery Steak is amazing!), I decided to stop in for a quicker and more casual meal in the Bar area. I ordered the burger medium rare and had high expectations.

Sadly, the burger came out totally well done (not pink even at the very center of the patty). Its a shame to ruin a burger with so much potential. The burger had great dry-aged flavor, and was well complimented by the caramelized onions, raclette cheese and a huge portion of perfectly cooked fries. It would have been a 5 star meal, if it were not overcooked. I don't think $22 is too much for an excellent burger (which can rival a great steak in my book), but it is certainly too much for a well-done one. 

The restaurant did the right thing and immediately acknowledged the mistake, comped the burger and apologized genuinely. That is worth a lot in my book, and for that reason, I am sure I will be back to give them another shot.
In short it is my favorite steak house!!! We came here for dinner on a Tuesday night. Wait staff was very friendly. They have great drink menu and delicious high quality food!!!

I came here for my anniversary on the recommendation of one of my friends who was raving about how amazing his food was from here. Never have I ever been so disapointed by food and the restaurant manager in my life. 

I made reservations and mentioned it was our anniversary and requested a booth table ahead of time. The restuarant had maybe 10 guests tops and we were given major attitude by the manager on the floor when we were not happy with the table near the cash register in what was a pretty empty restaurant. At this point I was ready to leave and they wanted to just put us at the bar/lounge although there were 4 booths and an almost empty restaurant. I said no and she reluctantly gave us the booth and told us we needed to leave by 8 because that table was reserved for some ceo. 

Personally I don't care if the Pope himself was coming don't talk to me like I am less important then someone who had reservations 3 hours later than me. Then talk to my husband who was fine with anything and not ask me who was clearly upset. Really awful start to what was supposed to be a romantic night out away from the kids. 

I ordered oysters to start, these were actually really good...the only good item really. We also had Wagyu meatballs which were ok they weren't amazing as the reviews make them out to be. For dinner I ordered the dry aged ny strip. Probably the worst steak I have ever had in my life. Burnt to a crisp, completely charred on the outside. My husband had the bowery steak ordered medium rare and was burnt to a crisp as well. Tasted like mystery meat with salsa Verde dumped on top. We were famished when we arrived so we still ate it and feared the staff would probably spit in our food cutting around the burnt pieces.

We didn't want dessert at this point and just wanted to get out of there. 

This was probably one of the most dreadful experiences I have ever had at a restaurant, so poorly managed. Completely dissapointed. The waiter we had was great ...nothing else ...even the freebies sucked! If this was my restuarant I would have been mortified that any of my guests who are dropping a couple hundred dollars were treated and fed this way...

Would never recommend... run run run! The only benefit of the doubt I can give is that maybe their real chef called out sick that day 8/1 or something, and maybe this was a substitute manager. This is a huge inconsistency to my friends recommendation and the other recommendations on here. Regardless this was my true experience.

SOOOOO yummy, great service. The shrimp scampi was excellent and I LOOOOOVED the sour cream and onion hash brown side thing!! Great service and cocktails!

Not cheap!

Mediocre, won't be going back. Appetizers were good. Had the buratta and the pork belly. Waiter was absent for the evening, paying attention to a larger group. The Bowery steak was the big disappointment. Swimming in chimichuri sauce, very undercooked, lots of gristle.   Many better places to eat for the money.

Not your typical corporate steakhouse which was a nice surprise.  It seemed kind of trendy and low key, but the food packed a punch.  Perfect for something corporate, casual, or a date.

Oysters - delicious
Sea Scallops - perfectly cooked
Meatballs - delicious
Farmer's salad - nothing special
Bone in Filet - delicious but possibly slightly closer to medium than medium rare, which was requested.
Eggs and Eggs - exquisite
Hash brown - different but good
Garlic spinach -  tasty
Mushrooms - good
Corn - good
Triple chocolate cake - decadent and delicious
Donuts and coffee - very good but heavy

Food here was really good for the most part, just very expensive I thought.

What a great steak house!! A lot of men with suits! Everything on the menu looked amazing and I wish we had more capacity to try more things! They gave complimentary bread and what also seemed like risotto balls? We decided to opt out of an appetizer since we got the meat for two and didn't want to get too full. We had the Chateaubriand for two and it was the perfect amount of food. I don't eat much steak to begin with so it was just right. This also gave sides of potatoes and greens. Flavors were perfect, also good selection of wine. For dessert we had the smokes desert and that was HUGE. Definitely full after our epic meal. Would like to come back and try many of their other items.

The food here is awesome. My brother and I went for dinner and had the oysters as and appetizer which was to die for. We both got the ribeye for dinner which was cooked to perfection. I would have given five stars if they didn't charge us $5 for tea which absurd. Overall the place is pricey but the food is well worth it.

Bowery Meat Company lost me during cocktails. I ordered a very specific "call" brand vodka on the rocks that I drink 2-3 times a weeks for the last few years. It has a distinctive flavor that I enjoy. I was served a "well" vodka that I would expect to be used in pitchers of Bloody Mary's. I made a comment to my waiter and was assured I got the vodka I ordered. Giving them the benefit of the doubt I ordered a second and asked the waiter to make sure the bartender poured my brand. I am sure it was still not the vodka I ordered. 

The steak was good, not great. I had the filet minion on the bone au poivre for $57. It was prime filet cooked close to how I ordered it. I like my steak a bit more charred on the outside and medium rare inside. It was more medium but it was medium rare along the bone as expected. A bit less cooked and bit more charred and it would have been worth discussing the vodka switch with the bartender, but I'm never going back anyway. 

My wife had the "Bowery Steak" which was about the same price and was perfect for her. Very flavorful and a petite portion. She loved it. We both shared and loved the baratta appetizer and the farmer salad. The spinach with garlic was perfect too. Service was good, bartender aside. My wife really enjoyed her 2 glasses of Prosecco. We did not stay for dessert. 

If they had not screwed me on my drink i would have given them 4 stars and considered going back again, but the steak was just good. If you are a wine or beer drinker or could care less about the liquor used in the drink you order, this place is fun, the food is decent, and the service is good. If they spent $5 more on the bottle of vodka they poured my two $13 drinks from I would go back again. Our check came to $221 including tax for two entrees, two appetizers, a side vegetable and two drinks each.

A Josh Capon restaurant and a 2 star review from Pet Wells is to be taken very seriously

This place is called a steakhouse. But its menu is far more than that. You really can enjoy the menu without ever touching typical steakhouse staples.  It's located in trendy Bowery with good vibe. Menu gets kudos for originality, many interesting dishes, (which can be found online). So not your traditional high end chain steakhouse but New York local, so perfect for steak lovers and not alike. 

My main issue is with the strip which had an excessive amount of fat on it, and was a bit tough. Not a particularly welcome cut. Because this reviewer is about the beef, and loses a big star for that.

Steak price is typical New York price, but portion size is 2-4 oz. smaller

Sides are done with original flair such as a mushroom risotto based with faro instead. 

Appetizers are also very good with some such as the cauliflower steak being very creative.  

With a few pastas thrown in, the similarity to Costata's menu in some respects is striking

Do save room for desserts as they are original, yum and well worth having

Service is very professional but relaxed, with managers attending to the floor.

I LOVE this place. The first time I went there was Christmas Eve with my family and the service was wonderful, and the bone-in fillet to die for. I also went there to celebrate a promotion, and both times, I must say, the sommelier was amazing! Completely unpretentious, and recommended wonderful wines that complimented our meals exquisitely (and weren't the most expensive on the menu!). This is our new favorite restaurant for steak.

Food: 5
Service: 5
Cleanliness: 5
Atmosphere: Dressy, Dimly-lit, chic with a touch of casual 

Food was ridiculously good as well as ridiculously priced. Get ready to throw out some serious dollars if you're dining here. Four people, no booze and a starter and main course each, with one dessert = over $300, just to give you an idea... 

As far as the food goes, I amost feel guilty for giving so many other eateries five stars after dining here. If I were to keep the rating equivalent to Bowery Meat Co, only but a few places would remain five stars and the rest would immediately move to four or three. They definitely raise the bar of my new found food standards. What was the best thing ordered amongst the four of us? Everything. Not one single selection made you even remotely mad about the high priced cost. In fact, it only made it clearer to understand. The best of the best out of the best:

Grilled Swordfish with Royal Trumpet & Pistachio Pesto; This one was my personal favorite.

Skuna Bay Salmon with Summer Squash, Cherry Tomatoes & Basil Broth; The finest Salmon fillet cooked to perfection.

Market Sides: Sautéed Green Beans & (organic, non-GMO) Grilled Corn; who knew these two sides could be so flavorful?? The chefs are far beyond the standard salt, pepper and butter. So many spices smothered in a perfect array. Also be warned, if you're sensitive to spice....there are tiny chopped jalepenos mixed in with the corn kernels.

*Bone-In Filet Mignon 14oz Au Poivre (I didn't try this one, but heard it was incredible)

Shrimp Scampi was smothered in butter and garlic (as it should be...), and the shrimp were the most plumpest, healthiest shrimp I've ever had. 

The waitstaff was a delight. My water glass stayed constantly full. They were on point here... with timing and clearing and filling and waiting from start to finish. 

Would I return? 

Sure. As long as you're buying.

7PM reservation for 3 on a Saturday evening. We were seated promptly and at that time the restaurant was pretty empty but as the evening when on every table filled up.

Broiled oysters was basically like clams casino except with oysters. I'm personally not a big oyster fan but I tried one anyway and I all I could really taste was breadcrumbs, garlic, and cheese. Probably a waste for oyster lovers because there just isn't enough meat to hold up to the toppings like clams would. Not bad tasting, but not worth the price and I would have rather had another starter instead.

Foie and chicken liver pate was phenomenal. Very good portion of pate cut out on the plate with several toasted brioche points and a heaping of sweet onion marmalade. Texture was amazing, slightly cool with a nice, thin ring of fat surrounding the slice but perfectly smooth and spreadable. Flavor was fantastic, basically a very, very rich tasting chicken liver but not so overpower that I could probably eat it on it's own. Onion marmalade was great although I would have loved some capers on the side as well as another option.

Duck lasagna was good. Very generous amount of duck meat in it to justify the price and definitely very filling. Served in 4 portions, one last portion went home with my friend in a to-go bag. It's worth getting but I don't think it's nearly as great as all the hype other reviews give it. I do wish this was served AFTER the steak though because after the lasagna, we were already starting to get full (didn't help that we spent the afternoon at San Gennaro festival and then also stopped by a Nepalese restaurant for a pre-dinner dinner).

The main event, we got the tomahawk ribeye medium rare. Presliced off the bone in around half inch thick slices, the flavors were fantastic. Not sure what the rub consisted of, but it added a great flavor, crusted up very well, and didn't overpower the flavor of the meat itself. I would suggest maybe seeing if you can get a real knife to use because there was still a good amount of meat stuck on the bone that we proceeded to gnaw on Fred Flintstone style (probably much to the chagrin of the wealthy looking guy in the fancy suit and high polished suit at the table next to us with his date). Comes with a sauce (fortunately on the side) that is completely unnecessary and overpowering. The spring onions on the side were nice, lightly charred and made for a great palate cleanser between sliced of beef.

Burger and fries came out a little bit after the steak. Medium, juicy, and overall what you would expect from a burger made out of premium beef ground up and cooked to a nice medium. Honestly we probably didn't treat the burger all that fair because we were advised to eat the burger as soon as it came out and because it come out just after the ribeye we just devoured our thirds of the burger quickly to get back to the steak. There are so many good burgers coming out of NYC kitchen these days and I'm not going to pretend that I can pick out all the intricacies of them all and rank them. It was good, cooked very well, and priced similarly to other burgers like it. Fries had a nice, earthy flavor to them. Like there was potato skin flavor on all of them without the bitterness, even on the fries cut from the inside of the potato. I do wish they were meatier though, they were fried to the point where there wasn't much starchyness to them on the inside.

For sides we got the spinach and hash brown and they were probably the biggest let downs of the meal. Spinach was seasoned well but needed more garlic. Hash brown I thought was a little too thick, the onion on top should have been sauteed to a deep brown to really add flavor to the pretty bland potato. It also could have used a flavorful fat element like drippings from their roasted chickens or duck. I say skip the sides and get more starters...

For dessert we got the donuts and coffee and PB&J. the donuts and coffee has great presentation but I felt the flavors were a bit off. Donuts smelled great of cinnamon sugar but I felt they were a bit too doughy and not light enough as you chewed through them. The "coffee" in pudding form looked great but I thought needed to be a bit sweeter since the donuts were lacking. The PB&J tasted great and everything on the plate came together well but after the coffee and donuts the presentation of this was a bit boring.

Overall service was fantastic. Water was constantly refilled. Our waiter was a very pleasant, southern french gentleman who conversed with us and had no problems recommending dishes to us. We were never without a drink either; as soon as one of ours was low we were prompted asked if we wanted another. Leftovers can be boxed up as the meal progresses and were kept off the table in a marked bag with our table number that we got at the end of the meal.

I went here for my birthday dinner with my mom and my boyfriend. I did a lot of research on picking where to go for my birthday dinner and was really happy with my choice. The atmosphere was dimly lit, trendy and everyone was dressed very nicely. We got seated quickly and were greeted shortly after by our waiter who helped us pick out a bottle of red for the table. I tasted a couple and picked a great malbec for around $60 (pretty good for a bottle). 

We started with the short rib ravioli, which was the most amazing pasta I've ever had in NYC. The meat was perfectly tender and melted in my mouth. For our main course, the three of us decided to split the Chateaubriand. This 20 oz steak costs $110 but it was really worth it because it was enough meat for the three of us to split. It was the best filet I have ever had and I definitely recommend. We got a side of Fondant Potato which was good but next time I would get the mashed potatoes, as the table next to us got that and it looked much better. We finished the meal with the S'mores Sundae with consisted of toasted marshmallow ice cream, brownie bites, chocolate dipped graham crackers and hot fudge - I was so full at this point but so happy we got dessert because it was amazing! The ice cream alone was the best flavor ice cream I've ever had.

Bowery Meat Company is definitely pricy but I will definitely be back for the next special occasion.

Skip the steak and go straight for the meatballs. We wanted to love this restaurant, but with a $140 steak served cold, it fell short.
The scene was a classy one, with mostly people in their late 30s to late 50s. The restaurant was beautifully decorated! The wait staff was very attentive and did a great job servicing a busy restaurant. 
Now for the food, the appetizers were amazing, make sure to try the meatballs and shrimp scampi. The spaghetti wasn't too great, I would skip that dish. And the let down of the night was that the Code de Boeuf that was served cold. It was cooked beautifully, but was not hot. Overall, we had a fun time with the company we were with, but the main dish was a let down.
Burger was ok salad were great service good nothing bad about the place but maybe a bit overhyped

Wow this place is amazing. I came to this place because I saw it on a list for "best cheeseburgers" and had no clue what to expect. In the end I did not get the hamburger but got the Bowery steak and steak tartare which were out of this world. The steak beats out strip house and del fricos by far. Honestly I've never had something like that before. Furthermore you get a lovely rice ball at the beginning of the meal and a unique desert at the end. I would highly recommend this place to anyone who enjoys meat and cannot why the rating is not higher or why there are not more reviews on yelp. WIthout exaggeration one of the best and a gem in New York. Please go and support such top notch food.

We can't leave NYC without cutting into a real steak. Decided on this place as it was a cold evening and we are travelling with a baby. Reservation call 2 hours earlier was not accepted as they have fully committed for a Sat evening but told to walk in. So we got there and there was a table available but over at the section where the bar is located.

We only had the stomach for the steak and ordered the
T-Bone Florentine   40oz, 40-Day Dry Aged. $144.
Took about 30mins to serve. Came sliced and it waz exactly what we wanted -- medium rare. The meat is tender as it is supposed to be after 40 days of aging.  But there isn't a lot of favor from the meat. Perhaps the meat itself was lean and not much marbling. Therefore the 3 stars rating.  A similar one we had in Austin was so so much better which I'll rate a 4.5 star. The side we ordered were the creamed spinach and mushrooms. Nothing exciting about them either. Service was above average even though we didn't have any drinks or wines.

When I heard of this place I thought "oh great, another steak restaurant here to take away my money on overpriced meat". 

But when I went to Bowery Meats the service and the food were both excellent.  First I had a drink at the bar.  Bartender was friendly and handy at his job.  Great cocktail.

When we sat down, we had a large group so there was a shortened menu.  The salmon and the steak tar-tare were both delicious (the salmon being the diminuitive choice).  The tar-tare was served with crusty, grilled bread and was like having a delicious rare hamburger.  Excellent seasoning and really melts in your mouth.  The salmon sashimi was lightly dressed with some oil and not much else.  It was also excellent and I wanted more.

Then they served some small fried treats that I can't recall exactly their contents but equally good.  I wanted more of everything!

The steak came.  I had the dry-aged NY Strip and it was as tasty as any steak I've had in the city (including Luger's).  I rarely finish an entire steak but this was so good I just devoured the whole thing.  Succulent and delicious.

Sides were very good as well.  Hash-brown type potatoes very passable.

The check was no joke though.  Expect to shell out a couple benjamins per if you get some wine with dinner.
Excellent cuts of meat. Ordered three steaks - Cote de Boeuf / T-Bone florentine / Tomahawk. Tomahawk was the fav. Get the steak tartare!

This. Place. Is. Amazing.

I decided to treat myself and get the burger as well as the filet mignon. This was by far the best burger I have had in my life. The filet mignon was also cooked to perfection and filled with flavor.

The staff is kind, warm, and helpful. Water was always full and didn't feel like I was being stalked.

I will be back.

Much of what makes steakhouses annoying lives on here - a lot of "big guys" raucously eating out, flaky waiters, overpriced par-cooked steaks and scandalous wine prices.   While the menu is a bit more interesting than your typical steakhouse, it does not make up for a bunch of issues: 1) No table clothes (I get it, this place is cool - but please wipe down my table at least); 2) $57 (pre-tax, pre-tip) 14 oz. strip which was NOT on par with the big dogs; 3) $146 Porterhouse for two - roughly $30 more and again, not on par with the household names; 4) the lousiest bathrooms ever for place that gets $$$$$ for dinner; and 5) unimpressive, new construction, low-ceilinged dining room.   

Pros: sides were fairly priced and portioned, as was dessert.  The rest was an old-skool steakhouse rip-off with a new name.

I went there for dinner on a Wednesday night. My son, who can devour 25 Oz steak without breaking a sweat was excited. We ordered the 40 ounce T-bone.  He took one bite and literally gagged at the amount of salt covering this $146 entree.  The sides fared no better. Whipped potatoes and the brussel sprouts were essentially inedible. A performance this poor and this expensive should not and will not get a second chance. Arby's is a better choice.

I LOVE this restaurant.  Amazing food! All the steaks are awesome and I have tried them all, but I especially recommend the cote de beauf for 2 - easily feeds 3-4 thought.  Also make sure to get the polenta, the roasted oysters, the duck lasagna, the lobster.  Yum!  I'm getting hungry just thinking about this place.  And always fun when Chef Capon comes out and says hi to the diners.  Great fun environment!

Chef Capon knows how to do steak.  The crab claw, zucchini carpaccio, farmers salad and cauliflower steak were amazing.  But my favorite, by far, was the chateaubriand.  I also love the decor here and the service was top notch!
Triple chocolate layer cake to top it off.  I'll be going here whenever I'm in the city.
Decent at best.  Prices are too high and flavor was lacking.  Would not return especially when Minetta tavern is a 15 min walk, with better quality and similar pricing.

This is one of the best restaurants I have ever experienced. From the friendly welcome by the hostess to the smiling bartenders, my first few minutes were great. I gets better from there. Good waiter, great sommelier to help with fantastic wine selections (within budget), the people continued to excel. The food matched their top quality. Chateaubriand was perfect and delicious and anyone there should not miss the chocolate bread pudding dessert. I will be back soon!
Fantastic food and service! Waiter was very friendly. Everything was freshly prepared and the waiter was very knowledgable about the menu.

I don't eat steak too frequently, but after eating dinner here, I just might need to visit more frequently. The bar at the front is well-appointed and not overly crowded, with a small lounge space next to it and a pretty large dining room (at least by NYC standards) in the back to the left. It's a very well-appointed space despite not having an ostentatious storefront (I've walked by here many times before without noticing), and the service matches as well - very attentive, with drinks always present and wine glasses being refilled constantly.

We started with a trio of appetizers. The bitter salad was absolutely delicious - the kale makes the Caesar-style salad have a much heartier bite, and the breadcrumbs add a nice little crunch with each bite as well. The burrata was divine as well - very fresh and moist, with rich flavor and plated with balsamic that adds a nice touch of acidity without overdoing it. The pork belly was solid as well, but I think I have such a high standard for execution on pork belly (e.g. Momofuku's buns) that this seemed like a bit of a letdown, at least compared to the other appetizers. It wasn't nearly as succulent as belly I've had elsewhere, but I did appreciate serving it with lettuce wraps - a nice touch given the heaviness of the main course. I went with the namesake steak, and wow - no idea what cut the steak comes from (the menu description is pretty light), but it definitely seems to be aged a little bit, and it was done absolutely perfect for medium - no redness but still plenty of juiciness and succulence with each bite. The 'salsa verde' on top is really more of a chimichurri that lightly adds a hint of zest without being overbearing, and the small layer of mashed/whipped potatoes under the steak are a perfect complement; they soak up the juices of the steak, and they aren't too heavy, either. We finished off the meal with freshly-baked cinnamon donut bites (basically Munchkins, but way better)...airy yet full of sugary deliciousness without being overly fried.

What a meal! I cannot wait to come back and try out some of the other dishes, along with their acclaimed burgers. Great food, great drinks (very extensive wine selection, along with a nice selection of cocktails and craft beers - they were out of a few, which is probably the only negative thing I can say), and overall a fabulous experience.

Pro: The meat
Cons: Service, Prices, Noise level

The meal got off to a bad start. We had an early reservation, and while the dining room was half-full the hostess tried to seat us in the bar area which had a happy hour going on. Got moved to a table in a cramped part of the main dining room instead. 

The dining room slash hangar - it's huge! - was extremely noisy. I was having trouble hearing  my wife. It's a young and fun crowd at BMC, but it reminded me more of a night club than an ambitious restaurant. The waiter had to lean in so close I could smell his breath.  

Service was poor/sloppy. The busser served amouse-bouche twice: both before and after our appz. Clearly a mishap. It took close to ten minutes to get a fresh napkin when I dropped it on the floor. Coat girl didn't say goodbye - little things throughout the meal. I wouldn't normally mind at a diner, but a place where you're paying top dollar it's a bigger deal.

Prices are high. Oysters: $4.5 a piece. Sides to your steak: $12. A glass of Barolo: $23. An espresso: $6

We had the dry aged t-bone for two - it was spectacular. One of the best steaks I've had in NYC.

The bill came to $410 incl. tax & tip for 2 drinks, 8 oysters, 1 t-bone, spinach & 'srooms, 1 dessert, 2 glasses of red, 2 espressos and 1 digestif.

If you're looking for a modern, cool steakhouse, I'd head to M. Well's in LIC. For a fun night out, Minetta's Tavern. For the real deal, Keens or Lugers. But probably not Bowery Meat Co.

Food- Excellent
Service-Excellent
Decor/Music- I see what they're trying to do...

Went with a group of 7, ordered pretty much everything on the menu. Standouts would be- Meatballs, Duck Lasagna, Veal Chop, Tomahawk Ribeye- love the fact that this place is not afraid of seasoning.

This restaurant was a HUGE surprise. The menu looked good and but the dinner ended up being FANTASTIC. The Oysters were full of flavor and very fresh. We had a group of 5 so we split two of the big steaks. The Tomahawk rib eye wasn't just good but seriously incredible. One of my new top 5 favorite steaks. The s'mores dessert was creative and tasty.

Staff was great and I highly recommend trying this restaurant.

Knowing how hard a restaurant and a staff works, I feel bad giving Bowery Meat only 2 stars, but it just wasn't my kind of place.  It was very loud, the service was slow, and the food was highly over salted.  I think I have a high tolerance to salt, but I couldn't even eat the hash browns, because they were so salty.  And they were overcooked as well. The creamed spinach and lamb chops were also over salted.

The wine sommelier was friendly and helpful as he decanted the wines that we brought. That was the high point of the evening.  The little gem salad was very tasty.

If the place wasn't so loud, and the corkage was less than $35 per bottle, I would give them another try. But, I don't think that is going to happen.

BMC is very good for several reasons; including--but not limited to--service, steak, and sleekness. "Modern Steakhouse" seems like an oxymoron, but I'm not sure how else to describe it because in the darkness of the angular dining room, you'll find excellent steak being sliced and slotted into good-looking, young faces. 

Drinks at the bar while our table was prepared; vodka martini and a bourbon specialty drink were perfectly made; Hats off to the bar tender. 

The amuse bouches were excellent (salami and focaccia, fried risotto balls--you'll notice several Italian leanings here) were a nice touch considering how much you'll $pend. 

Foie Gras & Chicken Liver Parfait with onion jam on a lightly toasted brioche ($21) was, as obvious people say, a revelation. But, really. Spreading some of that rock salt-topped creaminess along with the sweet onion jam is the perfect way to start. The sommelier convinced us to split a $29 glass of Suduiraut, which is a dessert wine, as it "paired perfectly." We were skeptical but feeling audacious as we were celebrating a birthday, so we splurged. Looking back, we can't imagine NOT getting a glass. Just go for it.

The Tomahawk Ribeye (40oz) with grilled onions and Romesco sauce ($142) was EXCELLENT. Ordered medium-rare (and served perfectly), the crispy sear was just right. The onions it came with were just OK, but the Romesco sauce was very tasty...not that you'd need it on this perfect steak. Really, it was so freakin soft. 

We ordered the mushroom fricasse and Spanish potatoes as sides and this is probably what keeps me from giving BMC 5 stars. Sides were small, average tasting, and played second (maybe even third) fiddle to everything else. 

They thanked us for celebrating a birthday with BMC (and trusting their sommelier's recommendation) by bringing us the s'more sundae. The toasted marshmallows, brownies, and chocolate covered graham crackers were deliciously drenched in hot fudge and--wait for it--a "modern" take on the traditional campsite treat, but the real star is the ice-cream which somehow tastes like a campfire (in all the right ways).

Would definitely return and try one of the other steaks for two...but I would also be 100% on board with getting that wonderfully marbled tomahawk again. Service was helpful and lovely; I'm even counting the comedic Chef Capone who came by to display the different cuts earlier in the night.

The Steak is better than Peter Luger, Old Homestead and many of the best places.  The Côte de Beauf was simply marvelous..   Good enough for two hungry people.  One side dish and your set!  AWSOME experience!

Came here for a friend's birthday.  Overall good but prefer the T-bone Florentine steak, simple seasoning brings out yhr best of the meat.  Not so much of a meat person but I enjoy it same.

We also ordered a few appetizers, the zucchini carpaccio, salmon sashimi, broiled oyster, brussel sprouts and crispy hash.  Also came with a few complimentary sides. 

 Would definitely go for their happy hour.

Found this awesome restaurant when looking for a spot that was open on Christmas eve.
  We looked at the menu and the prices and thought it was perfect!
When we got there, we new we made the right choice!
GREAT FOOD!  GREAT SERVICE!
Truly a perfect night out at this restaurant!

My brother and I find it challenging to take our mother to a restaurant that will satisfy all of us, but Bowery Meat Company, you did it. The duck lasagna and ribeye were the highlights for me and not to be missed. The wagyu meatballs were skippable (a bit too salty and too much parsley for my taste). The space is modern and impressive but not so trendy that your parents would feel out of place. The noise level was actually pretty respectable for a Saturday night. The service was good, although we felt that as soon as it was apparent that we weren't ordering wine, our waiter sped up the service A LOT. 

Despite the last part, I highly recommend a date/ladies' night out/small group gathering at BMC and would not mind making a repeat visit here.

From the ambiance to the flavors and staff, this place was top notch! What an incredible dinner! Bread and arincini pesto to start, burrata, cauliflower steak with pine nuts and Dijon, flavorful wagu meat balls over gifts in marinara, succulent duck lasagna,  and crispy polenta with mushrooms!! Pumpkin ravioli with white lemon bechemel and creamed spinach that held its own in weight and flavor! Hello new favorite spot! Xoxo

Wow, where do I even begin? Bowery Meat Company  = flawless! 

From start to finish, everything here is top notch. The service, the food, the experience. The interior is beautiful, modern and open. 

When we were seated just past 7 for our reservation, the restaurant was pretty quiet for a Thursday evening, but by 8 o'clock I don't think there was an empty seat in the house! Our waiter began by bringing over quite the display of cuts of meat! Detailed descriptions for each were amazing to hear and see and I've never seen anything quite like it! Though interesting, we had come here for the "famous" burger, for our burger club night! 

Bowery Meat Company has excellent customer service. They began by sending over the wine sommelier, which was really cool, as their wine list is quite large. Although we didn't end up going with his recommendation due to our price point, I can appreciate how he belongs and is much needed there. Afterwards while we perused the menu, we were given rosemary bread with a cured meat, along with 3 pesto arancini balls. YUM! 

We ended up ordering 2 of the cheeseburgers to share between 3 of us, a side of crispy Brussel sprouts, & the burrata to start. We ordered the burgers medium rare & medium just to differentiate. The waiter graciously asked if the kitchen could cut them into thirds for us! (How generous!) Yes, yes please! 

The burrata was delicious, creamy and beautifully presented. I always prefer it with a good ripe tomato, as opposed to the eggplant they served it with, but I understand it wasn't tomato season! (The waiter said some menu items do change from time to time.) The cheeseburger: the meat was melt in your mouth delicious and smooth, and the medium rare was the clear winner, it was juicy and flavorful. They came with a MOUND of perfectly cooked French fries, and it also came with a side of pickled items: pickles, okra, green tomatoes. The Brussel sprouts were cooked to perfection with a nice crisp, but not overly done. 

While finishing our wine, we opted to order a dessert my friend had read about: the s'mores sundae. Oh my god. This could've been the most beautifully presented desert I've ever seen. (See photo!) The marshmallow was toasted perfectly, it had little brownie bites, and chocolate dipped graham crackers over ice cream. To top it off the waiter who dropped it off doused it in chocolate fudge sauce. Drool. 

Top it all off with a complimentary caramel chocolate bite, and boom, might be my best overall dining experience in the city. Can't wait to come back and bring others!
Great food in nice ambiance. Duck lasagna is my favorite, fish and steak are really good too.

Opentable res for 6 pm and by 7 the place was filled up!  The hostess greets you and takes your coat.  Booths are curved and comfy for 4. 

Complimentary bacon and rosemary focaccia bread and pesto arancini to start.  Foie gras and chicken liver parfait is creamy smooth served with toasted bread and delicious topped with onion jam. Broiled oysters were just as good (maybe even better than) the ones in NoLA?!  The guys enjoyed their raw oysters. 

Duck lasagna is perfect as a mid course, not too heavy or light, but cheesy, savory, creamy, crispy, meaty all at once!!  I'll prob never eat another lasagna again. 

Now for the steaks-friend and hubby enjoyed their filet topped with truffles. Another friend and I shared the tomahawk ribeye for two which was cooked a perfect medium rare.  Hash brown was delish and perfect for 4 to share. 

Smores dessert is all that-toasted marshmallow ice cream, brownie bites, chocolate covered graham, toasted marshmallows, hot fudge-delish!!!

Overall, meat is high quality as is the food!  4 out of 5 as a steak house but, 5 out of 5 as an NYC restaurant.  Service was attentive-water always filled, dishes taken away just as soon as food was devoured, repeat drinks were offered, etc.

Great Meal and experience until I received the wine bill.  The menu is misleading and I ended up with a $275.00 bottle of wine that I couldn't afford. 

This is a tough review as the meal was jus amazing .  The duck lasagna was remarkable.   Again great food but a confusing wine menu.

Just went this past Friday a great experience overall. Our reservation was at 9:30pm, and we were seated by 10pm. The ambiance was phenomenal, and the restaurant wasn't too loud. 
We ordered the famous duck lasagna, a NY hanger steak and side whipped potatoes. 

The lasagna was AMAZING! The steak was really lean, and little overcooked, thankfully the potatoes was bomb and made the overall meal worth it. 

I'd recommend this place for a bday dinner, anniversary or major occasion!

We went her here for a night on the town and were first annoyed because our reservation was at 6 and we were not sat until 7.   Once we got in we ordered their famous lasagna which was delicious and steak.  The steak was decent but not my favorite compared to some other well known haunts such as Roots.  
Overall a satisfactory but not amazing experience.

The food was excellent. Definitely one of my favorite New York steakhouses. The bone marrow appetizer was especially tasty. All the steaks we had were great, but I especially liked their "special" steak. Try it for sure!

Delicious place!! Came here to celebrate a birthday, great choice! From the starters we had the Burrata, Wagyu Meatballs, steak tartare, and the Chinese BBQ Pork Belly! Each app was better than the next!! The only thing I would change is the scallions in the tartare. They were a little overpowering, however it was all great. We then went on to the entrees. The Grilled Ribeye was the most popular at our table (shishito peppers gave the perfect balance). However, their special gnocchi was also so good. The drinks were also a huge hit: The Botanist and another one, can't remember the name but it had St. Germaine, both so good!! Finally, we ordered a toasted coconut cake for the birthday boy, huge hit!! Would definitely return!

I came here thanks to some great reviews of this place. While this place is expensive, the steak is absolutely worth it. They start off showing a platter of a selection of meats, everything ranging from a giant 2 person Tomahawk Ribeye, to a small unique steak called the Bowery Steak. The Bowery Steak is a unique creation of theirs made from the edge of wagyu beef  (the sides are most marbled) and then rolled up to make a slab of steak. I opted for this because I can get a Ribeye other places, but this seemed to be something I HAD to get. It comes with salsa Verde but I opted to get a different sauce on the side. In the end I realized I didn't even need ANY sauce as this was absolutely INCREDIBLE. Unlike most steaks where the most flavor is the edges, due to the nature of this steak, every bite was as good as the first and exploding with flavor. Yes, this steak is smaller than others, but that didn't make a difference. I was very satisfied at the end. I also had a bite of other people's filet mignon as well as the cote de boeuf (for 2). Both of those were also incredibly good but I still prefer the bowery steak. You couldn't go wrong with any of those choices. 

Now that I got my favorite part down, the apps were also great. We got the broiled oysters which were delicious as well as the meatballs. The zucchini carpaccio wasn't anything special so I wouldn't recommend it unless you really want it. 

In the end the chef came out to our table without being asked and it was great to be able to compliment him. Just a small extra touch that I appreciated. 

I heard the burger here was one of the best ever so I need to return for that!

If you're looking for a steakhouse with a modern twist, Bowery Meat Company is the answer. With steaks just as good as old style and classic steakhouses, but with a interesting/fusion like menu of starters it's hard to choose what you want to order. We started with the burrata which was delicious. In terms of steaks we went with the pepper rubbed ribeye and the bone in-filet. While they were both incredible, the bone in-filet was covered in a sauce which I had never tasted and fell in love with. The side of potatoes we ordered which was covered in a spicy sauce was a nice addition as well, although we probably could have done without them. For dessert, the s'mores sundae is a must. BMC is the perfect place to celebrate an occasion and I will definitely be returning!

The food was great but I felt rushed by the server and bussers. Refills on soda and ice tea are $4 each but the server didn't tell us. They use a tiny Collins glass so you need at least 5 glasses to equal one regular glass. We spent $70 on Pepsi and ice tea separate of our mixed drinks. Service was good but rushed. Don't go if you're trying to relax. Just being honest.

I live in the building above this restaurant and i have been a big fan since this place opened. The ambiance is great, amazing cocktail menu and very good whisky/rye selection. But, mot importantly, the dry aged steak is spectacular. Highly recommend it.

I came here with some friends after many good recommendations from others. We were not disappointed. The service was excellent, right from the beginning at the hostess. Everyone was pleasant, professional and polite. We ordered the meatballs and the pork belly for apps. Both were delicious and I would order them again. A few of us had the hanger steak and the burger. The hanger steak was ok. I was a little disappointed and I wished I had ordered the filet. I didn't think I could eat the filet, it looked to big but I should have. The stars of our meals however was the whipped potatoes and the creamed spinach. Both were delicious and decedent. We topped off the meal with the Smores Sundae which was really spectacular. 

The scene is trendier than I expected and it is a little expensive. But we enjoyed our meal and experience and I would suggest trying it out. It is a very New York establishment.

Really good beers/wines and very good steak. This is not your traditional steakhouse but it offers a more modern take on steakhouse.
Really nice vibe and a good spot for a different steak experience.

4.5 stars but I am rounding up to 5. As expected, the meat dishes we got here were delicious.  We started with the meatballs and pork belly, with both had a great flavor, then each ordered the super meaty cheeseburger.  

The cheeseburger was delicious.  The thick, juicy patty had a great beefy flavor and the soft bun held up well to the juices.  I loved that it came with a huge mountain of fries, served with ketchup and super fluffy mayonnaise, as well as a small side bowl of various types of pickles.  The only room for improvement is the size of the bun relative to the patty.  While the thickness was good, the bun was too wide for the patty, leaving lots of extra bread.

More like 3.5 stars. A trendier steakhouse in the city with a younger vibe. Had a reservation for 8:00pm but our table must not have been ready yet as we were directed to the bar first.

Broiled Oysters - Very yummy. The toppings didn't overpower the taste of the oysters at all and it was very obvious how fresh the oysters were. Made me wish I had ordered some raw oysters as well.

Foie Gras & Chicken Liver Parfait - Decadent and creamy liver dish. Don't think I'd be ordering this again as it was slightly too sweet.

Hand-cut Steak Tartare - Bigger cubes of steak rather than the usual almost minced steak. Wasn't flavorful enough.

Grilled Ribeye - Was cooked to the proper medium rare and flavor was good.

Creamed Spinach - Standard but a touch too salty.

We were a party of 4 with a reservation at 8:00 PM on a Wednesday evening. We were told upon arriving that they could not yet seat us, as there were several other parties that were late to their reservations.

9:00 PM rolled around and the hosts barely offered their apologies. After 50 minutes of lingering, they brought us an appetizer at the bar area to "tide us over" which consisted of 4 pieces of lettuce with a tiny cube of meat on each leaf.

We were seated after 9:00 PM, as if we should have been thanking them for allowing us to dine at such an establishment.

2 of us ordered 2 of the strips, and the other 2 ordered 2 of the burgers. We also got meatballs to start and a crispy potato side along with some brussels sprouts.

Everything was decent, but nowhere near worth the prices. I kind of expected at a place like this, your party would be treated politely and taken care of. 

With OK food and horrendous service, I definitely would not recommend - what a letdown.

First class all the way. Even though we waited over an hour for our reservation to be honored, it was well worth the wait. I basically recommend everything on the menu. Some of the highlights were the meatballs, burratta, duck lasagna (amazing), and filet on the bone. If you're going to spend big, spend it here!

Ambiance - awesome, dim light, cool decor. Two person corner seat was great.

Food - oysters are amazing! Burger meat was very tasty. Filet mignon special (not bone in) was good.

Service - very good though the server forgot my steak knife and I had to ask for one after my meal was on the table for a few mins....

I hope all you guys with 5-star reviews enjoyed your first steak dinner in NYC!  I'm jealous of you - you have so many better meals ahead of you.

When you drop a Benjamin on a steak dinner you expect a little flare, a little elegance, a little departure from the norm.  Not sure how this place manages to occupy such prime real estate while offering nothing unique.  Our server was, how should I put it, a dork, and even though we were clearly the last dinner shift (started at 9:30) they made several attempts to rush us out of the restaurant while our plates were still half full.  When we ordered wine the glasses came ten minutes after the bottle arrived. The "salt and pepper fries" were decidedly unsalted and unpeppered... was this some kind of joke?  Because I didn't get it.  The only bright spot for me was the freebie chocolate bon-bons that came at the end of the meal -- hence the two stars.

Stay thirsty, my friends.

This place is always solid. Service is outstanding, food is consistently delicious, and the atmosphere is very casual/elegant. Extensive wine list and the waiter will help you pick the perfect wine for your food choice. Can't wait to go back.

We came here before going to a show at the Lynn Redgrave Theater and were so happy we did. The food is straightforward. Good quality meat with well prepared sides and a decent wine list. The broiled oysters are also worth a mention. Somethings, this is exactly the kind of food you want, no fuss no muss. 

Our server was inexperienced, but that would be my only complaint.

FANTASTIC. Who knew NYC could have another steakhouse without it getting boring. They proved themselves worth of a spot on the NYC Steakhouse list for sure. Great atmosphere, music was such an added extra.

I think this is a nice steak place. The food good and the service was nice. I was surprised that our hostess seated us in the bar area even though I had reservations for two weeks in advance. We asked to sit in the main dining room once I  saw we were lead to the bar area. I didn't think that was very nice. The bar area is more crowded and cramped. I didn't think it was cool of them to try to do that. 

About the grub. I had the meatball app. It was tasty tho nothing too special. Then I had the 14oz rib eye steak. It was well cooked and it was big.  The steak was nice too but also nothing I haven't seen before. The side were tasty as well. 

Overall I had a good meal but I prob won't be back. It just not that great and memorable to spend so much money on this place.

3.5 stars - My husband and I aren't exactly connoisseurs of steaks. We tend to skip all the steakhouses for special occasions or promotions. We however came to Bowery Meat Company after hearing about their duck lasagna! It's portioned for two so it was perfect for my husband and me to share. 

It took a while for the dish to be prepared but we were given complimentary bites to hold us over. Meat bread, a slice of cured meat?, and fried pesto rice ball. Usually steak houses provide the most generous (gorgeous) bread baskets, I was surprised by bowery's bite sized offer. The lone slice of bread was stiff and cold. I couldn't bite or chew through. The rice ball however was crunchy, gooey, and delicious. If only it came with sauce. 

Then onto the main event - duck lasagna! 
Stacks of tender pulled duck meat, melted stringy cheese, perfectly cooked pasta - smothered in creamy sauce and a layer of crispy cheese! First 5 bites - so good! The other 3/4 of the meal - way too rich. I actually had stomach pain after eating such a rich meal - perhaps I'm becoming lactose intolerant too? Definitely order a side (probably best with a vegetable) to go with this dish!

We were given complimentary small bite - ice cream chocolate ball and a brownie to end our meal! What a nice touch from the service staffs! Overall - my husband described the duck lasagna dish - a between a good and a great. But not something he would ever crave. Perhaps one day we would return for their steaks.

This restaurant is a must try! Nicely setup. Comfortable and spacious. The food was amazing.The baked oysters were outstanding. The duck lasagna was also delicious. The service was exellent. I Took my husband here for his birthday and we had our one and a half-year-old baby with us. needless to say he wasn't exactly easy -he cried a little bit and wanted to play with everything.  The waiters were so kind and everyone at the restaurant was so pleasant. Never made us feel
Like we were a bother. I would highly recommend for dates or family dinner

I was taken here for my birthday and was pleasantly surprised by the great menu and food to follow. The sashimi was delicious with sesame seeds. They go brought us some bacon bread and mozzarella balls with pesto. Both were great as well. For our main course we had the filet with cream spinach. To complete the meal they gave us bonbons. Couldn't have asked for a more delicious meal! We will be back!

hands down best steak I've ever had, The ambiance is extremely romantic. One of my favorite places. 

Must have a bottle of wine along with your steak! 
Will be coming back here for sure
If you are ever come to New York you must have dinner at Bowery meat company absolutely 5 stars quality place and you must order the oyster

fancy spot. it's elegant as suspected. waiters are kind and attentive, food is great as well.
salmon sashimi 
duck lasagna.

Yum. Great bone-in filet! Cooked perfectly. Creamed spinach was also delish, it was whole leaves instead of chopped. Only complaint-we ordered another side and it never arrived, but they did remove it from the bill. 

Cool vibe, we'll be back!

Went here for a friends birthday dinner in a large group. It's a great space for group  dinners. We say comfortably with lots of room to move around. The vibe was hip. 

I was under impressed with the food. The cocktails and appetizers were good. The steaks were disappointingly under seasoned and overpriced. 

It was a fun environment to go with a group, as long as you're not looking for value.

I highly recommend their Prime New York strip, which is one of the best NY strip I have ever had. Indeed, I am not impressed by their broiled oysters since the original flavor of oyster is completely covered by garlic, crispy breadcrumbs and other spices. I also tried some Bone-In Filet Mignon, but unfortunately, it was not as good as I had imagined. I suppose they can do better than that.

As for the dessert, I ordered the sundae. I expected it to be light, but it turned out to be too heavy for me. So I did not finish all of it. But anyway, it was good.

I gave it 4 stars because of its NY strip. Classic.

Okay, but little overhyped and overpriced. Had a 6:30 reservation and didn't finish until a little after 10 pm for a party of 4. Very slow service. 

The appetizers were the standouts - broiled oysters, foie gras and chicken liver pate, crispy polenta were all excellent. We ordered the duck lasagna for two- good but wasn't wowed like a lot of other reviewers. we also ordered the lamb chops and grilled rib eye. Lamb chops were ok but the grilled rib eye was very good.

Ordered the sundae dessert and it was decent and the donuts with coffee. The donuts were 4 tiny pieces and not worth it although tasty enough.

Overall not a bad experience but for the price, except for oysters, wasn't too wowed.

I looooove this place! The funny thing is my husband and I passed by it and never noticed it until I discovered it on Instagram. The vibe, the atmosphere, the food, everything is amazing! We started with meatballs (best meatballs I've ever had). My husband got the lamb shank (Easter special) with polenta and I got the salmon with spaghetti squash. The lamb was cooked perfectly. It fell off the bone at the slightest touch. The salmon was perfectly crisped on the skin and soft and flaky inside. The spaghetti squash was to die for! Then came the dessert *drum roll* s'more sundae!!! Who thinks of this stuff? I'd like to thank whoever came up with the idea of infusing a s'more with a sundae personally. Overall a great night and most importantly, a happy stomach.

There are so many steakhouses in New York City. I don't need to come here. I made a reservation for dinner in advance. I had requested for a table with more privacy. However, upon arrival, I was informed all the tables have been booked for table of two. I don't remember the food being amazing. It was not memorable at all.

I noticed they sat us with four other Asian couples. I was wondering if they are put all the Asian couples in one section. I inquired about this to the manager and of course.. she said this was just a coincidence. It still bothered me because all the other couples elsewhere were not Asians and they had tables with privacy. 

I won't be back after this experience.

The duck lasagna was the highlight of the meal.  Considering that it is called the "Bowery Meat Company" the steaks left a lot to be desired.  The pricing is similar to what you may see at Del Frisco's or Ruth's but the serving size is about 75%... I would not come back here.

Absolutely wonderful service and great food! Dined here with a group of 4 last night and the service was outstanding. The food was delicious.  Our group ordered the Bowery steak, petite filet, salmon and for starters --charcuterie board and meatballs. 

The sundae was out of this world -- big enough to split four ways with some left over.
Way overpriced. The service was also terrible and nonexistent.  Wish I could say I would go back but I won't.

Complete classic NYC. 

This restaurant is so swanky and trendy, and the food is just amazing at every turn. 

We tried just about everything, and it's as if every item just for better than the rest... I'll just list off what we ate, each of which was incredible... Some of the best food in NY. The highlights are starred... 

-friend oysters*******
-duck lasagna 
-Bowery cheeseburger **** (the best you'll ever get in NY)
-filet steak 
-creamed spinach 
-side potatoes 
-smores sundae **** (the ice cream is made from toasted marshmallows... It literally tastes like whipped toasted marshmallows)
-red velvet ice cream sandwhiches

This would be the perfect place for dinner with fancy colleagues, birthday dinner, Saturday night date night, list goes on. 

Not to mention, service just as amazing as the food. Can't wait to try for brunch!!

Have you ever had a meal where you didn't want to drink or eat anything afterward just to savor the leftover taste in your mouth a little longer? 

Me neither.. Until Bowery Meat Company.

What. An. Experience! The customer service was impeccable from all members of the staff, the sommelier helped us pick an amazing Bordeaux to perfectly complement our meal, and can we just talk about the food?!

We had the broiled oysters to start, which were very reminiscent of the New Orleans chargrilled oysters, loaded with so much flavor from the garlic and cheeses. The oysters still retained their flavor and moisture, although I might say that they were overpowered by the toppings.

After the broiled oysters, the extremely hospitable restaurant manager introduced us to the raw oysters with fresh ponzu and jalapeño. Now, THAT was amazing. Definitely a must try if you like raw oysters!

Going back to my opening statement, the fillet rocked my world.
I had an off-the-menu special of the night that was a boneless fillet with mashed potato and a glazed sauce that I could not get enough of. The beef was cooked perfectly at a medium rare, tender and just the right amount of chewiness; but I would recommend getting it rare to preserve the juices and savor the fantastic meat quality.

This is how every meal should be.. Served at the right pace, by the right people, and with the finest ingredients. Thank you for an amazing night, BMC!

P.S. My friend and I found out that they closed at 10pm after we left at 11. They did not rush us at all whatsoever, didn't even mention their closing time to us even after 10pm. That's a gesture of true hospitality. So much brownie points!

Probably my favorite steak house in NYC.  Trendy vibe, good service and perfect food.  We started with the burrata which was extremely creamy but the roasted peppers that were strewn underneath were particularly good.  I went with the burger because I can never turn down a burger by Josh Capon.  Cooked perfectly to my medium rare specifications.  Husband wanted a steak that was tender and also tasty.  Their bone-in filet mignon was the perfect choice.  Enough fat and flavor from the bone with the tenderness of filet mignon.  Delicious!  The creamed spinach is also worth a mention.  The perfect consistency making it truly a comfort food.  
On a previous visit we shared the duck lasagna.  It's worth every calorie.

I can't say enough good things about this place. Enjoyed our dining experience immensely! We were not rushed... Our waiter allowed us to enjoy our dinner. The wine was delicious. Food was amazing... There is not one bad thing on the menus. S'more dessert was the perfect ending!

I came during the middle of dinner service on a weekday and was easily able to get a table by the bar.  I ordered the duck lasagna for 2, it was definitely a large portion but I'm a big dude and I probably could have finished it if I really wanted to.

The amuse-bouches they brought out (basil pesto rice ball, rosemary focaccia with salami, pork belly lettuce wrap) and the complimentary sweet after the meal (salted caramel petitfour) were unexpected and delicious.

The space is classy and the service was friendly and sociable.

Great food and service with a casual elegant atmosphere. Their broiled oysters were all the rave.  Duck lasagna was cooked perfectly with a good balance of duck, pasta, cheese & sauce. The grilled rib eye was not as tender as I would have expected but the creamed spinach and the complimentary sour cream and onion hash brown were delicious.  At the end of our meal they gave us mini-salted caramel ice cream balls which was a nice touch.  Will be back, its worth the visit.

Service slow and waitress not friendly.  Duck Lasagna dense but well worth the taste. Steak + Salt = Great Flavor and Taste . At BMC Steak - Salt = OK steak
Overall a good meal nothing to write home about Another strike...told the waiter to pack my bone with my leftover steak and low and behold no bone. Service is really bad and needs to be addressed. Will not be back anytime soon

The minute we walked in, the hostess greeted us with a smile and led us to our table. Our waiter was very attentive to our interests and offered great recommendations from the menu.

The manager came over to our table to say hello and see how our dining experience was going which made our experience memorable. I highly recommend dining here and will definitely dine here again!!


Food 5/5
Service 5/5
Ambience 5/5 
Location 5/5

Shady rolled in to this LES hyped hotspot on a cool rainy spring loaded with anticipation. Warming up next door at L'Apicio with some prosecco and merlot, Shady and crew tore right into the meal. 
Shady had done his homework and knew exactly the road to take. For apps the crew split two entrees..the duck lasagna  and the cheesebruger, both highly recommended by fellow yelpers. Both were home runs. The lasagna was split 4 ways and was a big portion for an app. Crispy lasagna noodles with delicious duck underneath was decadent dining at its best. The Cheeseburger was also split 4 ways and a perfect app sized portion. The Gem wedges rounded out the app round. 
On to the mains...The Bowery steak, lambchops and a Burrata ravioli dish all cooked perfectly and devoured in minutes by the group along with several nice bottles of Rhone Valley reds. Sides included outrageous Patatas Bravas and aparagus. 
We all swore to just have 1 bite each of the desserts, but that lasted about 3 seconds as we obliterated a Dark chocolate Dome  dessert along with a s'mores sundae. 
Service was on point up and down the line, the vibe in the restaurant is excellent as is the decor.
Bottom line-one of the dining highlights of the year for sure. At least several more trips are necessary to actually sample the large appealing  list of true appetizers we neglected this time around. 
Dinner for 4, with 2 bottles, was approx 130$ per person , with ...well, u know by now...

I went to dinner here for my boyfriends birthday. The duck lasagna was really delicious as well as the burger. My only complaint is that I ordered a basic margarita. The waitress didn't ask what kind of tequila I wanted so naturally she picks the most expensive and charged me $24 for the margarita. I thought that was a little underhanded. I used to waitress and I would never surprise a customer with that bill. Other than that really great food and good for a birthday!

Service was very attentive without being too intrusive.  Botanist cocktail was refreshing and could've ordered a third if not driving home. Companions ordered Bowery steak which was very very good but the marinated rib eye was super packed with flavor and so moist served medium...that it was the best in a long long time.
Deserts were good.  S'mores, chocolate dome and cheesecake ended the meal nicely..  I had the branzino which was very good.

Was just ok. Food was all good but the price tells me that it should be much better. Staff, location and ambience were all good. We went straight to the main when ordering and the server said 'Are you sure you dont want an entree as the steaks will be quite sometime arriving'. We said no Thanks then the steaks arrived within 7 minutes. Got to Love an upsell.

I have had the privilege to eat dinner here twice. The first time we had a birthday party of 9, and the service, food, and ambiance were exquisite. The restaurant is beautiful--reminds me of an LA billionaire's  yacht in the 60's--warmly lit, and not too loud.

The complimentary pesto arancini are incredible. We split a bunch of appetizers, and the hamburger was absolutely amazing.

You must order the cheesecake. It is the best I've ever had.
Best steak in the city.  All the sides are great.  Bread pudding desert is huge winner.  Fantastic service.

First Impression - food was great, esp the duck lasagna. 
Experience - interesting. 
Remember the server coming around with a slabs of raw meat and a lecture about each type of meat and its ancestry. Felt like we had gone back to the stone ages. 

All in all, you get what you paid for.

BMC was outstanding.  Steaks were excellent.  Service was impeccable.  Good choice of wines.  Cocktails had plenty of liquor in them. Took the family to celebrate a birthday.  Everyone was very happy.  Ice cream desserts and sorbets were amazing.  I would definitely return.  Worth every penny. As expensive as other good steakhouses in NYC.  You get what you pay for.  Fine dining which was not rushed at all.  Would give is 6 stars but limited to 5 in the ratings.  If you care about the quality and the service, this is the place to come , experience and enjoy life.

This place was incredible - I've been a fan of Josh Capon forever; the dude is awesome. He is a complete and utter culinary genius. BMC was unreal. I recommend getting the duck lasagna and the Côte de Boeuf. They were both incredible. The service was impeccable. The cocktails were beyond refreshing and the place was just beautiful. I will for sure be back.

Super impressed! The perfect dinner for any occasion. Recommendations: 

Char broiled oysters - perfect 
Duck lasagna - wish it was saucier but it was ducking good (see what I did there?)
Burger - the top 5 burger I've ever eaten 
Tomahawk steak - It's what they are known for
S'mores desert - I'm lactose intolerant and the pain was worth it. Do not leave without getting it! 

Great drinks, amazing food. Service was a bit slow , but they were very nice. They kept bringing us some small free apps that made us feel welcome. Def coming back for some scotch and steak. If you're in between the steak and burger...Go burger (unless it's the tomahawk steak)!

Excellent. The staff was so helpful in helping us decide what to drink and eat. The chips with Bacon Salt were fabulous. The steak was wonderful as well. Broiled oysters were a hit at our table. Highly highly recommend.

Very good food. 3 stars only because service was so so....I just didn't feel they were good about coming around to table. It felt like it took about 30 minutes to even come for our order of appetizers and similarly for check ins to table. 

Other then that - food was great including even the comp stuff they brought to table. Great date spot otherwise as well.

Great food, great atmosphere, great service. Had a Christmas dinner here and had a great time. 
Four of us split orders of wagyu meatballs, burrata, zucchini carpaccio, Chinese pork belly and a shrimp cocktail. My favorites were the zucchini and the meatballs. 
The only disappointment was the Bowery steak which we got in between our mains. A few people recommend it to me and I read good reviews about it but we really didn't care for it. Flavor and texture weren't for me. 
Then we split a tomahawk ribeye and a bone in filet both very good. 
All in all a good experience. Is it my new favorite steakhouse? No but I wouldn't tell anyone not to go and have actually recommend it to some friends to try the place. 
Great food, great atmosphere, great people watching and a great night.

More the feel of a French bistro then a midtown steakhouse fits snugly into the neighborhood ambiance.

Food quality is top notch with a concise but excellent menu.Desserts great as well.

However, the kitchen simply cannot cook steaks to desired temperature, so no matter how good the beef one leaves disappointed. Both steaks came out prepared wrong and several attempts to correct showed the inability of the kitchen staff to deliver on the chef's promise. My friend has never returned a steak. They failed him twice in one dinner.

In a word--Disappointing

What an amazing meal and service!!!! They were super helpful with the menu and helping us decide what to get...
We ordered the broiled oysters (amazing, super garlicy), the chinese pork belly (not my thing, but my boyfriend LOVED it), the T-Bone --- one of the best steaks I've ever had. 

They brought out the wrong steak at first, but quickly realized and took it back and were super apologetic. While we waited for the correct steak to come out, the manager came and brought us small slices of the duck lasagna - oh my god, it was SO good and I was dying to try it! They also gave us a complimentary side with the steak, and after the steak, they brought us a complimentary S'MORES SUNDAE!
