I'm not a dessert person, but this was probably the best dessert I have ever had. We were SO full that I barely even ate the steak and sides, but I managed to eat half of the sundae. YOU MUST GET IT!

Also, for the prices, you'd expect a more upscale vibe but its pretty casual.
Pretty good steak.  Cooked properly.  Took a long time for meals to come.  The salads are huge.  Service was just ok for an expensive place.   Probably won't go back.

Off top like everyone knows New York invented like hot dogs, pretzels and they got some kind of rare big ass apples or somethin, but I was like nahhhh IMA-SWITCH-IT-UP you feel me. I got off work ( high key beeeeen making paper you feel me? ) and was on my #LonelyBoyGang shit ... everyone always like "one, low key IS the loneliest number AF" but high key not in NY! hella people everywhere! Stays lit A-F they also got this rare ass half dead Pokemon fish that be like everywhere! So I find this spot, I walk in and it's all elegant and shit! I felt like upper class! I scooped a NY steak cause like I'm in NY right? Straight #DuhGang ... That steak was ALL DANK! High key perfect ... You know I went #VeggieGang too. Asparagus was lit squad. Then I went full posh and got the brownies with the ice creams cause Y-O-L-O ... Thought it was gonna be on some BJ pazookie swag but hellllll nah boo boo! 7 dank ass brownie cookies with the dopest ice cream STRAIGHT U-P. I dipped feeling all full. Spot was lit. Lez get it! Oh yea, waiter homeboy had an accent, hella tight.

This is a fantastic steakhouse that I feel is on coarse with establishments like Del Frisco's and the like. We ordered the Côte De Boeuf which was an abundance of steak. We requested the steak to be medium rare and it came out decadently juicy and flavorful. The appetizers and sides were equally remarkable.

Visited November 2015

First visit here for an anniversary dinner on Monday. Service in the beginning was very slow. Took 15 minutes for a server to come by and we had to flag someone down to place a drink order. 8pm reservation, there were some tables but it was not packed by any means. We spoke to the hostess about the lack of service and for the rest of the night service picked up. But if we hadn't said anything I have my doubts if it would have improved. Food was good but I prefer BLT in Flatiron. The steaks and sides are more seasoned and flavorful. Props to them for comping 2 desserts to try and make up for poor service in the beginning. I'd come back for drinks but not food.

I have been here twice for dinner and both times were excellent. The food was well prepared with interesting variety in the menu and the service is very attentive. The space is quite nice with some degree of separation between tables. The bar area is also very good with a nice selection of cocktails.

I don't have a ton of experience with steakhouses, but this was a really great (and delicious) one. I surprised my boyfriend for his birthday after trying to find a young and trendy steakhouse. I had requested they bring out the different cuts of steak which was a fan favorite. The broiled oysters were AMAZING, as was the hanger steak. Overall, great dinner!
Burger didn't have much taste and was under cooked, very bloody even though asking for medium. The duck lasagna was burnt and stale. The dessert was good.
Fine dining is at it best. Excellent and welcoming service, from wine to food. We had no complaint, everything was delicious! Will be returning again!

Found out about this restaurant from a relative to celebrate my birthday with dinner. Very courteous staff and the food is delicious. Definitely going back! Anyone looking for a good steak dinner with good staff, I highly recommend it!

Post the Open...we were in the mood for steak tartare after a full day of day drinking and tennis and found BMC on yelp.  SO GLAD WE CAME HERE!

From food, to service, to decor to presentation, all very lovely and I would come back here time and time again!

They presented us with an amuse bouche of meat filled bread with cold cuts and two cheesy fritters.  The bread, was tender but chewy and well seasoned.

I ordered the "Down In Mexico" drink as I am a big fan of mezcal; I was at first a bit hesitant because there were so many ingredients (mezcal, fruits, egg white etc.) in it but it turned out to be a perfect smoky sweet balance.

Now the food...

-Spagehtti Pomodoro: spaghetti was perfectly al dente, tasted and looked home made.  Sauce was perfectly seasoned, one of the best...I saw it on the menu and I was curious to see how a meat company would do pomodoro, and I am impressed.
-Chinese pork belly: deliciously seasoned and prepared, charred on the outside but goey and meaty on the inside.  It comes with lettuce as a wrap along with pickeled hot peppers and pickles.  SOOO good!
-Foie Gras: Had an sweet buttery coating, comes with perfect amount of toast points!  
-Steak Tartare: OMG would eat this all day.  The hand cut meet gives a great mouth feel and chew, while the seasoning was outstanding.  Their steak tartare had a umami taste in the seasoning which helped elevate the overall taste.

Thank you BMC for an incredible dinner

Came here yesterday with a few friends to celebrate my birthday. Cozy atmosphere. Took a while for our server to come but once he came he was great! He knew everything about about every cut and what to recommend. My husband and I wanted to share the Tomahawk but he likes it medium rare and I needed it medium well since I'm pregnant. Server offered to have it done first medium rare for my husband and then recook whichever pieces I wanted to how I wanted. Best of both worlds! I also didn't want creamy spinach so he offered sautéed spinach. Beverages were always topped up so no one ever had an empty glass and table top was always cleaned up from any dropped food or spillage. Chef even came out to check we were happy with everything. Food was awesome and service was spectacular. Would definitely come again (the medium rare steaks looked so delicious)! Oh! And apparently they do their own baking! Somehow an ice cream cake appeared and it was just perfect to end the night! Five stars!

My favorite steak spot in NYC! And my favorite salmon in NYC! Double win. Great seafood and meat. Zen-like but warm and cool decor. The food is so good!! And so is the service.
Highly recommended!

Disappointing.  There was a lot of hype over the opening of BMC and we were really looking forward to our evening here.  First off, it can be challenging to get a reservation here but half the tables were empty during our meal.  Service was very slow and for our party of 4, we were there for 3 hours.  The food was overall mediocre.  The best aspects of our meal were the amuse-bouches, duck lasagna and smores sundae dessert - and they saved this from being a 2 review.  The pork ribeye was just awful, very fatty and undercooked.  The veal chop and tomahawk ribeye were nothing to brag about - everyone said they've had better.  At their prices, it ought to be the best darn meat you've ever had.

The experience was magnificent from beginning to end. We started at the Bar waiting for the last member of our party to arrive and were graced with the home made potato chips. Best chips I've ever and will ever put in my mouth. We were seated right away once our fourth had arrived and were immediately given our bread basket which was a pleasant surprise of bacon bread with a side of cured meat. Cocktails were decent,a bit sweet. Wine was delicious and completed the dark meats well, but a bit pricey for a glass.

 The appetizers were divine. Of the three we got- i would recommend the meatballs and steak tartar. Unique and tasteful.

The wait staff was very well informed of each meat and its cut, which was a big help even for a table of foodies. 

Tomahawk steak was delicious and perfectly cooked as requested (medium rare). I also would not leave the establishment without a bite of the Duck Lasagna, because that was bomb.  

Desert was perfectly sweet but the check bitter. One of the best restaurants I've been in a while- great for a group of 4 +. Enjoy!

The food was good but the service was terrible and hence the 2 stars. 

The hostess was incredible rude and arrogant. We had reservations for Saturday night and when we asked a few questions she was clearly annoyed huffing puffing. I've worked as the hostess before and understand dealing with people can be difficult but c'mon, take pride in what you do. I'm pretty sure her name was Kristen, if you're reading this- please don't twirl your hair and say I don't know what every question asked.

This was an exceptional meal. We were lucky to have Chris as our server. Super sweet, fun, knowledgeable, etc....  We have been around a long time and have tried a lot, not just in NYC but all over. We were really impressed by  the shear taste and seasoning of all the food we craved tonight.  We wanted a little bit of everything and what we got was an incredible dinner going above and beyond.  Just yummy.

The quality of the steak here is far inferior to other NYC steakhouses, and the price premium is NOT justified at all. What you're paying for is nice decor and a hip location in lower Manhattan. We ordered the highly recommended & reviewed Tomahawk steak for 2, which was $150! OK ... we wanted to try the restaurant's hallmark dish & ordered it medium-rare.

Honestly, even at medium rare, the meat was really tough & chewy. Totally unacceptable for a steak that costs this much. Since I was there for a birthday dinner, I obviously did not want to complain & make a big deal. I was not impressed by this place. For reference, the steak for 2 at Peter Luger is $100, tender, and served sizzling on the plate!

Not worth the price. The steaks were good, but the sides, apps, etc. were not up to par.

Our bill came to just under $500 for a party of 4 with wine, and we left less satisfied than if had gone to Strip House, Peter Lugers, Del Friscos, or the like.

Lesson learned!

Let me just clarify one thing.  The duck lasagna is totally average and not impressive at all.  People rave about it because they are amused by duck being in lasagna, but it's just not a great dish.  It's not bad, but not worth the hype at all.  

I've had the burger a few times which was quite good.  It's a nicely prepared burger with just the right condiments.  Fries are standard issue, but do the job.  I was also impressed by the meatballs - quite good.  Steaks are good too, but not super interesting in my mind . 

Ambiance here is pretty good, but it gets very loud at times.  Service was good and I'll definitely go back to this place every so often.

Overpriced for what you get and I have definitely had better elsewhere. I like the ambiance and it definitely checks the box for that steakhouse feel. I feel like whenever you put "steakhouse" with any restaurant it immediately jacks up the price of the rest of the menu - even when you don't have any steak. Maybe go here with clients if you are looking to impress with the space and at least it isn't coming out of your pocket.

Was just okay. Nothing special and was for our anniversary. They barely did anything to acknowledge it. Steak was fine but again nothing special and there are so many different places that are so much better quality for that type of money. Actually my husband's steak was over cooked. He ordered it rare and it was definitely more like Medium. The farmers salad was plain. The oysters were good but the dressings were off and they didn't serve the normal horseradish and vinegar. Service wasn't so on point and there was a couple fighting next to us the whole time. That was not the restaurant's fault but unpleasant nevertheless. It also caused our waitress to partially ignore us which is very unprofessional. My husband wanted dessert but the wait for her to come over and take the order was so long that he lost interest. Wasn't a memorable anniversary dinner. It isn't likely we will return here.
wonderful experience - GREAT burger,  broiled oysters were amazing. While it was a small portion of the lamb chops, I walked away from the meal extremely satisfied. Would come again.

Came here with my brothers on a Wednesday night. I've heard a lot about this place and it's been on my list, so I was excited to say the least.

We ordered a bunch of starters for the table including broiled oysters, Wagyu meatballs, and the hand-cut steak tartare. These are all equally a great way to start the meal. The favorite might have been the meatballs which had a great pairing over creamy polenta and a cheesy gravy.

All three of us ordered the burger due to a recommendation from a friend. The burger is topped with griddled onions, raclette cheese, a tomato aioli and French fries on the side. The burger was not the best I've had in NYC, but it was right up there. They were all cocked to our liking, and there weren't too many complaints on the food. For dessert, we ordered butterscotch profiteroles (not always on the menu) and the favorite S'MORES sundae which is huge and terrific. It can easily be split with 3-4 people too.

Our overall impression was that we were very pleased with the service and the food. It's a place I've been wanting to visit and I wasn't let down at all. Maybe next time we get the steak!
Great restaurant. Menu options are delicious and more unique than your typical steakhouse. Staff is very attentive. I would highly recommend.

had a great time saturday night.  really nice ambiance will good upbeat music, none of that stuff steakhouse feel.  Its not pretentious but its still really nice in there.  had the broiled oysters which were perfect and wagyu meatballs- also delicious.  hubby had the filet- it was great but more charred on top than we preferred.  i myself had the burrata ravioli which was delicious.  hubby had a great cocktail and they were nice enough to recreate a cocktail as a mocktail for this preggo.  i had the japaneno infused drink-really yummy.  lastly we had a special dessert of walnut cookies w/ vanilla ice cream.  delicious but it was described as gooey, which it wasnt.  overall, will be back!

Such high hopes...dashed. The place itself is pretty cool. Good vibe and decor. We got the 2lb lobster. It's prepared Rockefeller style, although they don't tell you that. I didn't eat it because I'm GF. The pork ribeye was subpar. It only had 2 chewable bites. The rest was gristle and wouldn't cut with a knife. Won't be back.

One of our favorite restaurants! The steak is always A++
my only complaint (which might be insignificant for others) is that the seating is annoying- youre basically one on top of the other

Appetizers:
-Chicken liver and foi gras parfait:  good but not as good as I was hoping. 
-Broiled oysters: ridiculously good. Would come back to order this alone. 
-Bitter greens: oddly addictive. 
Mains:
Tomahawk: perfectly cooked and delicious. Did not disappoint. Well rested and perfectly seasoned. 

Bowery cut: honestly- just ok. The ribeye deckle is the best part of a cow, but this was nothing special and not worth getting again. Not bad, just not that good. 

Cocktails: we tried two of the house cocktails and they were not good. We then switched to a glass of Cabernet each and that wasn't very good either. Should have just ordered a bottle like we usually do. Waste of $75 or so for drinks we did not enjoy. 

Will be back for the oysters and to try different cuts- maybe the t-bone florentine or the ny strip.
If your a meat lover Bowery is a must! Chef Josh Capon great chef go find out for yourself!!!!

Good solid steakhouse. The three girls we dealt with coming in were great. Nice, friendly, pretty. I got there early so I hit the bar while waiting for my friend. The bartender made terrific Old Fashioned and Gimlets for us.  Waitress was on point. Nice Asian girl, don't remember her name, but she was perfect. Just the right amount of attention. That's an art.  The buss staff was sharp as hell. I broke a glass on the floor. They cleaned it up in 2 seconds, like it never happened. (It was an ACCIDENT, I haven't broken or spilled anything in a restaurant in nearly 20 years, so CTFD everyone) The sommelier was a really nice guy an lacked the douchebagginess that most of them have. Gave us a great bottle for a price that we felt good about. 

They are a bit lacking on bread for the table. They put these two bread sticks and 2 slices of dried sausage on the table...... that's it. I get it, less is more, but it just felt like less. 
Had the Chinese Pork belly for an app. The chateaubriand was quite possibly the finest piece of cow I have ever eaten, unbelievably good. They gave us steak knives but we didn't even need them. That's how tender it was. Unreal. 
Nice, Nice job BMC.  It was my first time there and I would not hesitate to come back again. Nice vibe, nice, people, beautiful steaks, good service and so on. 

4 cocktails, 1 app, chateaubriand for 2, bottle of wine, tax, tip, all in about 158 per person.  My friend put his half on his visa black card. Did you know that card is made of metal? its like a Chinese throwing star. He could kill someone.  Snob. 

Probably Gallaghers is next... stay tuned. some of these old steakhouses rest on their laurels and don't perform. We shall see. 

Ladies and Gentlemen, that's my time......

This review is solely based on service and not food. I had a late reservation on a Saturday night and showed up 45 minutes early. I didn't have any expectations of getting seated early, but thought that I would show up early and sit by the bar. When I checked in, the THREE hostesses at the front told me that a table would be available for me very shortly. For that reason, I didn't go to the bar and order any drinks because I thought that a table would be ready shortly based on what was said to me. I sat in front of the hostesses waiting for a table for 30 minutes. Thirty minutes turned into 50 minutes and I still wasn't seated. I checked in with the hostesses twice during that time and they continued to reassure me that a table would be ready shortly.

If the hostesses had been honest with me about the wait time of my reservation then I would have been perfectly content to kill time by the bar. Instead, they insisted multiple times that my table would be ready "soon." I waited for 50 minutes for a table and was not even seated at my reservation time. I left the restaurant on principle.

Quite expensive considering the food is only ok.
Burger: Good, but not worth the price. Get a better burger elsewhere.
Tomahawk steak: Flavor was good, really hard to chew. Didn't like their sauce. Save your money. Definitely not worth the price.
Bowery steak: Meh. Only ok.
Pork ribeye: I really liked this. Flavor was good and it was tender.
Overall, I wouldn't go back.

The boyfriend and I are big fans of Chef Capon, we've been to El Toro Blanco and saw him during the 2016 New York Wine & Food Festival while we saw him make his Shrimp Scampi recipe. Just like El Toro Blanco, Bowery Meat Company did not disappoint and was that and more.  Everything we got from beginning to end was great.  They sat us by a corner that was comfortable and pleasant, everyone that works there is very attentive and very detailed. As we sat down we were offered complimentary bread with bacon in them, I mean you can never go wrong with bacon and inside a bread, to die for. We also got complimentary pesto rice balls, also amazing.

We started with the Steak Tartare with toasted bread and lightly seasoned baby romaine lettuce, overall amazing and I wouldn't mind eating this every day, I might be wrong but there might have been some capers in there. 

For my entrée I got the herb crusted lamb chops with cucumber yogurt, for my side I chose the patatas bravas. Both went very well together, the lamp chops were charred and crispy and as I am writing this my mouth is salivating. Someone wrote that BMCo it's too expensive and the food is a-ok, I have to disagree. You get what you pay for and if you go to any other restaurant with the same food you will not get the same quality and love that you get at BMCo *drops mic and walks off*.

I can't seem to remember the name of the drink but it was the first one on the list and it was something that ended with Long Island, good as well. Great place to bring a meat lover, you can come here on a date night or any type of celebration.  Since it was Thanksgiving weekend we missed Chef Capon, hopefully next time the boyfriend and I catches him here at BMCO or any of his other restaurants.

This is our favorite restaurant in New York. 
The food is unique and delicious and the best in the city. The appetizer hash browns are a must!  They are the best you will ever have. Don't miss the oysters as they are incredible. The steaks are outstanding and the mushroom ravioli is one of my favorites. Make sure to leave room for desert you must try the s'mores Sunday. Our server Lindsey was very attentive and informative. Her suggestions were perfect. She is one of the best servers you will ever have. They also have a extensive beer and wine list to satisfy every palate. Our complements to the chef!!!

Place is great! Went there yesterday and had the ribeye. Great flavor and cooked to perfection. They serve it with a few peppers on the top that were awesome. The chicken was also really good. Two sides were potatoes and mushrooms. All delicious!!

Great meal. Great staff. Duck lasagna is on point! Highly recommend for a nice meal out. Waiter came out with all the different cuts of meat they were serving and explained the ins and outs of each one. We finally settled for the 40oz. Bone-in tomahawk ribeye as well as the 40oz. T-bone. Both cuts were cooked perfectly and tasted great. Also the broiled oysters was another highlight of the meal. Wait staff is knowledgeable and courteous. Also, was very cool to see the chef come out and check on a few tables to see how the guests were doing.

I decided to take my wife here for Christmas Eve. We were seated right away for our late-evening reservation in what looked like a full house. The glasses of red wine we chose were nice in variety and it didn't appear there was a poor choice on the menu. Despite the lengthy selection of bottles, they looked to all be priced on the very high end and I would recommend going by-the-glass.

We went with the salmon sashimi, broiled oysters, duck lasagna, bone-in filet along with a side of brussel sprouts. They also offered a complimentary rice ball amuse bouche which was a pleasant surprise. The salmon sashimi tasted fresh and was a nice start to the meal, while the oysters were also fresh and the breading and seasoning tasted superb.

The duck lasagna, as hyped as it is in other reviews, was a major salt bomb, along with the brussel sprouts that we had. It's possible we had someone who was just heavy handed with the salt that night. It was unfortunate too, because we did enjoy how unique the lasagna was, and how tender the sprouts turned out.

Luckily, the filet was perfectly cooked and well seasoned, and mostly the saving grace for a relatively lackluster meal. At this point I regretted not going for another steak instead.

The service was quick and very accommodating.

Overall, I think we had a decent meal that had suffered from a grievous error in heavy handed seasoning.

Had a great time here on a double date with my husband and good friends. We enjoyed the steak and our sides. I am a big fan of the sour cream & hash browns and would come back just to get some more of that.

I came here just a couple of hours ago with a friend of mine.
I would have liked to write to you a private message, but since on your website there isn't a "contact us" section I have to write it down here.

We ordered a Cote de Boeuf, asking it to be medium/raw.
It was properly cooked but we immediately noticed how full of tendons it was. 
So we informed the waitress, who told us that it was normal since that cut is very fatty and for this reason it contains more tendons.
After that Josh came to us (and that was nice at the beginning) asking about how it was going.
We said that we would have expected the meat to be more tender and with less tendons.
I think he listened to us considering as if we were just to two guys who don't know much about cuisine, steaks and restaurants, because he just didn't listen to us, saying it was all "ok guys". 
Then my friend showed him a slice of meat where it was clear the tendons were really too much, but he kept saying the same things.

Even if that cut of meat should (as they said) normally be "fatty and with tendons" we noticed that there were too much tendons, making it not easy to eat.
Obviously I wouldn't have complained if it was a cheap restaurant.
Moreover we have always known that cut of meat should be tender and not "with tendons" as they tried to convince us.

Anyway, I don't want to judge the whole restaurant on a single dish, but this was our experience.

Excellent in every aspect. Service was great and very friendly without being overwhelming. Food cooked to perfection. Quality out of this world. We got a lecture on what to expect from every cut of meat (that's what she said) 

It was my birthday dinner and they brought a Tiramisu from a different restaurant knowing they didn't have it on the menu. (It's sort of a b-day tradition)

The quality of everything was excellent so it was a lot of money but not expensive by any means. 

The only thing I didn't enjoy way the wine glass itself. The wine was amazing and at the perfect temperature. I felt it was a bit "fat" for my liking. That being said, they got two new customers FOREVER. 

People who love to cook for other people.

Came yesterday have been several times as diner before I was   solo and as I was in area buying some bar stools hunger came over me  . Staff were welcoming bartenders were knowledgeable  . Had the broiled oysters which never fail . Don't know how they get them so soft they taste like butter must have  .  Dry aged cheese burger gr8 flavor  , simple bun toasted  with grilled onions which is perfection .  Great to see a chef owned restaurant doing so well . For some people this is expensive but you definitely get what you pay for .

Oh.m.tripple g. This place was fantastic! To start they bring over a raw meat platter and go over every cut. The cote de boeuf is 100% the way to go!! Fantastic. If you wanted to pop in for drink and apps the broiled oysters were to die for (the best I've since Acme in NOLO). The duck lasagna and wagu meatballs were good. Definitely get the smores sundae and the peanut butter chocolate cake was delish. As an amuse bouche they serve these delicious rice balls. We were also comp'ed the banana bread pudding, of which they only make a select few each day. Great experience!

Everything I ate was pretty damn good. The Kumamoto oysters were perfectly dressed and the foie gras was so smooth and full of flavor! The caesar salad was topped with flufffy cheese. Yummmmm. The cote de boeuf was cooked to perfection. I asked for extra of the chimichurri sauce for our steak. Last but not least, we had the s'mores for dessert. The ice cream was a marshmallow fluff! 

The foie gras had to be my favorite dish of the night. Service was okay nothing too memorable. We waited 30 minutes or so even with a reservation on a Friday night. 

I will definitely be back when I'm in the city.

Made reservations for my birthday dinner since I always have to order a steak to celebrate. Normally I always get a porterhouse steak, but based on this place's reviews I decided to try their famous Tomahawk ribeye (also recommended by our waitress). It was good, but not great. Too dry for my style (got it medium rare and should've done just rare), which is why I'll stick with juicy, rare porterhouse steaks moving forward. 

Highlights:
- Hefty portioned complimentary appetizers. beyond the assorted breads they give you upon being seated, they also offered us a sample of the chef's special (it was a lasagna-type dish) which was delicious but super filling. Try to resist if you plan on having a large main course!
- Pretty and modern interior, not stodgy like most other steakhouses. Also mostly booth-style seating for a more comfy and lounge-y feel, which I prefer. 
- Friendly and helpful wait staff.

My wife and I went to BMC while we were staying in NYC after we were married there that same weekend. I had been following BMC on IG for some time and was eager to see if the menu tasted as good as it looked. BMC far exceeded my expectations. The food (oysters, steak tartar, grilled ribeye, and dry-aged duck breast) was PHENOMENAL!! Each cooked item was prepared perfectly to temperature and served at just the right intervals. Cocktails were out of this world. Lastly, but no least, our server was exceptionally well versed in the menu and able to articulate each dish item  perfectly, as well as being extremely professional. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

I enjoyed my dinner at BMC fine but overall was a bit underwhelmed, especially for the price. We started with a round of cocktails that were tasty but  a little steep at $18 each. I had a jalapeño tequila one that was like a margarita - just pretty good. The winning appetizers were the cauliflower steak and an order of confit duck wings, which was a special. 

Next the steaks. I don't mean to sound like a snob but given all the choices for great steaks in NYC this place doesn't stack up. I had the ribeye with shishito peppers and it was pretty average - and $50 is a lot to pay for an average steak. Wife got the bone in fillet which was actually very good. For the sides we had Brussels which were tasty but oily,  hash browns and patatas bravas which were both just OK. 

The service was a bright spot. Our waiter was friendly and knowledgeable. I should have taken his recommendation and ordered the fillet.

Went her for my husband's birthday, and it was very good!  I was searching for a nice steakhouse for his birthday...but one with a more romantic and trendy vibe and this did not disappoint. 
I am a big pasta lover, and I had heard the Duck lasagna was fantastic, but we didn't want it as our main dish so we each got a 'baby lasagna' - a few bite taste that was the perfect size! (and only $3/each - I had been worried they would way overcharge for something so small).  And for my main I got the truffle burrata ravioli - it was fantastic.  I previously thought the Mamo truffle ravioli was my favorite pasta dish, but this may top it.
My husband got a lamb starter and the veal and thought both were very very good.
They had a few small bites before/after dinner that they bring everyone, and they were very good as well. The service was perfect, atmosphere was great, and we were in a nice corner table so we could sit close together.  
We will definitely be coming back!

Bring lots of money!!!!

The food was outstanding.  Their Kale Caesar Salad was great.  Loved their sides.  We had the Brussel Spouts, a 5+ and the Creamed Spinach, a 4.  I had the bone in filet mignon and it was excellent.  Good seasoning and cooked to perfection.  Every bite was a treat.  My ladies had the T-Bone Steak for 2 and also said it was a winner.  

The place is not without its faults though.  The tables are right on top of each other.  Not particularly private or comfortable.  Ask for a booth.

As food as the food was, it was too expensive relative to what you could get at just about all the other traditional NYC steakhouses.  The T-bone for 2 was $148.  Luger's, Sparks, Keen, Benjamin's et al have the same thing for about $100.  While good, the BMC T-bone was no better than others we have had elsewhere.  

We each ordered the Caesar and when they came out I saw that one of them would have been fully sufficient as a starter for the 3 of us to share.  I did point out to our otherwise excellent server that she should have told us how big they were.  At $16 per salad, this was quite a significant service failure in my opinion.  I will admit though that we left nothing over as the food was that good.  

By the time dessert came we were very full and didn't order anything.  At that point the server comped us one of the menu desserts that had smores and ice cream.  It looked great but it was barely touched by us.  

It's a pretty place but like I said before, it is too cramped.

Food 5.  Price Points 2.  Atmosphere 3.  Service probably a 4.5 except for the salad thing dropping that portion of the rating to a 3.  

I might be back, I might not.

Last minute decision before Blue Man Group show.  Reservation was not available at 7pm Saturday, but plenty of room at the bar.  We sat at a high top.  Right out of the gates, service was questionable The menu was short and sweet and appropriate for a steak house.  The waiter was not happy to answer questions and less happy when he found out we weren't drinking (he was a young,  inexperienced Asian man).  The food itself was awesome.  Ribeye cooked to perfection, with little unique green peppers that enhanced the steaks flavor.  The side order of creamed spinach was awesome.  The other entrée was a burger, order medium well.  It came pretty Medium, but was very good. So the food was a 4.5 rating.  Again the service hit... He dropped a bill before asking if we wanted anything else. Maybe we Looked rushed, but we weren't and were actually going to order 2 cappuccinos and look at dessert.  We decided not to ask and paid the bill and left.

Came here on a Saturday night at 7pm and was seated immediately. We were sat at a table for two, right next to another couple, the tables were so close together we could literally have joined in their conversation if we wanted to lol. 

The restaurant has a nice ambiance, they played top 100 songs, the servers, busboys, and everyone was very nice. The service was good. Me and my husband ordered two ribeyes, the hash brown, and spinach and cream. The ribeye was just alright .....nothing special. The hash brown was our favorite. The spinach and cream tasted like PARMESAN cheese. I think it partially made me lose my appetite. It was so salty it overkilled my palate. Mayb that's why I wasn't so interested in the rib eye. 

There are definitely better steak houses in the city, I probably wouldn't come back here ...wait no, I would most likely not come back lol

This place is great all around. We came in with a group of 4. We ate like a group of 10. 

Started off with a cocktail called the Botanical that was really delicious. BMC has their head chef visit each table to go over the various cuts of beef they offer. This was a nice intro to what went on to be a wonderful meal.

We ate everything. They dropped off some prosciutto bread, soppressata, with 4 small rice balls the size of a gum ball. They appeared to be risotto and pesto.  Small but tasty. Next up we split Tuna Poke (new item that night), Duck Wings (new item that night), Duck Lasagna (delicious),   burger split 4 ways, and  Wagyu meatballs. That was our starters. Everything was on point. Id easily order any of the above again on a future visit.

For dinner, the table shared: Bone-In Filet Mignon 14oz, Bowery Steak, Charred Hanger Steak, Côte de Boeuf, Tomahawk Ribeye 40oz. We cleaned house. Wrapped up the bones and a few small scraps. Everything again was excellent.

None of us at this point thought we would eat another bite, so we forced ourselves to split a smores dessert. BMC complimented us with a special Banana Parfait dessert. Im not huge into desserts, but these were really awesome. The parfait especially. Overall, this is a great place to recommend for anyone. Not just for steaks. It might be pricey with some of the higher end cuts, but you get what you pay for. 

Service was top notch as well. I wish I could remember our servers name. He really kicked ass all night.

Ohmygod the duck lasagna.  Its been weeks since I had dinner here and I still think about it REGULARLY.  Like....a weird amount.  It has changed my life.

Honestly everything was amazing.  For apps we ordered the ricotta, meatballs, octopus, and my beloved duck lasagna.  Was this too much food?  YES.  Did we regret ordering anything?  NO WAY.  If you have to choose, go for the lasagna (how many times can I say lasagna in one review?) and the ricotta.

Looooved that they brought the platter of raw meat to the table so you could see the cuts.  Super cool and actually v helpful.

We opted for the Cote de Boeuf with the spinach, hashbrown, and brussels sprout sides.  Again zero regrets.  I only wish my stomach could hold more.

The dessert special was an Oreo Ice Cream Cake...need I say more?
Actually yes I do need to say more...it was incredible and I couldve eaten 2 more slices even with my stomach full of steak and lasagna.

If I'm ever Oprah rich I will be dining here every night forever.

I have never eaten at this restaurant in person and am judging the food purely based on my experience with two deliveries through caviar. The food is so delicious!!
Most restaurants that are good in person are horrible for delivery. My delivered ribeye, mushrooms and brussel sprouts were divine. I hear the burger is supreme, and can testify that the fries arrived hot and crispy and the pork chop was a home run.
Excellent steak house.  Had the tomahawk which was great. Also recommended the duck wings. I'll be back.

Bowery meat company is aptly named. You are surrounded by meat in more ways than one. By the decadent cuts of beef offered, as well as the overwhelming majority of male patrons in suits dining here. This place seems bougey--almost too bougey, but the food holds up extraordinarily well. 

The risotto balls, the foie gras parfait, the charred octopus--okay, so pretty much everything here is just hands down fantastic--even if it is impossibly heavy. I'm going to be honest--I had A LOT of entrees here, but I can't remember anything as vividly as I do the Duck Lasagna. Just fantastic. It was decadent, delicious, and full of melt-in-your-mouth flavor. What I appreciate about Bowery Meat Company is that I came with a party of 10, and they portioned out all the entrees evenly so that everyone got a piece. That means everyone got a bite of the $125 Chateaubriand (YES, DELICIOUS) as well as the $26 Cheeseburger (Good, but don't come to a place with the words "Meat Company" in the title, and order just a cheeseburger). In my opinion, I don't think their signature item--the Tomahawk Ribeye is actually worth it. Seems like you're just paying extra for the bone, which makes me question why I am paying for something I can't actually consume. The other steaks are just as delicious and well-prepared.

What I don't appreciate about Bowery Meat Company, is that being such a large party, they held us to a spend minimum. Naturally, I try not to let these things bother me--but really, is that necessary when we were already ordering $100-something steaks? We ordered a very expensive bottle of Red Wine to buffer, but who likes being reminded of those things during your dinner? Not I.

The ambiance was casual yet formal. I was craving steak and was recommended this place by a colleague. Went there and and had prime rib and my boyfriend had the duck lasagna. The prime rib was fantastic.  The best steak I have had in years. It was perfectly cooked rare, superflavorful and tender with little fat. The lasagna was good but honestly the steak was better. The price was high, 50 dollars but probably worth it. If it were 10-20 dollars cheaper it would be fantastic.

Came here on a Saturday night and it was crowded - definitely recommend a reservation. The place is not tacky compared to other steakhouses, which is big plus. 

I had a duck lasagna with my wife and unfortunately I did not find it so outstanding as most of the people here. I think the duck flavor was lacking a little but overall is a solid choice. It is not so large, so I recommend ordering one or two appertizers.

3.5 stars. Came here late on Saturday (10pm reservation). Pretty spot-on in terms of what you'd expect reading all the reviews: "trendy" spot frequented mostly by young people, extremely - extremely - loud, dark, busy, cool decor. Definitely not a stuffy steakhouse. The meat was good, and exceptionally expensive. Worth trying, though won't be back in a hurry!

I came here on a Saturday night and the service was outstanding. The atmosphere is swanky, warm and refined all at the same time. The staff were great and helpful. They looked happy even. The best dishes were the steak (of course) and the ricotta appetizer. The wine list is wonderful, too!

Nice convenient downtown steakhouse. I like that it's not too stuffy, but not too casual. Been here about three times now, twice for work and once for my bday birthday - had a blast every time. As of my last trip, I gave up eating red meat, but figured i'd have my last hurrah meal here to go out with a bang.

For apps, you can't go wrong with the charbroiled octopus, BMC meatballs or the oysters. The duck lasagna is also a hit as well; three people can partake of it even though it's made for 2.

I've had the Tomahawk Ribeye, the Cote de Boeuf and the charred hanger steak. You really can't go wrong with any, but the Tomahawk is definitely quite the meal for two. For cocktails, i've always been a fan of the Full of Smoke. The service is also A+.

This place is definitely one of the better steakhouses in the city and is worth checking out!

I was looking for Wagyu beef and this pops up on the best Wagyu in nyc.  Guess what, no Wagyu ever but their menu was very interesting.   We had a celebratory night here and tried appetizers, entrees, salad, meat, cocktails, champagne and wine.   The charred octopus was very tasty and tender.  The yellowtail poke was fresh and light, more light appetizer than sushi style.    The bitter green salad was borderline the best salad I have had.  I don't like bitter but the combination of greens and such was fantastic.  You don't want to skip this.  I had the bone in Filet (not my normal but gave it a shot) and my wife had the veal chop.  The steak was perfect, the veal chop was perfect.  I can't say anything better.   We did have desserts, they were good.  I can't really remember much more about them.  :)

The signature cocktails were balanced.  I would recommend trying a few and finding your liking.  They aren't sweet which is nice.   They have Krug and Billecart-Salmon Rose in splits.  They are both excellent quality and two different price points.  Two of my favorites normally.   We had the Turley Zin (Rattlesnake) and if you don't know Turley, you are missing out. 

The synopsis is they have great beverage selections to go with great food in a great atmosphere and the staff was very nice and courteous.    I really was surprised to find BMC, the other reviews and the menu made me interested and we now have a go to place for fun and business. (oh and please get some Wagyu)

Wow! I was blown away by the service here (the foods great too). The service was amazing, consistent, helpful, thoughtful, without being any bit annoying. From the host, to our server(s), and each person that cleared away a plate. I had a wonderful meal in a great atmosphere. Thank you!
Terrific place for great steak and wine. Service is exceptional.  Not too formal and not too casual.  Just right for the impressive dinner
Terrific place to grab a steak, particularly the bone-in filet. Has a fun vibe, relaxed, and the portions are solid but not overwhelming. The service is terrific and they really go above and beyond.

Enjoyed my night at this restaurant with my friends...we all enjoyed our food and drinks.... customer service was very good as well... great bar tenders, waiters and hostess.... I personally ate the filet Mignon , it was definitely two thumbs up... I would eat her again...
Wow what a meal!  Great steak and everything else.  Chef Capon really knows how to run a restaurant all his places are solid choices.  Everything was great just throw a dart at the menu and enjoy!

I had a reservation for 8:30pm for a party of 4 on a standard Friday night.  We all got there on time but apparently the table wasn't ready yet.  Fine, nbd.  We went to the bar got a few drinks.  Next thing you know it's 9pm.  I went to the men's room, saw the entire dining room, and spotted a few tables open.  I was absolutely dumbfounded why we had to wait to get seated so I ask the hostess and she said "either wait or .... you can sit here in the parlor."

Why would I make a reservation at 8:30pm to be seated at 9:30pm in the parlor?  Riddle me that?  I voiced my discontent and quite frankly they couldn't have cared less.  9:30pm rolls around and they finally seat us.  

Forget the front staff's incompetence, the food itself is lacking.  I have literally nothing good to say about the food.  Horrible steakhouse.  For the price there are so many other options.
Seated right away with no reservation. Had the tomahawk Ribeye Steak. It was to die for! The juiciest   and flavorful steak I've had!

Ate here last night. The best Restaraunt I have ever been to in my life! The staff are all so friendly and helpful. The hostess, waiters and manager are a class act! The decor is beautiful and trendy in a classy way with a large bar area for pre dinner drinks. Fun music pumped throughout, but not too loud as some trendy places think they must do.
The food OMG!! We tried all of the following and they were all spectacular:
Wagu Meatballs (ridiculously good!)
Mushroom Polenta
Barbecue Pork Bellies
Cauliflower Steak
Tomahawk steak for 2 (Best ever in NYC and enough for 3)
Chateaubriand for 2 (prefect and also enough for 3)
Mash Potatoes
French Fries
Spinach 
Gelato & Sorbet wonderful. We're so full we didn't have room for some of their signature deserts which looked amazing.
Go here and you will have a memorable culinary experience. This is not your typical steakhouse. It is special in EVERY way. It's not cheap but it's worth every Penney and MORE! We can't wait to go back!!!!!

I COMPLETELY fell in love with this restaurant! I went yesterday with my boyfriend to celebrate his birthday and the service was beyond amazing. 

The moment you step into the place, you are impressed with the atmosphere/decoration of the establishment. This place is great not only for couples but definitely for larger groups as well.

The food is delicious! If you are a meat lover, this place will definitely leave you satisfied and the waiter was super friendly. He addressed any questions we had and even had the wine director come to our table to suggest which wine would go best with our meal! 


Bowery Meat Company- thank you for making my boyfriend's birthday very special, we now have a favorite place .

Wow!  We've visited several NY steakhouses & this place was incredible.  We had the ribeye & the strip & they were cooked perfectly with a tasty char.  The oysters may have been the best I have ever had.  The shrimp cocktail was tasty as well.  I asked to speak with the chef so I could compliment him & he actually ended up giving us a tour of the kitchen.  What an experience.  Highly recommended.

I go to a steak place and I look for solid drinks (check), flavorful appetizers (duck lasgna.. OMG!, ricotta plate, and octopus salad!!), and perfectly cooked meat. (check).

I read in another review that they are not shy from seasoning their meat; I agree and love it! It's not over the top and it's not bland. I had the tomahawk streak and it was amazing. Perfectly cooked, a little on the rare side (which you expect at a steak house, as overcooking is a sin) with the perfect salty/yummy seasoning!!

Lastly; which I think pushed it to a 5 star review is the ambiance. It's pretty chill; not overcrowded, not too loud.

Had dinner here last night for Father's Day. We had the bmc meatballs, cote de boeuf and duck lasagna. The food was absolutely amazing but our waiter was the worse. He look like he didn't want to be there. However, the waiter at the next table was very nice.

Made a reservation here after seeing some of chef josh capon's videos awhile back. For a Saturday night the joint was never completely full, so I suppose you could show up here without a reservation. The decor and ambiance inside all flow well together. 

The food:

1) a duck lasagna was offered for free from the chef. There was a generous portion of duck in the dish and it was very good. I believe it's offered on the menu but it's rather large and meant to share. 

2) the cote de boeuf. 38 ozs of goodness I am still dreaming about. For 2 hungry people it's up to you whether sharing or ordering 2 individual entrees, most entrees would be cheaper than sharing. As the shared dishes are all rather large. Since they're known for the tomahawk and cote de boeuf, we ordered the cote. For the fans of steaks with a nice char, this is the place for you. The ribeye was nice charred all around and cooked to a lovely medium rare. The cote de boeuf is aged 40 days, with sufficient marbling. 

3) ordered sides of potato purée and broccolini. Both were good, if you're ordering a tomahawk or cote, I'd say skip the purée. It's too much food. 

4) dessert was awesome. We had the chocolate chip cookie. It tasted like some sort of hybrid between that and a brownie. Lovely. 

5) the wine list is deep!!! Lots of selections including DRC and the 5 houses of Bordeaux. Their somm is also a really cool guy and very helpful. 

I can see how some here wouldn't like this establishment. However they failed to research just what this restaurant is. If you love meat and red wine, this is the place for you.

Really not sure why this place has such great reviews. Needed a last minute dinner reservation, and this place was available. The best part was the ambiance, though it is so dark in there, you can barely make your way to the restroom. Also, I unpleasantly bit into huge chuncks of fat, because I couldn't see what I was eating. Service was very attentive. Good complimentary bread. Steaks were sadly mediocre - didn't even feel the need to finish mine, which is very unusual. Left without dessert.

I had to host a friend from Beijing and decided to come here because I saw Chef Josh Capon featured on Bloomberg. While waiting for my guest to arrive, I sat at the bar to hang out. To my surprise, Chef Capon himself was hanging out with his impressive friend (front office fixed income trader at Royal Bank of Canada), and I was sitting next to them. I let Chef Capon know that I was here because of he was featured on Bloomberg, and he appeared to appreciate that. Chef Capon's personality really shines and I would probably watch his Netflix special if he made one. Anyhow, onto the meal.

The bar: the warm potato chip-like snack, followed by the fried salami, was wonderful. It was also difficult to make a decision from the selection of seasonal cocktails on the menu, so I had a lovely Belgian beer first and read through the cocktail list. I decided on the Wood Reserve bitter cocktail, which was as bitter as advertised, perfect for my preferences.

Food: the appetizers we chose were the octopus, duck wings (which were really duck drumsticks), and broiled oysters. I liked the broiled oysters the most because the duck drumsticks were relatively tiny and the octopus was cooked well, just not really "wow" in terms of flavor. The thing that stole the show was the Tomahawk Ribeye. Per the recommendation of our server, we ordered it medium, which was a great temperature. The outside was seared just perfectly, and the meat itself was exceedingly high quality. (At this price point, I honestly expected more meat). It's difficult to impress my guest, who has probably eaten everything on the planet, but this impressed him. The wine list is gigantic, and it took me a while to choose a pairing, which we loved. We chose wine number 3688, which I recommend. We wanted the doughnut dessert that we saw on Yelp, but it was no longer on the menu and the server advised us that there were no longer any doughnuts in the kitchen. Sad.

Service: this is where this venue earned a fifth star. I made a reservation for 7 p.m., had to change it to 8 p.m., then my guest did not show up until 9 p.m. However, the venue was extremely accommodating and told me not to worry, that the table was mine for the rest of the evening, and that they don't close for a few hours. I could never get this type of treatment at other steakhouses (*ahem* Peter Luger). 

Decor: the bar is beautiful. The dining room got a bit dark for my tastes but that's how people like to dine in NYC, I guess. Restrooms were quite clean, if you could find it through the dark hallway.

Service was 10/10. We couldn't have been happier with our waiter as she made sure we had everything we needed. I got the ribeye medium rare and it was way too charred on the outside and ruined the steak. Glad I tried the restaurant but I'm not sure I would come back with so many other quality steak options in the city.

Went out for steaks last night with two of my friends for a birthday. We go for steaks for each of our birthdays and always choose a different steak house to try something new. 

First I'll start by saying it's in a great location if your looking to go out for some nightlife after dinner. The ambiance and decor in the restaurant made for a nice setting for dinner, they had music playing which was enjoyable. The service was quick and our waiter was very knowledgeable when it came to the menu. They start us out with a pretzel crusted pesto ball and some bread with dried sausage to start complimentary. 

As for the food we ordered the BMC meatballs, the duck wings, and the charbroiled octopus for starters. The ducks wings were outstanding, the meatballs came on top of polenta with a sauce they were tasty but a little dry in my opinion. The octopus came out cold which I was not a fan of and could've used some lemon or acidity to it

For my main course I got the 14oz ribeye which was boneless personally if I go to steak house I want a bone in steak because we all know that's where the flavor comes. The cut wasn't the greatest because it was very fatty but the chef cooked it perfectly to temperature for me. They had a good house made steak sauce which I needed because the char was a little to much. Usually a good steak needs know sauce, but it needed a little booster. The loaded baked potato wasn't really that loaded it just had some sour cream on it, but the creamed spinach was good. We ended dinner with the s'mores dessert which was out of this world (toasted marshmallows ice cream graham crackers with brownie bites and hot fudge) and a cappuccino.

As a whole  the dinner was good and a good start to a night out with a group

Came here yesterday for my friends birthday dinner and had an amazing time. The food here is top notch and what makes this steak house stand out is the outstanding service. 

The meal starts with complimentary freshly baked bread and salamis and fried mozzarella cheese balls, which was awesome. 

For apps we started off with duck wings that was the best thing i've eaten in a while. The flavor was mind boggling and they were crispy and cooked to perfection with some type of mint dipping sauce. We also ordered meatballs that was in a polenta sauce that was was also amazing and full of flavor. The cream of spinach was killer and the baked potato with sour cream was the bomb. The octopus was a home run as well.

For my man entree i decided to go with the bone in fillet mignon and I'm glad i did. Whats awesome about this resteraunt is they bring out your cut of steak that make you which is amazing and great experience to add. I found that unique and different mow let go back to my steak. My fillet was cooled to perfection and had a nice charcoal sear on the outside of the steak and was full of flavor. It came with a sauce i poured over it that i really enjoyed and was different. The sauce wasn't your typical steak sauce, but was nice and warm and gave the steak nice touch.

The staff and waiter was very assertive and attentive to me and my guest the whole night. I had a little spill on my paints by my waiter that sucked. But the house manager got note of it and came over shortly and told me that they would pay for my dry cleaning, which was awesome, but felt no use for it unless they had a dry cleaning machine in the back on the premises. I found that professional though and appreciated the gesture in making sure i was taking care of. 

Nice bar on the first floor where you can grab drinks before getting seated. The inside decor of the resteraunt was fabulous and very trendy and modern. This resteraunt overall is just beautiful and nice place to come for dinner. I had a great time last night.

*GREAT SERVICE
*AWSOME FOOD
*BEAUTIFUL RESTERAUNT
*GREAT SIDE & APPS
*AMAZING DESERTS

OVERALL a solid steak house that i recommend for anyone looking to have a great dinner.

Went there for a birthday celebration. We ordered the beef tartare and foie gras as appetizers. Love the bread for foie gras (carbs for life lol) and we had the t-bone and ribeye between the four of us. Also had mashed potatos, mushroom, asparagus and the hash brown. YOU MUST GET THE HASH BROWN. best one you will ever have. We were so full we packed the unfinished meat. Then they brought out a slice of their infamous cookies n cream (oreo) ice cream cake with a candle. and we also ordered the s'more sundae. Everything was delicious. 
Saturday night wasn't very dressy; People were mostly casual. I would recommend it for a large group.

If you are in your 20s and don't know any better, you might love this place. We had a steak craving and we're gonna go to our usual Wolfgang's or Luger's, decided to try this out because of all the good reviews... Mistake. We got the tomahawk for 2 which was pretty good, cooked well, but not anything to get excited about. The hash browns were good. The salmon ceviche was terrible. Duck wings were ok.  Even the bread and 2 measly pieces of salami to start were not worth the calories. Nothing was good enough to want to come back. For the price, could've gone somewhere​ much higher quality.

food here was very good, service was good too, but i looked over my amex bill and realized i was overcharged $50 after organizing the split between diners and leaving a cash tip.  i haven't asked any of the other diners whether they too were overcharged.

Great place for amazing food. Pricey but worth it! The meatballs were amazing! I could've had this alone for dinner, but I came for the steak so just had to try this... The steak was perfectly cooked! It had this crunchy salt crust on the outside that had this smoky flavor. The bite was this crunchy and juicy piece of steak!!!! The mushrooms and hash browns were very tasty! This was a dinner for two and was definitely more than enough food.

Took the family and a few friends for our eldest son's birthday dinner.  The place is certainly trendy and popular.  The meal started out very well with an assortment of appetizers that all made a good impression - the Ricotta dip and broiled oysters were really terrific. Disappointment came when the entrees were served.  Truly UNexceptional.  I had the lamb chops which  were plated on a pile of chalky cucumbers and yogurt.  The lamb was gristly.
My husband had veal chops he didn't LOVE and while we really don't mind high prices, the food and service (I'll get to that) have to support the prices.  THe one vegetarian in our party called the Ricotta Ravioli "fine". Our guests were not wowed. The sides - creamed spinach, loaded potatoes and the sauteed mushrooms - well one out of three was good.  The desserts were also ok with a 6 -1 "meh" for the much touted smores sundae. And about the service -- the hostess came and apologized as we were eating the entrees because of the long wait.  OK, It was acknowledged and that meant something but the waiter was generally UNavailable.  He seemed to have a lot to take care of and our table wasn't on  his radar.  If you are looking for meat, any other the other great steakhouses have Bowery Meat Company beat.

Had dinner here with 5 friends on Saturday for a group celebration.  Let me start with the good/great:  The food was excellent.  We went for it and ordered the 40oz T-Bone Florentine, 40z Tomahawk Ribeye and 20oz chateaubriand (100oz of steak!!!).  We also had all four kinds of oysters, the foie gras parfait and ricotta as appetizers with creamed spinach, mushrooms&carmelized onions and green beans on the side.

Everything we ordered was excellent but quite fittingly, the steaks were the true stars of the show.  Our group had a vehement disagreement as to whether the T-Bone or the Tomahawk was better (both were 10/10 topnotch). Aside from the steaks, the foie gras was a standout. I think the only thing that missed the mark was the ricotta which could have been a little more interesting.

Drinks were also great.  We started with a round of their well mixed craft cocktails, followed by an excellent cabernet over dinner and the montenegro amari to finish. All were excellent, especially the amari.

Our only main gripe (which given the $200 pp price tag is a big one) was our waiter.  If you are coming here with a group on a Saturday night it is because you are having an epic meal and it felt odd from the beginning that our waiter never greeted us, asked if we were celebrating anything or gave a general overview of the menu.  We also saw other tables where the waiters were being more helpful and showed diners the butcher block of raw cuts to help better inform their ordering.  To be fair, our waiter's recommendations were all great but I had to continually ask for his opinion and guidance when we were making decisions.

This really is a great restaurant and the meal we had was one for the ages but our waiter's demeanor left a bad taste in our mouth and it was something we noticed from the very beginning right when we sat down.

I came here on a Thursday for dinner with coworkers. The hostess greeted us and showed us to our table right away. We started with various cocktails which were pricy but interesting and tasted good. I had the Italian fizz which has a prosecco base and comes with a lemon peel it was bitter but in a good way. The server brought out a meat board and described each cut so that we could pick based on our preferences. Prior to our appetizers we received complimentary risotto balls, bread with bacon, and salami. We had appetizers to share, we ordered the broiled oysters, steak tartar, and Cesar salad. The oysters were really great the meat was fresh and the breading was crispy. The steak tartar was very good it has plenty of parsley and other herbs and comes with grilled bread and lettuce wraps. The steak tartar does not come with a raw egg however our waiter was nice enough to bring one out for us. The Cesar was very good it was a mix of kale and radicchio with tons of cheese.
We ordered the duck lasagna as a middle course and each had a piece. The duck lasagna is so luscious the duck inside is so fatty and good, extra cheesy and the top has a little crisp to it - highly recommended.
Our group ordered the tomahawk ribeye, chateaubriand and I had the Bowery special steak. All the steaks were cooked to perfection, well seasoned and tasty. We ordered the hash brown side and the creamed spinach. I thought the hash brown was good but the creamed spinach was amazing.
For dessert we had the cookies and cream cake and the s'mores sundae. These desserts are big definitely get them to share and don't skip dessert! At the end of our meal we received complimentary caramel ice cream balls they were so good! The overall experience was similar to a classic steakhouse yet very unique! I will be back Bowery Meat Company!

BEST STEAK HOUSE IMAGINABLE. Normally I can take it or leave it when it comes to a steak houses, but this is like no other steak house. First the decor is warm and inviting, while being upscale and classy. The bar tenders were very helpful in recommending drinks and carried themselves well. Our table of 8 was seated in a beautiful room with a few other tables and were given great recommendations on drinks and meats.

A massive tray of the different cups of meat were brought table side so we can see and be explained what each was like. That tray was maybe the most beautiful thing I have ever seen. We decided on the chateaubriand, the t-bone, the tomahawk, and a whole lobster with sides of hashbrowns, creamed spinach, and whipped potatoes, and market onions. For our appetizers we went with king crab claws, 4 different types of oysters, the ricotta dish, hand-cut steak tartar, charbroiled octopus, and the duck lasagna.

You must try the duck lasagna!! Without a doubt a must must get. My favorite meat to my surprise was the chateaubriand. Normally I like a marbles cut of steak, but this steak was cooked amazingly I could eat it plain for every meal for the rest of my life. Add the sauce that came with it and you go to heaven.  Everything was absolutely flawlessly prepared and cooked to perfection. The good thing about this place is that they didn't ask how you would like the meat prepared, they cooked it the way it would be presented best.

Stopped in with a few buddies for dinner.  We didn't have reservations but that wasn't a problem as we were seated pretty quickly.  For the appetizer we ordered the grilled octopus and it turned out fast and well.  For main course two of us got the rib-eye which turned out to be cooked exactly to what my friends wanted.  I ordered the salmon (which the waitress loved too) it was pretty big portion over a bed of greens.  It was one of the better fish dinners I have ever had and it was seasoned well.  The service was impeccable as the waiters were on top of things quickly and to the point.  Didn't try the desserts as we were too full from having dinner.

oh man.  when this first opened, I loved bowery.  been there 2x and it was great.  There again this week, and not sure what has happened, but the quality has tanked.  ordered shrimp cocktail and octopus.  the first was just okay...but the octopus was so fishy i had to spit it out.  the steaks came (we both had filets) and they were just ok.  were going to stay for a bottle of champagne and dessert, but decided to bail.  The service was nice, but i'm going to stick to my strip house and 4 charles favorites.

Took my boyfriend here for his birthday. The Tomahawk steak and octopus were so worth it. Pricey but worth every penny. We ordered the cookie ice cream cake too which was a bit too sweet and heavy for us but I didn't expect them to be dessert expert so it's okay. The interior design and the staff were amazing too. I would definitely come back for another special occasion-- it was the best steak I've ever had in my life!!!

One of my favorite steakhouses in NYC. Everything is excellent and has such a delicious twist. My mouth is watering writing this review. Service is excellent and Josh the chef is a lot of fun. My favorites are Duck Lasagna, Meatballs, Burger, Tomahawk Rib eye and basically all of the sides. Deserts are even amazing including the off the menu bread pudding which is a must. I have been to every single steak house in NY and im telling you this is excellent.

Dining here was not planned, we (boyfriend and I) literally was walking by as we were trying to figure out what to eat and decided to walk inside. 

Decorations: dim lights, candles and r&b playing in the background.... yup! When I heard sky is the limit-B.I.G ft 112, playing in the background I just knew we had entered the right place

That first bite brought me a contentment I'd never known (such a fatty ) 

I had lamp chops (cant remember if it was $46 or $54), cooked medium well with a side of broccolini. 

Boyfriend had the bone in ribeye ($56) with a side of loaded baked potatoes ($12)

The portions were large so we were able to share our sides 

My lamp chops were seasoned and cooked to perfection lol yummm and the steak was sooo good, lightly seasoned.
 
It's a perfect location for a quiet date night or just a night out to enjoy/appreciate some great meats and wine! 


My server was such a sweetheart. This will now be our go to spot for excellent steak! There are NO Crowds!!

Excellent all-around experience here. Very attentive staff, and everything I had was amazing. Only complaint I heard was that the duck lasagna was a smidge salty but I didn't have any. Prawn scampi appetizer was off the hook. My friends who got the oyster appetizer special (the ones from Long Island) said they were much better than the WA-based oysters on the menu. I had the 14 oz bone-in filet mignon and it was magnificent. Brocollini side was really good, too, which must be saying something since I normally hate vegetables. Key lime pie was a dessert special and you MUST get it while it's available. Absolutely fantastic! Would definitely come back to this restaurant and highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys meat.

My first time eating chateaubriand and it was magnificent.  It was so tender and tasted like filet mignon but softer.  It came with roasted green beans and petite potatoes drenched in butter.  We also had broiled oysters topped with butter, garlic, parsley and breadcrumbs - divine!  Our cocktails were hit and miss.  The Sunset in Caracas (rum, mango, coconut water) was just okay.  The Padre Picante cocktail was delicious.  It's made with Casa dragones and espolon tequila, pineapple, green chartreuse, and jalapeño, with a cucumber garnish and red chili rim.  Excellent service!  Love the ambiance. Check it out if you're in the area.
3.5 star. It seems that their service has declined since some r views. No presentation of meat. However, their broiled oyster tastes great. Their stake is a little bit on the raw side.

It was meh and just not very good for the price point. Both our filets came out over cooked..... my husband is never one to complain or send anything back - I think it's actually the first time I've seen him send anything back.

They argued about how it was cooked and tried to point to the pinkest portion of the steak as proof and tried to make the argument that the steak cooked medium well was really medium rare....
it was really odd and awkward. At this point, it wasn't worth the headache so we dropped it. The manager came by later and said they would take it off the bill. They never did, but at this point we just wanted to get out of here so we paid the bill and left.

There are so many amazing steakhouses in the city. This one just isn't worth your time.

Came for my wife's birthday on Sunday. We found Bowery Meat Co on yelp after searching for a Steakhouse near the West Village where our Comedy Show was after. 

We made a reservation online for 5:30 (think thats when dinner service starts) and had the whole restaurant to ourselves. The inside of the restaurant is beautifully decorated and we sat in a semi round table that was comfortable and spacious. 

We got a bottle of French wine recommended by our sommelier that was the perfect selection. We then ordered the broiled clams (bread crumbs and cheese baked ontop) for an appetizer and decided to go with the T Bone steak for 2. We ordered cream spinach and a hash brown potato with chives and sour cream. Our meal was delicious.  The cream spinach was the best I've ever tried. The T bone steak had a great crust and was cooked perfectly that it didn't need steak sauce. 

We finished up our meal with a baked cookie topped with ice cream. My wife loved every part of her special dinner. Bowery Meat Co was a great choice, albeit very pricey, I definitely recommend.

Second time visiting the restaurant and the food was just as great as the first visit. Food was phenomenal - and the ambiance was great (not your typical steakhouse atmosphere). Ate family style with meatballs, zucchini carpaccio, burger, salmon, and of course - Chateaubriand for two. Everything tasted great - and they also have great cocktails that compliment the food. Would definitely be back for a third visit!

Only knocked off a star because the service wasn't on par with the first visit. The waiter was not very attentive and barely came around the table to see how we were doing.

Expensive, but so, so good.
We had the octopus which was so well balanced and had an incredible texture, duck lasagna (9/10 -- could be a little too salty for people who don't REALLY like salt) but the duck was so tender, and the 20z ribeye that was super good. ALSO, the cast iron cookie is ridiculous. Seriously ridiculous. Get it, please.

A very strong steakhouse, from my experience.

The steak:  75% of a serious steakhouse's grade should be based on the steak.  Starters and desserts and sides are nice, but nobody should be choosing a steakhouse based on the quality of their lasagna or their pie.  You choose a steakhouse because you think they have excellent steaks.  I'm happy to report that Bowery Meat Co cooks an *excellent* steak.  

We ordered the Chateaubriand (for 2) and found it excellent.  Cooked to a very nice medium rare, it was so tender you could cut it with your fork.  Excellent prep, meat quality and overall flavor.  I was very happy with the steak.  I'd definitely recommend coming if you're looking for a quality cut of steak.

We also had the salt + pepper fries (relatively normal fries, but good), the charbroiled octopus (succulent, packed with flavor), the zucchini carpaccio (fresh and light, very tasty) and for dessert the Key Lime pie (standard KLP, but pretty good).

Odds and ends:  There is a bite-sized hors d'oeuvre and a bite sized dessert brought out.  Despite having a reservation we had to wait 15 minutes past our reservation time.  Room is somewhat loud due to acoustics.

It's weird to me that this place isn't packed every night. Some of the signature dishes are expensive, but this is really, really good food.

Most recent visit, we got the meatballs and steak tartare to start, followed by the duck lasagna, cheeseburger, and filet mignon. Both appetizers were great, especially the meatballs, and while I thought the filet was very good, it was the other two that really stood out -- the burger is one of the better ones in the city, and the duck lasagna is absolutely outstanding. I'd like to try some of their other steak dishes at some point, but it would be hard to go back and not get that lasagna.

Overall, really excellent food for not-unreasonable prices, depending on what you get. (We haven't gotten the most expensive dishes, so I can't comment on those yet.)

One of the best dining experiences I've had. I got the filet, yes it's pricey but it was huge, delicious, and totally worth it. My friends split the tomahawk ribeye. Just seeing that steak served was an experience. We had a couple bottles of wine, perfect complement to the meat. This is definitely a great and not a regular outing but it's definitely a place I'd go back to for another special occasion.

This is one of my favorite steakhouses in the city. The food is amazing. My partner started off with the broiler oysters and the foie gras both of which were amazing appetizers. The oysters are a bit rich an decadent so you definitely have to split the order with someone. For our main course, we had the chateaubriand for two which was excellent. It is served in a rich mushroom sauce which really isn't even needed because the steak is cooked so well. The Brussels sprouts served on the side are great. However, the potatoes are a bit bland. The only reason this review is four stars and not five stars is because the service is incredibly slow. I had to continuously call for my waiter during dinner service as she rarely checked up on our table. However, the food is so good I would definitely go again.

They seem to really like salt. 

We had the cauliflower steak for starter which was way to salty. 

Then to their credit my ribeye steak was excellent but the fries on the side was way to salty. 
My girlfriends burger was so salty that she couldn't finish it. 

So a very disappointing meal for us. We expected so much and instead of so much great we got so much salt.

I wish I could give this place 5 stars but I feel like the host was a bit annoyed that we were 9 minutes late to our reservation. My reservation was at 9:15 PM and the resturant was not busy at all. The host did not smile and I saw she puts some coats away for others and did not offer to take ours. My boyfriend and I were both dressed up, after coming from a broadway show. I wanted to surprise him to somewhere special for our birthday/early anniversary since he's a huge fan of steakhouses. I should've said something to the host or waitress but usually I'm always asked if were celebrating an occation. We were checked in on roughly every 10 minutes asking if our food was okay and if were comfortable. They were really great about clearing things out of our way once finished. 

Food was really great! I do reccomend to go to this place and to make a reservation. We ordered Broiled Oysters, Filet Mignon, and Prime New York Strip!

I'd give this place 3.5 stars if I could..

The restaurant itself is beautiful. Very dark, romantic and nicely decorated. The food was a hit or miss.

We ordered the baked clams, grilled octopus, a sirloin and a salmon. The clams were absolutely amazing. The grilled octopus was overly salty. The sirloin was honestly just par and the salmon had an interesting horseradish flavor but still too salty..

We had to return our soda 2x because it came flat. I guess I just expected more from this place..

Lively modern steakhouse that serves great cuts.

Had the Florentine and Chateaubriand for the table. The mushrooms are one of the better sides I've had at a steakhouse. Wine list is extensive but not cheap, with some great hard to find selections(JF Ganevat) from lesser known areas(Jura, for one).

I really wanted to like this place. Overall, the service and ambiance were great, but the food was just okay. It was definitely now worth what they charged. The appetizers and desserts were good, but the steaks were very underwhelming. For $60 a piece, I was expecting to be blown away. I have had way better steaks for had the price. The meat was cooked well, but both our steaks were very fatty and under seasoned. For a $200 meal, I was very disappointed and will most likely not return.

Friends of mine were at the Bowery Meat Company last September and were treated very nicely and promised to return in November which we did on the 17th. Our waitress was fantastic, and we were treated very nicely by the attractive hostesses. Again, I would rate this just a bit short of the other pricey steakhouses, but the food was suburb. They do throw in sides that the other steakhouses do not do. I would come here with friends. Great place to take a date. Were thinking about returning in 2018.
Real time review.  First course bacon chop.. good.. but completely sold as nice piece of bacon... really just a nice pork chop

Great ambience and doting service.  Dishes were generally a bit salty and the bacon chop doesn't taste like bacon - it's a pork chop.  Duck lasagne and broiled oysters shouldn't be missed, but, if you care, pay attention the vintage on the wine.  Ehem - at this level the sommelier should tell me and I shouldn't have to catch them that it's wrong.

Outstanding Tomahawk Steak cooked perfectly. Had the Octopus app and Brussels Sprouts side, both awesome. Wine a list a bit pretentious and pricey, only Cab by the glass was $25. That's dumb. That aside, would definitely go back.
