Great ambience and attentive staff, matched by an excellent menu. Thoroughly enjoyed the Ricotta appetiser and the Hanger Steak as a main. (Their Sauce Choron was perfection in flavour & texture.) my husband had Shrimp as an appetiser & the Bronzino as a main, while we shared the mushrooms & caramelised onions as a side.

Only two downsides: service - for a Sunday night - felt a bit rushed for my liking; other than that, the sort of mini arancini & Parker Rolls they give you when you sit down we're both a little heavy on the salt.

Definitely going back to try other dishes.

Absolutely fantastic!  All around wonderful experience.   Drinks were great, food was amazing and staff took great care of us.  Loved the Duck Lasagna, the cheeseburger was perfect.  Juicy and perfectly seared on the outside.  Bread pudding and cheesecake melted in my mouth!  Will definitely be visiting again when we return to NYC!

I'm a big fan of large group dining so once I saw that Bowery Meat Company had several big cut options, I knew I had to come!

We started off with a complimentary amuse-bouche of a pesto arancini ball, but where was the bread? Next came the duck lasagna (which we opted for as our appetizer since there were five of us). We ordered the cote de beouf and T-bone as our main with creamed spinach, roasted brussel sprouts, and salt and pepper fries. To end the meal, they brought out complimentary homemade ice cream bites coated in chocolate. 

The star of the night was the duck lasagna! Great flavor, tender sheets of pasta, and lots of duck. The steaks were good but not the highlight of the dinner. As for the sides, the brussel sprout and fries were fantastic! I was a bit disappointed by the creamed spinach (usually my favorite side) as it was basically overly salty wilted spinach sitting in a liquidy cream sauce. I would pass on this. 

The service was stellar. At the start of our night, our waitress brought out a tray of meat and pointed out all the different cuts to assist our order. When we asked about dipping sauces for fries, she ended up bringing out all the sauces they make. Best of all, they fold your napkin and push in your chair, when you leave for the bathroom. It really is the little things. 

Overall, good food, fair prices, and great service. I'm looking forward to coming back to try their appetizers and their signature Bowery steak and cheeseburger!
Great ambient with a romantic feel. The steak presentation is very creative & separates this house from many other places. Will definitely return..

The Tomahawk Ribeye was great. The service was even better. The creamed spinach was really a highlight. The ambiance was particularly nice. The Crispy Duck wings were good. The charbroiled octopus was excellent. Skip the hash brown. The Broccolini was ok. The lady at the next table must have been getting a commission the way she insisted it was amazing.

My meal at Bowery was nothing short of transformative!  The Raclette Burger was perfect for a cold winter evening and super romantic.  The burger transported me instantly to the Swiss alps!  The pickles + fries were also superb.  The ravioli special was equally inspired with generous shavings of tip quality Parmesan and pomegranates in a light cream sauce.  The short rib filling left me entirely speechless.  Words cannot describe how delicious it was.  And then, the piece de resistance  was... the cookie skillet with incredible caramel sauces poured on it at the table!  What a show stopper. I am including a photo.  Thank you for an amazing meal!

Perhaps it is the NY steakhouse that is dead - then again maybe it's just Bowery Meat Market that is DOA...

I suppose that all restaurants in New York have been reduced to the same - get them in, give them the check- model, maybe it's wrong to single out this one. But it was my brother's 30th birthday tonight. We ordered cocktails - only one came on time. We had to cancel the other 3 to accommodate the wine we ordered. Appetizers - only one of three arrived on time. Then two bottles of wine - the 2nd took 25 minutes to come to the table. Only 2 of 4 main plates arrived on time. Then the desert, was the saddest scoop of ice cream I have ever seen, and an underdressed strawberry cheesecake. The price tag - 480$ for 4, and sub par service.... pick another steakhouse..

My group and I had a fantastic experience here. We tried many different cuts of meat, appetizers, and 3 desserts and it was all excellent. The service was A++. Very attentive and friendly staff. I can't wait to come back!
absolutely amazing! Great service and great food the burger it's literally wow! 5 star so worth i.t

Overall, really enjoyed my experience at Bowery Meat Company. Strangely, the things that ended up really standing out for me were the little things. There were little complimentary surprises all the way through the meal that really enhanced the experience: the little buns they start you off with were pure heaven...little puffs of clouds with a dusting of sea salt. The duck lasagna was fantastic but while the idea of using duck in this dish is intriguing, I didn't feel it actually added anything to the dish. But whatever; still delicious...that cheese they used was a standout!  The little Arancini balls were crisped to perfection and the little chocolate covered ice cream balls were a fun end to the meal.  

But let's get down to business and talk about the meat! We ordered the tomahawk for two. The presentation is absolute perfection and so exciting when it comes out to your table! Beautifully cooked. One of the few places that still know what medium rare really means: Slightly red in the center, pink all around.  The char and salt seasoning on the outside was great. BUT, there was a downside: The steak itself was ever so slightly chewy and even a little too lean for my liking. Later I saw the server present the entire meat selection (the ACTUAL meat selection: meaning, the raw steaks spread across a board for your viewing pleasure) to the table next to us after we already ate and I could see that there was far less marbling in the Tomahawk. Perhaps we just chose the wrong cut?  I felt that for the price, I wanted a steak that absolutely melted in my mouth. I have had steaks for half the price (Prime Meats' Steak Frites..get it, you will not regret it!) that did just that. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case with the Tomahawk.  Both the sides we ordered, the broccolini and whipped potatoes, were fantastic but the latter was the standout.  However, I do wish it was served with a little peppercorn red wine gravy or jus to add a little dimension and heat.  

Still, all in all, a very enjoyable meal!  Perhaps next time I will try a more marbled cut of meat to see if that changes my opinion about the steaks here.

I enjoyed my experience at this restaurant. The restaurant was nicely decorated and gets pretty crowded on a Sunday night starting from 6:00 PM. We came at 5:30 PM so it wasn't so bad. The service was alright, it seems like the servers were a bit rushed. 

Anyway, the food was amazing. The duck lasagna was very unique, I've never had a dish like this before. It was cooked nicely and was super flavorful - but I did find it a bit too savory (salty) at the end. There wasn't a lot of cheese in it and the duck was cooked to perfection. The portion is really big and I would suggest sharing this with at least 3 people.

We ordered the Chateaubriand in medium rare. I found the meat a bit too tough for my liking. The two ends of the meat were a bit burnt. I would've liked it more if it was juicier. The meat was already cut for us, so there were about 9 pieces for you to share. We had potatoes on the side and some greens. 

Overall, I would come back again but would probably try some other meat like the T-bone steak.

It was my birthday celebration dinner and at the end they came out with a cake, so it was pretty sweet - thanks to my boyfriend :)

Came here on a Saturday night at 6pm with a reservation. There didn't seem to be much people at the time but it definitely got a lot busier around 7pm-- doesn't hurt to make a reservation before coming. They have happy hour on the weekdays, only for the house cocktail and wines though. Usually the bar cocktails are around $13 and up each--though expensive, they were extremely tasty! The bartender was super attentive asking me whether I liked the drink or not. 

The meat was DELICIOUS! With a party of 4 we all decided to share the Tomahawk ribeye for 2 and the chateaubriand for 2 as well. Though you can order vegetables in the side, these dishes came with veggies so there was no need. Those dishes alone were enough to make all of us full. The meat was so juicy and tender-- they also have their respective sauces. Would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a great steakhouse!

This place reminds me of American Cut.  Average steak that is overpriced but stellar service and decor.

The place is beautifully decored with a nice clean classic look with ample lighting but still intimate.  Noise level is conversational although I thought some of the tables were a tad too close.

The moment I walked in the hostess was friendly and warm, the bartender was attentive and a quick pour and finally the waiter and his staff were on point, five stars for that.

I am perfectly ok with an expensive steak if it is worth and being somewhat of a steak snob after visiting most places I believe in an expensive steak doesn't mean its good and a good steak doesn't mean it's expensive.

Basically a very expensive for an average steak at best.  It's not bad and if it was priced on par I would be ok.  My brother and I both ordered the ribeye; it was cooked perfectly (perhaps a tad too much char if I had to critique) but it was a solid steak...but not at the $60.

Ordered over priced broiled oysters ( I normally order raw but they wanted $20 for four kumomoto oysters...CMON MAN).  The broiled oysters were decent but somewhat drenched in sauce.  

Speaking of drenched we also ordered a side of mushrooms and whatever sauce/cream they used was simply far too overpowering.

At the end of the day, the service and decour does not make up for the overpriced average steak.

Would not return.
Sat at the bar,  Aisha and Stephen are very attentive  always asking how everything was. Food was great and fast service. Really enjoyed my experience, will come back for sure!

Nothing bad to say about BMC - went for a bite on a Friday evening.  We checked in, were seated quickly and our waiter was great. We ordered the ricotta spread, the tomahawk steak for 2, Brussels sprouts and frites. Everything was good. The cocktails were also expertly prepared. So why 4 stars, it's just a little pricey compared to other comparable ny steakhouse.  All in, Id go again, especially for special occasions.

My wife and I dropped by on a Thursday night and used opentable to reserve.  We were a few minutes late but they were able to accommodate us relatively quickly. The restaurant is decorated nicely and the bar area is pretty solid.  The cocktails are very expensive but they are made by experts. The beer list is pretty solid here too. 

The complimentary bread and butter was amazing! They also gave us some complimentary fried rice balls which set the expectations of the meal pretty high. We got an order of duck wings, a  rib eye with shishito peppers, a crab pasta and the patatas bravas as a side.  

Duck wings - how can I order these in bulk for my super bowl party???
The rib eye - served a perfect medium rare with beautifully charred shishito peppers, an absolutely amazing accompaniment to the steak.
The crab pasta - quite possibly the best pasta dish I've had in the past five years. Huge portion, lots of crab and a sauce that didn't leave my mouth coated with cream
The patatas bravas took me back to my time in Barcelona. Twice cooked fingerlings slightly crushed and served with a spicy/creamy sauce.

I wish we had space for dessert but it just wasn't possible. The complimentary salted caramel
Ice cream bon bons at the end were perfect though. I wish I could order a bowl of them :).

Had Saturday evening reservations and were sat on time. The restaurant is broken into two dining rooms. The larger one was very loud difficult to have conversation. We sat in the smaller one by the bar which was much nicer. Service was perfect. I had the bacon chop which was a cross between a piece of bacon and pork chop. Friends all raves about their steaks and the sides were excellent as well. Creamed spinach was best I have ever had
The appetizers were a little on the small and expensive side. A little pricey even by city steakhouse standards but a nice treat

Amazing steaks. Been here over 10 times and was never disappointed. Big fan of their 40 day dry aged tomahawk. As far as Appetizers go the ricotta is a hidden gem. The eggs on eggs, duck wings, and duck lasagna are great go to's

Ambiance and service are both top notch. It doesn't feel like most typical "stuffy" nyc steakhouses. It's vibrant and trendy while being classy and warm.

Instagram: @jeweats

The burger was great, the drinks very strong. Overall a nice place. Very upscale. Bartenders and waiters very attentive and will converse which is a great thing. I did love the fact that if ordering a steak, they bring you a platter of the different cuts. I came here solely for the burger, but may have to come back for the steak

Absolutely amazing steakhouse. Definitely one of my favorites in lower manhattan. I've been here over 10 times and I have not been disappointed in their steaks. I tried their pasta once and that was a big mistake. Stick to the steaks. 

I really like that you get complimentary little appetizers and little dessert bites. The sides are delicious as well. Amazing wine list. Delicious cocktails. The only thing is that the vibe is way too business dinner-ish but hey, that might be your thing.

I've been meaning to catch up on some New York City reviews for a while and thought it would be good to start with one of my favorite bar experiences in the city.  It only does Bowery have a great cocktail program and wine list but, the food game is real tight too. 

I'll start by saying, I'm a bar guy through and through. It's the best way to experience a restaurant if you're traveling solo or with one other. The bar at Bowery is friendly, attentive and proper. I'm a huge fan of their appetizers and any place that serves caviar and torchons are fine in my book! I thought both of the dishes I ordered were really great and came with all the necessary toast points, remoulade, etc. 

The cocktails were also spot on! Try some of the House specials from the list because they know what they're doing.

Meat was good and well cooked. We had the prime to be and the tomahawk. All orders came as ordered and was quite tasty.

The drinks were ok at best. The staff need more training and education on the products. I had to Google the difference between meat and cuts because they couldn't answer my questions. 

Ambiance was pretty. The price was ok for what it is. I'd rather go to Peter lugers.

Came here on a Wednesday night. This is not your typical nyc steakhouse. Their decor is modern with great service. It's a bit slow but it was a busy night. They would literally bring you raw meat for viewing to get a sense of the size and cut of the meat. Now the food: 

- Surf and turf for two: this came with ny strip and huge prawns. The prawns tasted as good as lobster honestly, fresh and nice texture. The steak was nicely done with crunchy crust. I normally like porterhouse more because you get the two different cuts. But this was decent. It comes with spinach. 

- duck lasagna: delicious. We got this from courtesy of the chef. The duck worked, not too heavy with the cheese.

First off the service was impeccable. I will give credit where it's due. Also the decor and ambience is very nice and depending on where you sit can be spacious. However, at those expensive menu prices, I was extremely disappointed with the steak. We ordered the tomahawk rib eye, and the steak was mediocre at best. It was not juicy even though we ordered medium-rare, and the char on it was quite unpleasant even though we like crust. This just tasted burnt in a bad way. Furthermore, everything is extremely salty. From the bread (yes) to every vegetable, just everything is loaded with salt. The subtle questions we asked of the server made him realize we were not exactly pleased, and a manager came over right away to ask us what was wrong and did everything in their power to make it right and make us come back. This was much appreciated and as I said wonderful service, but at the end of the day I don't want someone else to spend as much money on an expensive steak place as we did and come away disappointed hence why I am leaving this review.

Great Vibe when you walk in. Harold Who I am assuming is the manager is there to greet each table. The duck wings are absolutely amazing and also the ricotta cheese with pomegranate was a wonderful surprise . 
We ordered the T-Bone for two, French fries, and creamed spinach all wonderful. This place is a not miss for sure.

I really enjoyed the chips at the bar! This restaurant gives a lot of freebies. We were given mini rice balls and a piece of their duck lasagna before our entrees came out. We ordered the aged 2 steak for two. I like how the steaks came with a sauce and sides. We ordered an extra side of mash potatoes and creamed spinach. The sides were expensive and small. I probably would have rather tried an appetizer. The food was good but a little salty.
Amazing food. Not a fan of the 120-day dry aged Cote de beouf (compare to an over ripe cheese). The service and everything else we had was top notch. I'll definitely go back to try some other things

Ehr ma gerd!!!!! This was amazing. I called about a reservation for 1, they said to come on in and sit at the bar or the high tops. Every interaction I had with anyone  was so very pleasant! I was seated immediately, ordered my meal, they gave me some kind of parm cheese ball but I'm hard of hearing so I don't know what it was called. They game me rolls, fluffy and delightful! I ordered the Bowery steak and it was delicious. I didn't wait long for my food, about 10 minutes max. My waiter was amazing, again the staff was great! Thank you for such an amazing experience!

I would rather give this 2 1/2 stars, but since I can't I shall round up.  First, let me just say our waitress was excellent.  She was kind and patient, explained things when we had questions.  I wasn't happy with the glass of wine I had selected (only a small tasting but still) and so she gladly brought me a different one.  The service was very quick and efficient.  The whole waitstaff was great.  

The wine selection.  I ordered a glass as I had a headache and wine and headaches not really friends.  Thus, I can't speak to their bottle list, but the by the glass list was disappointing I felt.  I am no wine expert, but there wasn't much for choices.  I tried 3 of their reds..the malbec (my husband's), the Pinot Noir (the initial tasting), and ultimately had the Syrah which wasn't bad.  But none of them blew me away.  

As to the food, well this left a lot to be desired.  Some of the things were great...the meatballs, the duck wings, the duck lasagna samples they brought out when the kitchen was backed up..very good.  BUT...we came for the steak. I need to say that I grew up in the Midwest and have been to my fair share of steakhouses so while I am no professional I am not some rookie who orders my steaks well done and asks for steak sauce (sorry if you do this :)  hahah j/k to each his/her own).  My husband and I ordered the T-bone, another couple ordered the Chateaubriand, another the bone in Filet Mignon, and a few others in our party ordered the bone in Ribeye.  I found the steaks (I sampled the others) to be very lack luster...not a lot of flavor, kinda dry.  Overall just really disappointing...ESPECIALLY for the price.  Mind you...I expect to drop money at a steakhouse. I have no problem doing so.  Last month the same group of friends went to Del Friscos.  Our steaks were alot better and cheaper.  I haven't seen a Peter Luger menu in a while, but I am pretty sure Peter Luger is also cheaper.  So...back to my point...this place charges excessively for what they are offering, not just with the steaks, but with their lack luster sides, and their drink menu. Nothing was bad...it was just meh...take it or leave it kind of place.  If I am going to drop $300 for my husband and I to eat...I want to be wowed not walking out going meh.

That being said...excellent dessert.  We had the cookie skillet..very good.

Whoa, what a happy surprise! I was a craving some steak and a quick Yelp search brought me to BMC. 

I didn't know it would be so dressy, I certainly felt out of place in my sneakers and jeans. But they sat us either way. Our waiter was attentive and made recommendations to us based on what we liked. He even brought out the meat board with all their various cuts. He explained the source and how it would be cooked. After some deliberation we chose:

Cauliflower steak for appetizer
Rib eye
American Wagyu with whipped potatoes

Let me just say this was my first wagyu ever. I didn't know what to expect. Normally I love a ribeye, but you can't have a ribeye follow a wagyu. The ribeye was good, but the wagyu was AMAZING. It was beyond tender, it looked like the meat could barely stay together. The seasoning on both were great but the wagyu stood out. 

The cauli-steak was good too, but probably unnecessary. I would ordered a third steak as an appetizer when I come back in the future. All in all, a really delicious dining experience.

We couldn't decide on a dessert, and we were also impossibly full. But our server was amazing and brought us out a mini dessert on the house. That's the sort of amazing service that really clinched the entire experience for me. 

I can't wait to come back.

Pro tip: sit in the lounge over the main dining room, much quieter!
Wanted to try for awhile. Kinda upset I did. Steaks are average and service is sub par. At the end of the day, the classic steakhouse just works best.

This place had been on my bucket list for a while and I finally got to try it last night. Let's start with the exceptionals- the service, the ambiance and the steak - bone in ribeye, to be more precise. The steak was well seasoned, perfectly medium rare and the aging process definitely gave it its own unique flavor profile. The duck lasagna was good but i would have liked it more without the extra cheese on top. It just doesn't taste right when the cheese is not baked. Guess I'm just a traditionalist when it comes to pasta.
The so so dishes were our appetizers - crab cocktail and the farmers salad. The crab was too watery and the salad's dressing was somewhat boring. 
All in all it was a wonderful evening at the Bowery meat company and I would definitely return. Next time I'm getting the tomahawk ribeye. Just because.

Just back from Bowery Meat Company(BMC), I have to say that I never have such unhappy experience at a steakhouse but BMC. For a steakhouse charges such high price, BMC is very far away from my expectation.  

First, the whole restaurant was packed so every waiter or waitress was busy. Our waiter missed our appetizer and our bread but we were offered two baby lasagna which was charged and after we questioned, our waiter took them off our bill. 

Because our appetizer didn't come, we seat there without any notice until our order came, Tomahawk Ribeye. 

For a steak charging over 150+, it should be awesome or at least tasty, right? However, let me tell you why I don't like their steak. Our Tomahawk Ribeye had a very heavy char flavor with heavy bitterness so you couldn't taste any steak's own flavor or sweet. When we compliant to one of waiters, they said it is char own flavor that we paid 150+ for a char flavor steak?!

In addition, the steak is unseasoned with charred so they offer a sauce which supposed to cover bitterness of char (I guess this is another way to cover it, right?) but it didn't help. 

The lady's room is very dirty and this didn't happen at Del Friscos Double Eagle or Empire steakhouse that I just went couple days ago. I am very disappointed on the both food and service, and won't recommend to any of my friends or yelpers who doesn't like charred at the edges of steaks covering all flavors.

The food definitely looks better than it tastes. The tomahawk was cooked really nicely on the inside and with a good char on the outside, however, the char overwhelmed and the steak lost all flavor. The Brussels sprouts and the potato were good. 

The server was very attentive and asked at the beginning of the meal if I had any allergies, which I do (nuts, strawberry and egg). Unfortunately, he then served me, twice, food that had nuts and strawberry in it. He was super sorry but it could have been bad.

The food is 5 stars starting with appetizers(deviled eggs, beet salad, large shrimp cocktail and salmon poke). Next was our meal.... branzino and steaks are the best ever. The desserts? Just order each one as they're each divine. Dessert menu is 5 stars! Expensive steakhouse prices but this food was memorable and vibe is great. Check in reception welcoming. The food 5 stars!!!

Service 3 stars-a little slow. Our server checked in with us but too many times we were looking for her so that's sub-par Service. Perhaps she had too many tables. The food is that excellent so the service should b too!

After watching a video on youtube with the worth it guys from buzzfeed, my boyfriend and i wanted to try the tomahawk steak so bad! 
we were able to make a reservation online and there were even options for special occasions. 
we were greeted nicely and received our food very fast. 
the quality of the food did not suffer tho. it was very delicious. i gotta say, i've never had a steak that soft and yummy. we will definitely go again next time we visit nyc.

We enjoyed most of the food, but the food didn't justify the price. The potatoes and creamed spinach were good. My fiance had the filet mignon which he enjoyed, I tried the Bowery steak which wasn't anything special. No different then a steak you'd get at a friends wedding. Our waitor overcharged us for our wine. Overall, don't see a need to go back or recommend to friends.
Best lamb chops I've ever had. Excellent service, nice ambiance and great selection of wine. This place doesn't disappoint!

The chef/owner josh was there-schmoozing like a pro. Came to our table and offered us some dishes on the menu. Next thing you know it's on the bill. Scum bag city. Population Josh

On other hand have to hand it to Josh for playing us like that. Almost have to respect. 

If you go get the broiled oysters, but only if he offers it to you
Excellent meat, wine and service.  A great option if you want to go to an atypical steakhouse.

I came here for my boyfriends birthday last Friday and was expecting big things. I called the restaurant before and also noted on my online reservation we were coming for his birthday. We got here and were greeted by a bald waiter who seemed like he was in a rush to get us straight out. He spoke very fast and kept asking if we were ready to order. We ordered 2 cocktails- I had the whippet (titos vodka and grapefruit) which was very good but rather overpriced. We also ordered the bacon to start. Someone brought over the bread which was incredible and complimentary rice balls which were also good. The bacon was flavorful, but rather fatty- I thought there was too much fat. I then ordered the bone in filet mignon and my boyfriend got the ribeye. I got mine medium rare. When the steak came out it was extremely overcooked. The waiter did not come over once to ask how our food was, so I could not even tell him. I sat there not eating it waiting for him to ask, which he did not. I finally waved him down and said it was overcooked. He said to cut in the middle and it would be how I liked it, because the bone cooks the outside more. He did not apologize, or ask if I needed anything else or wanted another one. He just walked away. I didn't do anything else and just did not really eat the meat, however, the manager walked by. He asked how we were doing and I said that my meat was overcooked. He said he would bring it to the kitchen and take the temperature and if it was they would take it off the bill. they ended taking it off the bill, however, I was never offered a new steak or anything. The manager was extremely friendly, but the waiter was rude, did not pay attention to us, and brushed me off when I complained about how my steak was cooked. If you are paying $60+ dollars for a steak, it should be cooked properly and how requested. Although the manager was extremely helpful, the waiter should've been more accommodating. Although I was unhappy my boyfriend did love his ribeye and we also loved the whipped potatoes we got on the side. After the manager took away my steak, the waiter completely ignored us and was even less friendly than the start. We then ordered the cookies and cream ice cream cake which was incredible. the cake part was large with ice cream in between the layers and crumbled cookies on top. they then topped it with fresh melted chocolate. this was delicious and my favorite part. However, I was shocked they didn't bring out a candle or anything, although I had indicated several times it was my boyfriends birthday. Overall, all of the food was pretty good except my overdone steak and the fatty bacon, I just wish the wait staff had been more accommodating and friendly and they had remembered that I had told them several times we were celebrating a birthday.

The positives: service was excellent and helpful, the duck lasagna was a revelation, and the bacon and mashed potatoes were strong side order options.

The negatives: the tomahawk was a letdown. It wasn't worth the hype or the money, although it was a decent steak. It photographs well but that's about it. On a smaller note, the hash brown was pretty bad and the only thing I ate here that I would consider inedible. 

Overall, I would return solely for the duck lasagna. I wouldn't mind trying a different steak but the tomahawk was one-and-done for me.

FOOD POISONING. BE WARNED. When my entire party fell ill from our meal (we all realized we had shared one plate in our appetizer selection that caused all of us to get sick), I called Bowery Meat Company to tell them what had happened - to warn them that this might have been a "bad" dish, and that other patrons might be having a similar experience. The manager said: "No one else had food poisoning, so it's not our fault." 

Great customer service! Seriously! So glad we came here for my birthday, got food poisoning, and received zero apology from the staff.

Lets start with the good:  love the decor and general outlook of the restaurant.  And it stops there.

Lets get to the crux of the issue:  I enjoy my steak medium rare...NEVER have I had to return a steak because it was over cooked at any other steakhouse.  What I was served may as well have been medium well.  Regardless, after bringing this to the servers attention, a manager (I assume) came to the table with a pre-cut steak explaining that this is what a medium rare steak looks like and what I am asking for is a rare.  Errr.....ok mate, sure...if your restaurant defines a medium rare as rare, there's a problem!  

No apologies provided, very curt and really ruined my entire dining experience (last one to finish eating and sides had gone cold).  

Plenty of better, professional know-what-they're-doing steakhouses in the city....these people have a lot to learn.  Not spending a dime at this over priced place again.

Landing a new job requires steak. Thankfully, since it was my boyfriend's new job, he was picking up the tab, though I was tasked with the enormous burden of finding somewhere suitable a couple days in advance for a weeknight celebration. I settled on Bowery Meat Company thanks to its solid reviews (including a Johnny Prime rave, my sanity check for red meat in this town), its close location, and its availability. Deep down, I expected to find it overpriced and overrated, but I have to say Bowery Meat Company passed with flying colors.

It's a very mid-century modern space, like the background for a drunk dinner on Mad Men. Don wouldn't be out of place here, though it was largely couples and small groups of businessmen dressed on the casual side. It wasn't too full and I would expect you could easily walk in on a week night. The atmosphere was still nice despite not having a full house.

The menu starts high and goes higher. Most entrees are in the $50s and up, though you could cobble together a cheaper meal with a burger ($27) or non-meat dishes. Though they have a menu that goes far beyond meat and seem to be leaning away from the classic steakhouse experience, they also specialize in big cuts designed to be shared. We were ready to order but our waiter exclaimed, "You haven't seen the meat platter yet!" 

It's the most effective piece of marketing I've seen-- massive raw cuts exhibited and explained tableside. We succumbed to the machismo and quickly changed our order to the chateaubriand for two ($125), basically a 20oz filet mignon, ordered medium rare.

There was complimentary bread shortly after we ordered, an increasingly rare event in New York, pillowy rolls with a fleck of sea salt and good butter on the side. There were also some complimentary arancini, or fried risotto balls, that were delicious.

Of course, when celebrating, you need oysters and foie. The former come in orders of 4 for $19, naked or dressed with fancy Asian-inflected garnishes. We did kumamatos from Washington with wasabi leaf and lemon. They were good oysters with a complementary but not obscuring dressing, though at a pretty high markup to what you'd get elsewhere. The latter ($25) was awesome, a smooth pate that paired with grilled bread and a quite good citrusy jam. I could make little foie sandwiches forever while ignoring my complicity in animal cruelty.

The main event: the steak. Cooked to the correct medium rare, tender with a gentle chew, and more steak than we were frankly comfortable finishing as two small humans. This was complemented by very solid asparagus and little potatoes, and a wonderful sauce chasseur that tastes dead simple, is probably annoyingly hard to make at home, and that I want to pour over all of my red meat forever. Just great, classic execution that we had no complaints about.

Drinks run expensive as well, and we were served well by pregaming and sipping on a drink each here. My Argentinian Malbec ($17) was a classic fruit-forward example of the form, and though apparently you can buy a bottle for the cost of a glass here, I was so taken with it that I took a picture of the menu for later.

My boyfriend had the mezcal sour ($17), combining both his love of egg white drinks and mine for mezcal drinks smartly as he predicted I would be stealing sips. And steal I did, as it was so perfectly smoky and sweet and I would love to drink this forever. And eat those foie sandwiches forever and pour that sauce on that steak forever. But time marches forth.

At this point, we were stuffed with meat and carbs, and passed on dessert. However, they will give you some salted caramel, chocolate-dipped ice cream balls with your bill, which were positively decadent.

Service was excellent and the meal was appropriately paced. Despite its contemporary leanings, I found this to be a satisfyingly traditional steakhouse experience, and we left happy, though I was a bit more effusive than my boyfriend given I wasn't paying. I would still say that this is a splurge that feels worth it.

Nice upscale dining experience! Convenient layout of the restaurant with plenty of room and decent amount of space between tables. Oysters were on point and so were the other appetizers we ordered. Tasty meats and fish entrees! My favorite thing were the side orders and how well those were prepared. The spinach, asparagus, mushrooms & onions were truly incredible. My only negative comment is that it was too dark for my liking. I would have prefered some more light or maybe candles.

i just have 1 word: Sunday Industry burger special. 
Come for the burger stay for the friendliest staff in the neighborhood.

Sophisticated-chic restaurant with top of line service and style. The service is extraordinarily great and very informative on the cuisine and drinks. Obviously the steak is delicious and the Ricotta spread! ‍

We went to celebrate my daughter's graduation from NYU and it was worth every penny. We had the meatball and crispy duck wing appetizers, both of which were excellent. We ordered three steaks and the veal chop. My bone in ribeye was cooked perfectly and well seasoned. My wife and daughter enjoyed their steaks as well. However my son's veal chop was the real standout. Just glorious. The creamed spinach and whipped potatoes sides were also excellent. For dessert we had a trio of ice creams/sorbets, of which the black currant was exceptional. But the cast iron cookie with ice cream and salted caramel sauce was unbelievable. Just get it.

The service was impeccable. Attentive but not overbearing. The whole vibe was very chill and the place is formal without being stiff.

It was one of the best all around dinners I've had in a long time. Highly recommended.

Fabulous Place - from the minute you walk in the door greeting seating and service were spectacular 
We were celebrating a birthday and they accommodated our seating needs and special requests 
We ordered several appetizers shared and enjoyed each as if we had  been starved  
Our waiter offered drink options and wine choices and a taste of wine when we were not certain
One of  our party had the Pink Moon cocktail which was delight Others had beer and wine selections 
I  had the specialty flavored lemon cucumber soda and had a few because they were that good 
The ricotta Appetizers was extraordinary 
The duck wings were crispy tasty tangy and the marinade component the meat did not overpower it 
The meatballs were especially delicious
We all ordered different cuts for dinner 
Filet, Ribeye Strip steak all were cooked to perfection and as ordered
I had the Bowery Steak and as I usually prefer seafood really enjoyed the cut and flavors of this offering 
Shared  whipped potatoes hash browns and asparagus 

now even after eating all this we moved onto desserts 
having Cappuccino tea and shared a cast iron chocolate chip cookie and ice cream and cheese cake and Dutch apple 
Service was attentive and accommodating old school asking what you need ahead of time and offering options 
At no time did we have to search for help 
Space is mix of old school Steak house dark woods dim lighting and modern design with soft velvet cushioned booths instead of hard cold leather and comfortable space between table so you k who there are other people but you cannot are their food or hear every conversation 
You call skip away into your own private world and be served a delicious and enjoyable  meal
We will definitely be going back and if you want to walk away happy satisfied and please then you should go here as well 
Well done to the GM and team for making the evening an event to be remembered  and shared and praised 
You have GOT IT RIGHT and DID A NICE JOB 
Not too much to ask yet so very hard to find

I came here for my birthday dinner with the hubs and it was really good. We started at the bar with 2 margaritas while waiting for our table to be ready. We had a 9pm reservation but got there about 30 mins early. They margaritas were done well. We were seated within 10 mins, which was a nice surprise as the place was pretty crowded. Our waitress was really nice and attentive, which was great being that this was our first time here. Now for the food: 
The dinner rolls were warm and nicely salted - delicious
We received complimentary Risotto Balls - spectacular 
And complimentary Duck Lasagna - let me start by saying I'm not a big fan of duck but this was amazing
For the entree we both ordered the special Surf and Turf, Filet Mignon with a Lobster Tail and a side of fries - the downside was the filet was a little over done but otherwise fantastic and the fries was enough to feed 4 people. 

While the prices are a little on the higher side it was definitely worth it. I will definitely return!

This is definitely one of the better steaks that I've had in nyc. Got the dry aged porterhouse. It was cooked perfectly, and fairly tasty. I had read comments about it being too much food for 2, but it's not... in fact I could finish it all myself. 

The sides that we ordered (fries and asparagus) were also tasty. Dessert was good too (pound cake with strawberry, which was the special of the day). 

The thing that I liked most about this place apart from the steak is that they had a few complimentary small bites. 

What I didn't like:
-the prices. It's more expensive than other nice steak houses and I don't think it's worth the premium 
-doesn't really have a steak house atmosphere 
-service is weird. We had a bunch of different waiters, instead of an assigned person

Outstanding meal. Three of us got the steaks and one of us got the salmon. All better than great! The sides of spinach and mushrooms were so good too. If you arw looking for this type of meal the BMC cannot be beat!

I am a steakhouse purist, so I wasn't in a hurry to try this place. But when a friend was in town, I decided to give it a go as I'd seen numerous friends on Instagram posing with their chef and a big slab of meat. 

Upon walking in, I was impressed. The room was vibey and the two hostesses were warm, engaging and charming. I then went to the bar and had a very well made martini by an bartender who looked like she'd had one too many Adderalls. Who am I to judge though, especially when the drink was perfect. Seems to be how the industry runs these days, different from when I was a waiter when people would duck off the floor for some marching powder. Moving on...

My pal and I were sat, and the server brought over the cuts of raw meat to explained them. Nice touch. We were starving at this point and ordered. 

The first course came quickly, maybe too quickly as we'd barely had time to finish the drink and order wine. It was OK though and we dived in. We had the $21 bacon and all I can say is, compared to the stuff I've had at Peter Luger for example, this was not very good. It tasted reheated and dry.

Then came the steak which I had ordered rare. It unfortunately was cooked medium. I could've sent it back, probably should have, but didn't want to make the night with my friend about the food, so I decided to just eat this very nice piece of aged beef, ruined by a careless cook. 

I'm sure BMC can be a really great experience, but for me, a steakhouse is supposed to a reliable, dependable place, where at the very least, they get temperatures right. This was not. 

We were also blown away they didn't offer a cheese course. With such a robust wine list, it's baffling they wouldn't keep a few aged cheeses around. 

In summary, I'm not angry at this place, I wouldn't mind going back, but when you're paying upwards of $200 a head, it would be hard to pick this joint over a Keen's or even Del Friscos, which has half the vibe.

A few years in and stronger than ever.  The best steakhouse in the city has gotten even better.  Joining the already great lineup of the Cote de Boeuf, Tomahawk ribeye and T Bone Florentine is the all new Bone In Filet for 2! And just like the late 90's NY Yankees, the core 4 is complete.

I was in the city for the night and wanted to go somewhere where I wouldn't get bullied and rushed in typical NYC fashion. Bowery Meat Company went above and beyond--the meal was outrageously good. Broiled oysters were remarkable and the tomahawk ribeye was picture perfect. It was cooked to perfection and thoroughly blackened. This is a fine example of a steakhouse with a menu that would be almost impossible to recreate at home.

I went with my team to this place. We tried Foie Gras, Broiled Oysters, Filet Mignon, and Lamb chops accompanied by a White French and a Red French (Pauillac). 

The food was very good. Foie Gras could be a bit more tasty. 

The white was okay. But the Red was fantastic. Both were recommended by the Sommelier who sounded well versed with wines on the menu, we just had to tell him the type of wine we were looking for. 

Service was good. We were well looked after. 

4* (not 5) due to the ambience and restroom. The Ambience was alright but not very differentiated. The restroom was clean but basic and someone should keep the wash basins dry. There was water all around.

We went there for dinner with friends last night, our first time. Everything was excellent, perfectly cooked. The salmon and swordfish was great. One friend had a cheeseburger, loved it with a heaping dish of fries. 
Going back soon for sure!

Long story short, went for a black and blue steak. First  one came out beautifully charred but overcooked inside. No biggie, sent it back and the waiter was gracious about it. Next ribeye came out- cooked properly inside but not one bit of char on the outside. I did not try for a third. I know it takes a bit of finesse to get it black on the outside and blue on the inside which is why we chose chef capons place. Disappointed the staff could not pull this off. Total bummer.

We were able to get a last minute reso for 6 ppl at 830pm on a Saturday night quite easily.  It's a modern, chic set-up unlike most old school steak houses and the patrons were mostly a younger mix as well.  

Our dinner started with asparagus salad, farmers salad, ricotta and crispy duck wings. I liked the duck wings in particular. The skin was super crispy and the meat had a discernible flavor of the duck. If I had to pick between the two salads, I would pick the asparagus salad mostly due to the garlic and herb cheese. The ricotta came with perfectly grilled bread and was a hit at the table as well.

For mains, we all shared the tomahawk and lamb chops. Both were executed well but I have to give the edge to the lamb chops because I thought the harissa yogurt was a really nice touch. As far as steak goes, you can probably find better in NY but I think BMC holds their own and adding green onions does bring something different to the table - literally.

Can BMC break the curse that's Extra Place? We will see. This venue has changed hands many times but despite the myriad of good restaurants that have popped up here, no one seems to be able to lock it down.

The restaurant is modern and hip, with great music playing in the background, not something you'd typically expect from a steak house.  I've been to another steak house that was supposedly hip and trendy but the food was lacking. (will not name names, yet...that's for another review) That's where BMC differs, it's a real steak house for meat lovers.  Not the first time I've come here but this time it was for a birthday dinner, party of four, we ordered 2 steaks, some apps and sides.  One was person was a vegetarian, so no meat for her, but we still finished everything we ordered because it was that good.  Miss. Veggie was also left satisfied as well.  Honestly, there was a lot of wine involved, so I cant remember everything we ordered.  But our tomahawk ribeye and Chateaubriand was cooked medium rare to perfection.  Juicy on the inside, and a nice char on the outside.  The ricotta was fresh and creamy, and also we ordered some basic sides creamed spinach and whipped potato, the flavors weren't so basic (in a good way).  My only complaint to the restaurant is BRING BACK THE COTE DE BOEUF.  I miss it so much that I just shed a lone tear down my cheek.

I came here for my boyfriend's birthday. After watching a bunch of YouTube videos of Bowery Meat Company's Josh Capron tout the quality of the meats, I was intrigued. I also read many positive reviews on yelp and opentable.

HOWEVER, the experience was lackluster. I felt like I was at a classier chili's or longhorn. The service was okay. But the food was pretty bad. I ordered a the linguine and crab pasta that tasted sour, over cooked, and contained very little sauce or crab. I later got sick that night.

My boyfriend ordered the bone in ribeye which he found greasy.

Phenomenal meal and dining experience! Ever since I saw BMC listed in an article on this city's best steakhouses, it's been on my list of places to try out for a few months now. I finally got the chance to this past weekend and boy, it was certainly worth it. Super easy to make a Sat evening res for a party of 2 and I was even able to request for a booth (thank goodness we did because the side by side tables would have been tighter on space and not much room for all the food we ordered). Initial service took awhile, but other than that there weren't any issues. Between the two of us, we ordered the steak tartare (very good, huge raw onion flavor going), bacon app (I didn't try this, but apparently it was good), the tomahawk steak for 2 (worth it...the bone itself is only about 3 oz), duck lasagna (some people might find it strange to order lasagna at a steakhouse, but the reviews I had read highly recommended it. I would say go for it, but it's not a dish where you can over-eat in one sitting because it's very heavy and it was more than enough for 2 people that we had to take leftovers home), whipped potato puree side (AMAZING...velvet texture and very smooth), creamed spinach (underwhelming...could skip out on this one), and the oreo cake dessert (a little too sweet, but the frozen ice cream and cake combo was great). Between all that, a bottle of wine, 2 cocktails, tax / tip...the total was about $700. So not exactly the most budget friendly restaurant, but there are other options to order that could make the total cost a little more reasonable. The menu is extensive and they even give you complimentary appetizers (it had pesto, but for those with nut allergies....it's actually okay to consume. We were dubious because of the pesto, but trust me - it's safe to eat!).

I love this place. I've been here several times and have always received a great steak. The decor makes me think hip, midcentury modern. Dark and can be a romantic spot. I love the Pesto Arancini balls they give you for an amuse bouche. They used to give a little cheese and salami plate with prosciutto bread which was amazing. I honestly didn't like my salmon poke appetizer because the fish had a weird starchy after taste. It was way too acidic. That's the only bad thing I had there. I loved the Prime NY strip but thoroughly enjoyed the following: Charred Bauvette was scrumptious, meaty and not too fatty. I wouldn't call it lean but it's a leaner steak. The Bowery Steak was velvety and flavorful, had great marbling as it is shaped into a perfect circle. They also have amazing desserts. I usually don't like steakhouse desserts but they do it up very, very well. I ate the Cast Iron Chocolate chip cookie but it really should be for two people. It's very rich and decedent; it made me so happy. But full. I was painfully full. My husband got the special chocolate cake. It comes out under a chocolate dome and they pour more hot chocolate so it melts then you see the vanilla ice cream on top of the cake. So delicious! If you want a good steak with great ambiance, appetizers and desserts, this is the only place to go. Only steakhouse in the that has it all.

Came here with a couple buddies for dinner. 

The decor looks very modern and masculine. Feels a little like the ambience at quality meats if you've ever been.

We sat down and ordered a few drinks. All the cocktails have very inventive names. I had the my name is Adam cocktail which is made with bitter orange soda. Wasn't as sweet as I anticipated. Tasted a bit like cough syrup but in a good way. I also had the golden calf which is an amazing cocktail that I would highly recommend to anyone that comes here. It's supposedly a type of milk punch whereby they ferment this drink in a barrel with whey protein. The protein gives the drink a nice body you only get in cocktails with egg whites.

We got some duck drumsticks which were delicious and were unmistakably duck. So if you like duck flavor, definitely get this.


The Cote du Beouf was the piece de resistance. Aged for 100 days, it had such an intense beef flavor. Supremely tender. Chef recommended medium which was perfect. We had it with some salad and French fries. Both were perfect accompaniments to the steak.

Everything we had was delicious and the service was likewise fantastic.

The prices are on the high side and we ended up spending a bit over $400 for the 3 of us. Much thanks to our friend who treated us to such an amazing meal. 

This is definitely up there with the best steakhouses in NYC.

I came with my family because Rachel Ray recommended it.. I read the yelp reviews and saw duck lasagna was highly recommended. My hubby and boys got the ribeye steaks. For the price which is comparable to other steak houses in the city, I expected to be on par. It wasn't. My duck lasagna was very salty. Not enjoyable at all. I asked the boys about the steak and they were like it's ok. We go to a lot of steak houses to find the best place for steak and this was not it. It wasnt crowded, very easy, too easy to get a reservation so that should have been a sign. A lot of empty tables. Overpriced meh steak. Service not so good either, waitress seemed very disinterested and spilled water (from some veggies) on my son. We had to ask for more water from busboy (which we waited to ask since he was busy chatting with the waitress) And he kept refilling water from across the table sticking his arm on our faces, it's really not that hard to go around to fill the glasses. Especially since he is not busy. Spend your money elsewhere. Decor was nice. Modern style steakhouse decor like quality meats. Won't go again.

The steak and food in general were probably worth 4 stars (though the price was also high). I didn't go for the ambiance though - I guess some people might be into the loud music and general club vibe but I had imagined a more subdued steakhouse feel.

Elegant ambiance, tasty steaks and other foods with adequate service. Pricing fair for food but wine list spans to outrageous( the 1-2000$ bottle. Ordered per sommelier recommendation $120 Bordeaux which was fine  but nothing spectacular or complex as promised. Came here as part of my ongoing quest to find the best cote in NYC. The search continues but this place was good.
Came for my birthday last night and overall pleasant experience. Waitress was present with adequate service. Sommelier most attentive.
Shared apps of broiled oysters, squash carpaccio and duck wings. All inventive well seasoned prepared and delicious.Not the most lovely plating- very comfort styling . Mains -cote de boeuf, single rib eye and lamb chops. Table shared mashed potatoes and broccolini. Cote ordered rare -not bloody enough for my taste but rare enough to be officially labeled rare  but well seasoned char on exterior. Would like to have tasted more grill.Not enough marbling for this price point($120) and did not like the cut steak prior to serving instead of at the table. Lamb chops a bit gamey for my tastes but dinner partner enjoyed. Rib eye enjoyed but a lot of gristle fat on surround. Mashed potatoes buttery deliciousness but too liquid. Broccolini under cooked and not enough grill or garlic. Dessert shared carrot cake and s'mores. Carrot cake one of the best I have ever had - light not too sweet with lovely accent of airy citrus cream. S'mores not very good. To be fair I don't love s'mores anyway but my dinner mates do and it was thumbs down all around. Uninspiring milk chocolate ice cream, inadequate melted marshmallows, unexciting milk chocolate drizzle. Only good thing was graham crackers.
Overall would come back here for apps dessert and cocktails. Mains were fine but for this price point I need more than fine

Very Elegant atmosphere, and delicious steak! Service is also great with servers being very knowledgeable of different types of meats and great wine pairings. Definitely come for the steak, everything else just adds to the great experience.

Been here multiple times and each time I want to go back again..its that good. Its pricey but satisfies the carnivore in me. We usually order 3 shareable cuts for 8 ppl.. My faves are Tomahawk and the 100 day aged house cut.

We had the 100 day aged Cotes de Boeuf for 2.  The meat was exceptionally flavorful and was delicious with or without the bearnaise sauce that accompanied it.  I enjoyed the food and service here much, much more than my experience at Nusr-Et at a fraction of the price.  The sommelier, Harold was especially knowledgeable and friendly.  We definitely will return for future meals at this fine establishment.

I came here with my wife for my birthday, and the service and food were great.  

The cocktails were excellent... I had the Solo Giggolo (don't ask), girlie color and glass but it was very good.  

We had the Grilled Neuske Bacon and Eggs & Eggs (deviled egg) for appetizer... the bacon was "eh", but the devil's egg was yummy.......

For entree, we ordered the 40oz Tomahawk Ribeye Steak for two.  I asked for medium rare, and every single slice was perfect.  The Romesco sauce was good, but the steak was perfect on its own and I preferred it that way.   

Overall, great experience, and I would definitely recommend Bowery Meat Company to anyone looking for kick !@$% steak.

Fantastic! 

Here from southern Cali for work (& we have some spectacular steak houses)... place is decorated very male/traditional and no white linen which I loved. Notorious BIG was playing when we sat- what's better then that? Colleague and I had a cocktail then duck wings. For me, nothing to rave about. But the dinner! He has the Bowery signature steak and I had the salmon. Both exceptional! I cut a piece of his steak with my fork so I could try (& he ordered it med rare to Medium). I've never had salmon with horseradish, and if you're a fan of a nice piece of beef with some horsey sauce... do not let the salmon detour you! Incredible. Service wasn't over bearing and all over you while you're trying to eat/have conversation. When I visit again, I'll be back.

The food is 4 star, the service is 2 stars..All the food was excellent, our steak was delicious and the duck lasagna was absolutely amazing.  The service was just AWFUL!  I ordered a drink and it took 2 reminders to get it after a half hour.  Then it was delivered without my husbands beer.   My husband went to the bathroom and one of the busboys folded his napkin and put it on the table, another busboy came over and took the napkin off the table, folded it up and placed it by the water pitchers.  THEN, he took my husbands USED napkin and was using it to wipe off other tables!!!!  We got our dessert and we had no silverware, no napkin.......at which point we asked for our check and left.  The most frustrating dining experience and it ain't cheap for that kind of service!!!

Do not waste your money here. Very mediocre and over priced food. We had the rib eye and foie Gras appetizer. The foie gras toast came with cold bread not toast and the foie gras had almost no taste and was served with a too salty jam. The cheeseburger was small and had almost no cheese and for $30 was not worth it. The rib eye was fine, nothing special. However what really made the experience not worth it was the terrible service. Our waiter appeared disinterested when we had questions, never offered the wine list until much later and did not answer our questions about which steak we should order. Additionally we went here for my husbands birthday and I made a note of that when I made the reservation. At no point did anyone wish him a happy birthday or make him feel welcome. Very disappointed in the experience if you're looking to celebrate a special occasion go elsewhere.
The food was just AMAZING! My husband and I still talk about how delicious and flavorful the oysters were and nothing compares. The steak was so juicy!!!

Really enjoyed the vibes of this place. Came by the other night for a date night and the food was really good. The steaks were well crafted and flavorful but definitely pricey (what you'd expect from a steakhouse). I also tried the cheesecake when I was here. I would probably skip on this next time, just a typical NY cheesecake. I would come back next time to try some of their appetizers.

Great steakhouse! Definitely a fan of this place. The only reason why I didn't give 5 stars is because I ordered a bottle of wine and literally took 15ish minutes. Someone forgot not sure what exactly happened but I was a little annoyed. BUT the general manager came by and gave us a free ricotta appetizer which was nice. The food was amazing and the service was great. 

Things I ordered: 
- Ricotta: Pomegranate Seeds, Crispy Rosemary, Sea Salt, Chili, Honey, Grilled Bread (must get!!!) 
- Broiled Oysters: Garlic, Romano Cheese, Bread Crumbs, Parsley (must get!!) 
- Maine Lobster Ceviche: Cara Cara, Cucumber, Avocado, Cilantro, Leche de Tigre (its okay, I wouldn't get it again)
- T-Bone Florentine: 40oz, 40-Day Dry Aged
- Tomahawk Ribeye: 40oz, Market Onions, Romesco Sauce
- Caesar Salad
- Patatas Bravas

Happy Halloween NYC. Most of the dishes we ordered were really good. My favorite dish is Bowery steak for sure. The meat was very juicy and tender. Oreo cookies cake was fantastic. Definitely, we will come back another time :)
Our steak was horrible full of fat, and the hand cut fries scraped from the bottom of the fryer. Ricotta cheese appetizer was ok. I don't think I'm coming back any time soon.

Came here for my GFs birthday last night. They reached out to me the day before to confirm my reservation and asked if I needed any special accommodations. I requested a candle to come out with dessert and they said OK. However, the candle did not come out with dessert which was disappointing and annoying.

This place is what I would call an upscale steakhouse. The ambiance is elevated to a more fancy version of your typical NYC steakhouse. After coming in and being greeted by the hostess we were seated in probably the worst seat of the house all the way in the back corner by a wall. I would expect a better seat for a special occasion and a reservation a month in advance. We moved to a slightly better seating situation at the front of the restaurant but still this was annoying.

The food is priced around 20% higher than your other NYC steakhouses. My GF ordered the Bowery Steak and I got the ribeye. I was expecting the steaks to exceed my expectations due to the premium pricing but they did not. They were cooked to medium rare but lacked salt and just was not as tender as they should have been. The highlight of the food was probably the creamed spinach which was packed with flavor and did not taste like mush. The chocolate chip cookie in a pan was also amazing but the sour note was it did not come with the candle I requested for my GFs birthday!

I am glad I got to cross this place off the list cause it was highly recommended. In all the service was OK and the food was forgettable. It is overrated and overpriced in my opinion. I will not be coming back or recommending this place.

This place used to be good, and although the service is still excellent, the food leaves a lot to be desired. My wedge salad was good, not great, being overly salty. The steak was cooked well on the inside, however the outside was completely charred, and the creamed spinach tasted like a mix of too salty and like it was made with heavy cream that went bad. Used to be a great restaurant, last two times have made it so I won't be back.

Was amazing dinner, the steak one of the best than i never tested!! Amazing!! My wife and i went there for our anniversary. Like i said was amazing, the home courtesy was a croquettes from Spain and was it really really good, the steak was a little expensive but worth it!

It was a cold wintery night, one filled with snow, wind and my hungry tummy. I ventured through the streets surrounded by a chorus of car horns honking and lovers holding each other tight to fight off the cold. I was a man on a mission... to banish the hunger that had taken over me. Each step brought me closer and closer to an oasis of savory meats and all sorts of salacious appetizers. That oasis... is Bowery Meat Company!

Upon entering Bowery Meat Company one is greeted with the scent of deliciously, painstakingly perfectly seared steak. It's as if the gods came down from the skies to greet you and your belly. I exchanged a welcome glance with the hostess and was brought to my table of 9 with coworkers in tow. We quickly drew our attention to the drink menu and began to quench our thirst with libations from the bar. I enjoyed the sweet yet bitter taste of my Manhattan (on the rocks) and poured myself a deep glass of Malbec.....

Then it happened..... we began to order... fast and furious... like a gazelle running through the sanguine deserts of Africa! We started with a gracious helping of oysters that were expertly grilled and seasoned. We realized immediately, we were more than hungry clients... nay... we were ROYALTY! The cast of characters at the restaurant that served us were excellent, providing smiles and ample pours of wine and whiskey when necessary. 

Next up were the appetizers! The food came in like a frenzy of flavor.. first there was the foie gras parfait.. which was perfectly accompanied by slightly toasted bread. PERFECTION! 

Suddenly there was a gust of wind outside and a chill came over the table...then like magic.. the true appetizers arrived... It was as if Dionysus, the god of wine himself, was providing us these ample morsels of deliciousness. Grilled Neuske Bacon! BOOM! Bitter Greens Caesar Salad! BOOM! Two Cheeseburgers cut 4 ways! BOOM! and... the best of them all... DUCK LASAGNA FOR TWO! Words will not effectively describe the pageantry of food that was displayed on the table and ultimately... in our bellies..

A lull then came over the table... but we... were...not.. finished! The entrees came in to tear into our hunger like vultures attacking their weakened prey. Tomahawk Ribeye?? Ya damn right we had that.. oh and how about some T-Bone Florentine.. sure why not? Both steaks were perfectly medium rare, pink in the middle, but seared on the outside to perfection! Even Zeus himself would've shed a tear... The sides were plentiful, potato puree/mash, mushrooms, brussel sprouts.. BOOM!

Finally, it was dessert time... and we jumped in as if we were children jumping into a chilled pool on a warm August day. The Cast Iron Chocolate Chip greeted us like a warm hug on a Christmas morning... and the S'mores Sundae was like reuniting with a long lost friend after years apart... but the real star of the show was the Bread Pudding. Deserving of it's own Medal of Honor... it was the one moment of the meal when the table truly got quiet. Not a sound was heard, just the slight chomping of the deliciousness that was on display. 

So in a nutshell... Bowery Meat Company is great! The service is awesome and the food was fantastic. The chef is phenomenal and even came out to say hi! Go there now!

Found this on Yelp, and it did not disappoint. Went here for my Fiancée's Birthday with a group of friends and we were very pleased with the attentiveness of the wait staff and the quality and selection of food. Hands down some of the best steak we had. The waiter was so cool that he even gave us the chocolate chip cookie dessert on him for her birthday. Would highly recommend.

I want to say that it's rare for me to give 5 stars to any restaurant because I eat out a lot since I don't cook but this place deserves more than 5 stars!

The whole team at Bowery Meat Company gave me the best dining experience I've ever had. The service alone gets 5 stars - the hostess was super friendly as soon as I walked in. Lindsey, my waitress, was absolutely top notch. Her suggestions were spot on and she was very attentive the whole time I was there. I think I was there for about 2hrs eating dinner and reading my book.

The chef and the whole kitchen team also did an amazing job with all the food I ordered and didn't order :)  every dish had so much flavor that it was so difficult to not clean every plate but I had to save room for my next course or courses in this insistence...lol

There's not a single thing I would change about my experience tonight at BMC. I just wished I lived in NY so that I could go back whenever I wanted.

Wow. This place was amazing from start to finish. We were greeted warmly when we walked in and the hosts were very friendly while they fixed our table (we ended up having 1 less person than expected). Our server came over soon after we were seated to get us started with drinks and dropped off risotto pesto balls to snack on while we perused the menu. He brought over all the cuts of meat on a board, rather than just talking about them, which I think is a really nice touch.

We ordered a bunch of apps (the bowery plateau, crab legs which were a special, duck wings, broiled oysters and steak tartare) and the server recommended we add in the duck lasagna as a mid-course. The food runner even portioned and served the lasagna (another nice touch). For the main course we ordered 2 family-style steaks (prime rib and Côte De Boeuf) and the lobster, plus creamed spinach, brussels sprouts, shishito peppers and all the potatoes. That was the perfect amount of food for 8 people. All the food was delicious, cooked well and delivered timely. It felt like there was a constant flow of food, without feeling overwhelmed. 

Our server was Jonah; he was great. He made good recommendations and kept our glasses full, while being friendly and attentive but not hovering. He made our experience that much better. This was one of the best overall dining experiences I've had in NYC.

Went for a holiday dinner with two friends. Excited to try Bowery for the first time. Wonderful menu. Ordered apps to share. Our waiter Steve was friendly and knowledgeable. We loved the apps and moved on to entrees. I ordered a  wagyou steak. One of my friends ordered a different type of wagyou. When my steak arrived I noticed it was a strange shape, not uniform, possibly an end cut. It was incredibly tough on first bite. I cut two more pieces hoping it might be less tough a bit further in. Not the case. I tasted my friends steak. A uniformed cut, tender and delicious. I told the waiter that it was tough and he pleasantly offered to take it away and replace it with a different type of steak. That was fine with me. I didn't mind waiting for another one to be cooked. Five minutes later a manager named Moe approached the table and quite abruptly informed me that the kitchen has determined that I had eaten too much of the steak and he would be charging me half price in addition to the cost of the replacement steak! I couldn't believe it. I manage a restaurant myself. I would never approach a customer in such a tactless manner. Regardless that I really had only eaten a few bites it was really poor form and I told him that I felt as such. When he realized that I was offended he backed down and said I would only be charged for one steak. Moe is completely unprofessional and should not be trusted with public relations in an otherwise lovely upscale establishment. On the other hand Steve's table-side manner helped us enjoy a special holiday meal somewhat soured by unpleasant management.

One of my favorite places in the city! Every time I go to Bowery Meat Company, I know exactly what to expect. The atmosphere is amazing, the staff is knowledgeable, and the food is delicious. Always a hit!

BMC is one of the greatest steakhouses that serve aged cuts in NYC. I always come here, it's always great food, service is very consistent and attentive and the vibe is great. The establishment is decorated very simple unlike it's competitors, it's a very simple yet sophisticated restaurant (not too fancy which i love) dim lit, small table restaurant in SoHo. The appetizers, we love the meatballs you get two in an order but we always order and extra piece because they're delicious. My go to items on their menu is definetly the dry aged cuts, heavy marbled, thick cut A5 wagyu grade cuts are always my favorite. We always go for the Tomahawk and their burgers, it's to die for, the burgers are nice and juicy dry aged beef with raclette cheese and the tomahawk is crispy outside and soft inside,it melts in your mouth. Two things to note,  I'm not a big salt fan, the rolls that come on the table and the fries that come with the burger are extremely salty and we did let our server know. Considering the competitors down the block our bill was worth every penny we paid, not cheap nor expensive just a little moderate.Skip the dessert it's too overpriced there are better options down the street. Make sure to use public transportation or uber to get here, there's very little parking in the street. Overall if you're looking for great cuts in a small tiny steakhouse, this is the best bang for your buck in the city.
Amazing service and fantastic menu. Big thanks to Alexandra for making our birthday celebration the greatest. Highly recommend this menu and atmosphere. Thank you, BMC!

Been looking forward to visiting this establishment since November...of 2017.  My now fiance, then boyfriend, and I had been planning a Christmas vacation to NYC for over a year.  While getting here to the city and getting settled in the hotel was like a Greek Tragedy, the much hyped visit to Bowery Meat Company was straight out of a fairy tale.  

We showed to the restaurant a half hour early and were very grateful they were able to accommodate us.  We were sat in the back of the restaurant and immediately were quite enthralled with the ambiance of the restaurant.  The colors and wood walls really felt homey and inviting.  The staff were already aware of the celebration of our engagement and were coming around to the table wanting to know more about Tyler and I.  

Our server came several times during the meal and delivered small portions of some of their most popular menu items, as well as items not usually seen on the menu.  We were given samples of their risotto balls, which you would think would be heavy, but it was light and fluffy with a nice saltiness adding to the flavor.  We were given rolls with fresh butter.  Now, when the rolls knock your socks off...it sets the stage for a great meal.  The rolls felt like they would melt right in my mouth.  Next, we were brought a sample of Chef Capon's Duck Lasagna.   Now, let me tell you, I am not a fan of Lasagna, like...at all.  Never have been.  However, I was eager to see why this item was so popular and...OMFG!  This item blew me away.  It was soft, moist, flavorful, and came with shaved cheese and a fresh romesco sauce.  The romesco sauce was the key to the whole dish as it was so light but the flavor profile made the dish phenomenal.   Me and my fiance wanna return just for a meal portion of the Duck Lasagna.

For our dinner, yes the samples were plentiful, but it was not yet time for the Main Event.  We got the 40 day dry aged 40oz tomahawk rib eye.  And...just....wow.   perfect medium rare, succulent, juicy, with the right amount of char and seasoning.  We got their whipped potatoe puree as out potatoe side and it was great.  For a vegetable side we got their flash fried brussel sprouts that they finish with a citrus vinaigrette which absolutely blew both of us away.  As it was our Anniversary and we were celebrating our engagement the manager Mohammad, said our dessert would be on the house.  Even though we would have loved to try them all, we were so stuffed from the meal and only got their house Bread Pudding to share.  The bread pudding was presented in a casserole dish fresh from the oven.  Cooked with pecans, apples, and spices , it was the perfect complement to our fantasy meal.

I want to give a special shout out to Mohammad, who actually pulled a chair to our table and sat with us for 10 minutes.   We talked of food, life, love, and all things NYC.  He really went out of his way to ensure that this meal would be really special and it delivered from start to finish.  I cant compliment this visit enough.  If you want, fantastic food, decor, and an experience to write home about then you need to visit Bowerys Meat Company. 

10 out of 5 stars!

I had tried to get reservations at some of the bigger name steakhouse's in town like Del Frisco's, Keens, and Delmonico's but was unable to do so with less then a months notice and around the holidays. So I had done some research and the same restaurant kept popping up on the different websites I was checking for good NYC steakhouses, Bowery Meat Co. I called and was lucky enough to snag the first reservation at 530 on a Saturday night. The service was absolutely wonderful, the wait staff was incredibly helpful throughout the night. When it came time to order they brought out a large platter of all the different cuts of beef they sold and explained each one. All of the beef was beautifully aged and had wonderful marbling. We decided to try the 100 day aged "cotè di boefe" which was their signature steak for 2. Before I get to that, we also ordered the duck wings with the soy/honey glaze and cucumber salad along with the BMC Meatballs with polenta. The duck wings were perfectly cooked, nice and crispy on the outside and juicy and tender on the inside with the glaze being perfectly proportioned and not too sweet. The meatballs were incredible, so savory and rich. You could tell they used good cuts of beef. The polenta was also cooked perfectly and paired well with the meatballs and red sausage they were cooked in. The cotè di boefe was cooked medium-rare and was delicious. It literally melted in your mouth, and the flavor was wonderful. It didn't need any clarified butter or the different sauces they offered. As for sides we got the sautéed wild mushrooms and the sour cream and onion hash browns. Both were great choices. For dessert we topped it off with their signature S'mores sundae which was incredible I must say with the toasted marshmallow. We will absolutely go back again. However be prepared to spend some money! BMC can definitely hang with all the larger more popular steakhouses in NYC. Don't be afraid to travel off the beaten path and give this place a try, you won't be disappointed!

One of the best steaks I've had in long time. I'm from the south and  I love meat and seafood.

My family and i decided to try some duck wings, oysters and cocktail shrimp to start off. They were extremely tasty and did not disappoint. We all decided on ordering the 2 tomahawks that were available for our entrees. One was 40 day aged and the other 100 days. We had ordered both at medium and it came out all pre cut which was fantastic. The quality of meat was on par for american wagyu and the service was exceptional. I will be back when I am back in town. This place is a hidden gem if not already discovered by New Yorkers.

Another great meal at Bowery. Opted for the burger (off the menu now, unfortunately). Delicious. As were the apps and the sides, especially the meatballs and Brussels sprouts.
