This was an abysmal experience. We had a party of 5 celebrating a milestone birthday and couldn't have picked a worse place to host it. 

We were seated at some back room table (fine - we understood we're a group) next to a table so loud, the table next to them actually asked them to keep it down. Staff did not address. Apparently it's cool to treat this place like a frat. 

Next up, we ordered mostly wine and 2 cocktails. Nothing complicated...and yet the appetizers, ordered AFTER drinks, came out first??? Are these just sitting under a heat lamp?

I ordered a final glass of wine as were finishing up and it took 30 minutes because "nothing was chilled." No one on staff is qualified to suggest an alt recommendation, let alone let me know what was taking so long?? By the time it finally materialized, I didn't want it. 

Finally, we had to ask 3 separate times for the check.  Our party spent over $170 EACH for the most expensive, regrettable dinner any of us ever had.
Service was good,  however, the food was I would say average. You can definitely find better food, especially for that price.
Very good meat, the Cesar salad was great even deserts was delicious. One thing need reservations

The food, service, and ambiance were great! I'm just taking one star off for the higher prices.

Jumbo shrimp cocktail - The jumbo shrimp were fresh and plump, but it does only come with 4. 

Broiled oysters - These were unique and tasty! The herbed bread crumbs added nice flavor and texture. This was one of my favorite appetizers and I'd definitely recommend!

Poached pear & butter lettuce salad - This was my other favorite appetizer! The ingredients all complimented each other so well, making for a flavorful but light and refreshing salad. 

Mac & cheese - Good but not super memorable.

Duck lasagna - This was such a unique entree, with a good balance of duck, pasta, and cheesy sauce. The duck comes shredded and was mostly tender. I guess the way it was baked made some of the pasta and duck pieces on the crispier side, which added nice texture but wasn't my favorite. It's a big portion that serves up to 6 people. 

Sides - All of the sides were very good! My favorites were the mushrooms, Brussels sprouts, and crispy fingerling potatoes with truffle oil and cheese.

Valentine's Day 2024. The worst steak house I ever been to in New York City. The only positives about the experience were the decor and service. Walked up at 5:00 PM for our reservation (the only time available, a month in advance), to find the doors were locked. We waited outside for a few minutes and then they let us in. So they were late to open the restaurant to begin with. Sat down and they were absolutely blasting music from Django Unchained, Pulp classical Spanish music, and then peppering in country love songs. I've never noticed music in a restaurant being off putting until this experience. Ordered an appetizer of lobster Mac and cheese.  This was the best thing we had, but still extremely underwhelming and small. Ordered Filet mignon for the entree and it was extremely chewy and cold. Also ordered The fingerling potatoes and they were dry and had no flavor. For being a steakhouse and an expensive one at that, this was the most underwhelming flavor experience I have EVER had. After an hour, there were only around ten people in a restaurant that could potentially seat at least 75. No idea why they didn't have any other reservations. The manager came over to talk to us about the food and I almost spoke up if it wasn't for the fact that all the staff was standing on the side of the floor looking at us, taking pictures of the environment and it was so dead inside that all ten people in the restaurant could've heard me. For the record I am 27 years old and I've never written a yelp review in my life but I felt so unsatisfied that I was COMPELLED to write this. I would never recommend this to anyone and can name you ten different better, affordable, FLAVORFUL steakhouses.

I went to this unique steakhouse with a large group of others months ago where we shared a lot of dishes as per usual. The staff was friendly but still very professional as expected for a steakhouse. We spent a lot but we left quite stuffed with a couple dishes definitely being the highlights and other dishes being probably not worth it but the portion sizes of just about everything was quite decent so even the dishes that maybe weren't as flavored well would still be worth it for a group. The lighting was mostly candlelight and I think the spot would work well for a date spot. They show you a platter with all the daily cuts which is a fun touch. They have fun names for their cocktails which are all $21. I went with the You Have Chosen Wisely with barrel-aged Woodinville rye, Method vermouth, and January amaro which is apparently known as an Embarcadero which is a variant of a Boulevardier. As per the ingredients, it is of course spirit forward with a mix of bitterness and sweetness and I found it very tasty.

Most of the appetizers are shareable and in the mid $20s and most of them are pretty rich. My favorite of the group and possibly my favorite dish of the night which was the Kung Pao Duck Wings with toasted peanuts, cilantro, and yuzu ranch dressing for $26. The wings had plenty of meat and there was a bit of sweetness and spiciness to them. The peanuts added some crunch and maybe my only complaint was that there wasn't enough yuzu but the ranch still went well with them.

The remaining appetizers were good but a level below the wings. The BMC Meatballs with creamy polenta, tomato pan gravy, and Parmigiano-Reggiano for $24 was the second best of the appetizers. This had two very large tender meatballs over said very rich polenta. I felt the polenta texture was a bit softer than I would expect. The Grilled Nueske's Bacon with cracked pepper, pickled red pearl onion, and moscatel vinegar for $26 was also tasty. The onion helped reduce the richness and the bacon had a touch of sweetness and it was quite rich of course.

For main dishes, we of course had one of the steaks as one of our dishes. The 14 Oz Prime New York Strip with roasted shallots for $69 was a tender tasty piece of steak cut up into several slices. It was cooked properly medium rare and the texture was solid. I guess the only complaint I would make is that I think the shallots should be on the side and there should be more of them but overall it was still good.

Our only other main dish was the Duck Lasagna with Caciocavallo and Parmigiana-Reggiano for $68. The price is that high as this is listed as a dish for 4 to 6 people and that is quite accurate. This was the richest dish of the night among every rich dish. The duck was shredded and I wish the pasta had a bit more texture as I prefer lasagna to have a bit of a crisp in some parts. The flavors were of course rich and tasty though it can become quite overwhelming and I would only really recommend this for a large group. It was tasty but a bit of a one note.

We got two side dishes. The Crispy Brussels Sprouts & Saba for $16 was our easy favorite. They had a bit of sourness and sweetness to them and I presume they were roasted with balsamic or something. If you're looking for a little bit of a less rich side dish to go with your steak or other main course, I would recommend this heavily. The Hash Brown with sour cream & roasted onions for $16 was just okay. For a hash brown, it lacked the crispy textures I associate with them and it was a bit oily for my liking. The roasted onion was a nice touch but I wouldn't really recommend it much.

Because we were gluttons, a couple of us split the BMC Cast Iron Chocolate Chip Cookie with vanilla gelato and caramel for $14. As per every other dish, the portion size was quite large. The cookie had a good crisp and the gelato was nice. It became perhaps a little bit too overly sweet with the caramel mixed with the chocolate but if it's shared, it's quite manageable and I thought it was pretty tasty. I think two others maybe split a slice of one of their cakes but I don't exactly remember. 

What I like about this restaurant is that it's not really pulling any punches. They're a modern steakhouse and most of the dishes look like they'll be rich from their description and they definitely are. The prices are a tad higher than most other steakhouses but the portions are larger and there's a couple nuances here compared to most other places. There are definitely better places if you're looking just for a fancy steak especially at these price points but if you want a steakhouse with a little bit more oomph, it's hard to go wrong here. Low 4

I am visiting from Las Vegas, and let me say, I've seen great customer service in my life, with Vegas being the best hospitality scene in the world and all, but nothing compares to the service I received here. Our service was the best we've experienced our entire time in New York. We had filets with an array of sides, and everything was just perfect. I completely recommend this spot if you're looking for a good steak house that's not overrated or filled with wannabe instagram models. 10/10. If I could give 6 stars I would.

The restaurant exceeded any/all expectations. They have managed to take the concept of a 'steakhouse' and moved it up to a level that I have not experienced in any other steakhouse across the country. This was 'fine dining' at the highest level, featuring steaks. The decor and ambience were exquisite, the staff as professional and expert as they come, and the food was beyond your imagination. In a city like New York, with a multitude of good steakhouses, this was by far the best I have ever been to. Hats off to GM Watchara "Bon" Thaunthong and his staff. I will be back!!!
Definitely pricy, but the food, drinks, service and ambiance were perfect.  We sat in a round booth in a corner, which made it feel more private.

This is such a fantastic place. Steaks done right and perfect. Excellent sides. It's really nice inside and the staff were phenomenal. Our server was "Richard", inside joke, and she was amazing. The only negative from tonight, and I'm reaching, is that the tables are too close to each other. You are elbows length away from the table next to you to the point when someone gets up to go to the bathroom their body will absolutely hit your table and/or your food. Would happily come back here.
Took my mother here for her birthday and we had an exceptional experience. Food was delicious and Paul took excellent care of us.

Experience was fantastic from start to finish. The hostess bartenders, wait staff were super friendly and attentative. The food was amazing. The Hamachi credo and kung pao duck wings were delicious and the steaks were cooked perfectly and flavorful. Mac and cheese, spinach and fries were great sides. Really...top notch as always from start to finish.  Ambiance was also great...definitely hopping on a Saturday night.
Fantastic restaurant with amazing service. Highly recommend if you're looking for a great steak.

Enjoyed dining here! Ordered the prime bone-in rib steak that comes with shishito peppers. The sides were great too (highly recommend the hash brown). The restaurant was dimly lit and intimate but can get loud. Service was great though.

Are you kidding me?  The A3 Wagyu strip flown in from Japan was out of this world.   You see a lot of A5 Wagyu in NYC but to be honest it's too fatty for my taste.  I can't have more than a piece or two.  A3 Wagyu is perfect for steak.  Plenty of fat and flavor but not too overbearing.  If the fattiness gets to be too much do a light dip into ponzu to cut the fat.  

Tomahawk was no slouch either.  Rich, flavorful and was trimmed expertly so you didn't just have hunks of fat which can sometimes happen.  I also like the presentation where they slice the meat and put it on top which made it easy to serve.  

Wait staff was efficient and friendly making good recommendations.  The chef came out and greeted us which was also a nice touch.  

Inside is modern and the room is quiet so I can actually have a conversation.   

All in all this place is definitely going into my rotation of steakhouses in NYC.
A high quality steak house located in East Village.  Food is good.  Service is good. Environment is nice too.  A nice place for a good piece of steak
Our dining experience was amazing. The American Wagyu strip steak was so delicious. The service was outstanding.
Possible the best meal I've had I. Three years. Amazing steak, wine and desert. Wow o ! .
Jonah took great care of us. We ordered a bunch of oysters, the octopus appetizer and some good old lamb chops and french fries... it was divine.

Absolutely cannot recommend this place more than I have in the past 24 hours. I have a bunch of severe allergies and they exceeded my expectations of how a restaurant should handle them. Delicious food and drinks. Amazing service and great ambiance all around. Definitely recommend this restaurant.

Bowery meat company is a great dinner spot and a great burger spot. We went to get some burgers, fries and a few apps and the burgers were worth it. Usually the burgers are only serves around the bar area and not in the main restaurant however the waiter was wonderful enough to talk to the manager since we were all getting the burger in the main area. And it was worth it. Very juicy patty and enough sauce to have your hand dripping. The bacon and wings were also ready good and the fries were very crispy. Will definitely be back!

For being a restaurant in NYC, I really wanted better vegetarian options since I was coming for a family member's birthday. We were sat 30 minutes after our reservation because the party before us was running behind, but the bar area was nice to hang around for a drink. I ordered a St. Germain Spritz, which was very good. 

I ordered the ricotta with toasted bread to start - which was incredible! Everyone at the table had great things to say about this appetizer, which came with pomegranate seeds, herbs, and honey. The toasted bread was smokey, too. I would definitely order this dish again. 

The reason for my rating is because of the vegetarian dish, which was  mozzarella ravioli floating in a cream sauce with truffle on top. The dairy was  completely overdone on this dish. The portion was good - decent for two meals - but I couldn't eat more than 4 raviolis before feeling like I would regret it later. The cream sauce was way too much, more like soup. It would have been better if it was maybe a spinach ravioli, or any other kind of ravioli, with the cream sauce in half the amount. Everyone else seemed to enjoy their dishes, but I was disappointed with the vegetarian offering.

Went here this past weekend. Great place with a lovely, cozy, ambiance. I had the West coast oysters with the charred octopus for a starter and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Octopus was very tender and the oysters were perfect. We had smooth red wine and a champagne (Bordeaux and a Salmon Brut Champagne). For dinner we had the branzino which was excellent, and the A5 Wagyu steak to top it off. An amazing cut of steak to top off a wonderful night. Highly recommend!

The lobster Mac and cheese is a must order! I would recommend family style for it, but it's so good you won't want to share.

Portions are hearty, so if you're in between options share with a friend! 

Pro tip! Ask your server about the different cuts of meat, and they will bring out all options and explain each one.

This is a restaurant that has perfected it's craft in superb service, outstanding meal presentation, ambiance  and  mastering cooking quality steaks and other dishes. It is pricey, but worth every last penny for an optimum and personalized dining experience.
We were very easily able to make last minute reservations for 6:45pm on a Saturday night. We lucked out but do encourage planning well in advance. 
We were warmly greeted and immediately seated even though we arrived a few moments early.
Drink orders were taken and immediately brought to table while we perused the menu. 
Our server arrived with a board of meats, describing each cut and it's price. This visual really is a game changer to really get to know what it is you are ordering. 
For appetizers we got the jumbo shrimp cocktail and the house ricotta. Both were amazing.
For entrees the dry aged Porterhouse (med rare), and the the 7 oz Grass fed Argentinian filet mignon (med rare)  with chimmichuri, and hash brown and creamed spinach for the sides.
Every single thing we ate was supreme quality, beautifully executed and absolutely beyond delicious.
The chef himself came out to our table for our feedback. Excellent. 
The carrot cake for dessert also blew us away. 
Water glasses were never empty, drink refills came in a flash, and new linen napkins were given without even an ask. 
The ambiance is upscale yet inviting and casual with a certain decorum. No distracting t.v.s. 
The attention to detail was impressive and all of our needs  were  genuinely taken care of. 
We lost track of time and all other concerns outside the enjoyment of the meals and one another's company. 
This establishment is just as good as some of the most highly rated steakhouses in NYC. We would highly recommend and plan to return for another fantastic meal and experience.

We were charged $320 for this steak as medium rare American wagyu. We absolutely ordered the American wagyu but were told it was $220 and the real deal Japanese was $350. Nobody on earth would think this is a $320 steak, and no one would order this if Japanese A3 Wagyu was $30 more. Also it was over cooked like literally everything we ordered. We also ordered a chateaubriand and tomahawk as well . Our server was a total gentleman and made our night , while he got us a free dessert we all would have preferred a multi hundred dollar entree prepared to our liking. His manager ridiculed us for scoffing at this $320 steak. No one , not even the manager , offered to refire us a new steak.  The manager in fact told us this was the best steak in New York. All of our meat was over cooked. It was super nice to be reminded of my grandmother and her pot roast .Exceptional wait staff , crappy management.

Pretty chill yet upscale ambiance. We sat at the bar for dessert on a Monday night. Very friendly staff. The chocolate cake was very cold and kind hard like as if it was in the freezer a little too long. The flavor was still good tho a dark chocolate with some rich undertones. The carrot cake was really good. Tbh maybe better than Floyd's. The frosting was really sweet and little bit too much frosting to cake ratio but it was delicious nonetheless
I don't understand what the hype is about this place. Yes they have quality ingredients but it's very boring!  Decent service but not fun or interesting just very basic.

Warning: If you order the 28oz American Wagyu New York Strip, you may never be able to eat any other steak ever again. It's that great. Truly. 

Bowery Meat Company continues to set the gold standard for steak in the City of New York. Wonderful service. Lovely dining room. Great menu. Certainly a great spot for a special occasion... or any reason for a great, great steak.

Amazing experience. Came here with four  friends for a guys night out.  Ordered the Filet, medium rare and was perfectly done.  We shared a bunch of sides - Mac and Cheese, creamed spinach and brussel sprouts - all excellent. 

We split the bread pudding amongst us and again, it delivered.

The atmosphere is very sophisticated and lots of care was given to us all around.  I would come back again.

Was in search for a last minute steakhouse for dinner during the holiday season. A lot of the famous joints were booked out but Bowery had slots so decided to check it out. 

1. Hamachi crudo was pretty good. Nothing to write home about 
2. Ricotta was pretty bomb. Great starter for the table 
3. Oysters were good 
4. Steak was pretty damn good. Tender and flavorful. Perfectly cooked. 
5. Mushrooms were yum
6. Sautéed spinach was also good. Standard 

Overall, Bowery's a pretty good steakhouse. Ambience is great and service was good. Pretty standard offerings but good nonetheless

Being a self proclaimed beef expert, I can say BMC is probably top (3) in the U.S. for steak.  I know, I know, bold statement, but true.  The cut are tender, and clean, meaning no excess butter etc.  The drinks at the bar are top notch, and you have to try the duck lasagna as an app.  Fantastic place.

If you are looking for a nice steak dinner, definitely go here!!! Our hotel concierge recommended it and it did not disappoint!

The restaurant has great vibes with low lighting. We sat in a booth and it was so comfy and spacious. 

The waiters come around with meat to show you your steak options and they are very knowledgeable on the menu. There are a ton of different options- not just steak, and there is something for everyone. I got the salmon with asparagus and it was great, especially the sauce it came with!

The greatest part for me was the service. I mentioned I was pregnant, and the server was so attentive on the things I may and may not be able to order. He made sure we were always taken care of. There were also other servers whose job was to fill your water and make sure the table was clean. My water was never less than halfway empty- for someone who drinks a ton of water at restaurants. This was amazing!

Would definitely go back- great place for friends and great place for date night.
